| `font.heading.xxsmall` | 11/14 | Eyebrows, group headings, menu section labels (the component adds the uppercase). |
| `font.heading.large`   | 28/34 | A stat value, a dashboard number. Not a page title.                               |
| `font.code`            | 12/18 | Code blocks only.                                                                 |

Prose never grows past `dimension.layout.measure`, 720px (`max-w-layout-measure`).

## Sizes

| Token                      | Value | For                                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dimension.control.xsmall` | 24px  | Button `xsmall`.                                                    |
| `dimension.control.small`  | 28px  | Button `small`, chips, menu items, side nav items, a Toolbar's row. |
| `dimension.control.medium` | 32px  | The default: Button `medium`, inputs, selects, combobox triggers.   |
| `dimension.control.large`  | 36px  | Hero forms only.                                                    |
| `dimension.row`            | 40px  | A table row; `.compact` 36px; `.header` 32px; `.menu` 28px.         |
| `dimension.icon.small`     | 14px  | An icon inside a small or medium control.                           |
| `dimension.icon.medium`    | 16px  | A standalone icon, an icon button's glyph.                          |
| `dimension.layout.rail`    | 272px | The rail beside a record: Inspector, Aside.                         |
| `dimension.layout.panel`   | 320px | The preview panel before the reader resizes it.                     |
| `dimension.layout.sidenav` | 228px | The side nav, expanded.                                             |
| `dimension.layout.topnav`  | 48px  | The top nav, and the banner above it.                               |

## Radius

`radius.xsmall` 2px, `small` 3px, `medium` 5px, `large` 7px, `xlarge` 9px, `xxlarge` 12px and `full`, as `rounded-xsmall` to `rounded-full`. The bigger the surface, the larger the radius: a control is medium, a card large. Which part takes which is one table, on the [Shape](?path=/docs/tokens-shape--docs) sheet; a part you build takes the radius of the part it sits beside.

## Motion

| Token                                       | Value | For                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `motion.duration.micro`                     | 70ms  | A toggle's thumb, a checkbox's tick, a chevron turning.                    |
| `motion.duration.fast`                      | 110ms | Hover and press colour, a tooltip's fade, a menu leaving.                  |
| `motion.duration.medium`                    | 150ms | A menu arriving, a section expanding, a dialog leaving.                    |
| `motion.duration.moderate`                  | 240ms | A dialog or sheet arriving, the panel sliding in, a toast, content rising. |
| `motion.duration.slow`                      | 400ms | Chart marks arriving, a drill-down redrawing.                              |
| `motion.duration.slower`                    | 700ms | The blanket dimming the page.                                              |
| `motion.easing.standard`, `.enter`, `.exit` |       | `ease-standard`, `ease-enter`, `ease-exit`. Honour reduced motion.         |

## What has no token on purpose

Structural utilities carry no design value and are allowed as written: `flex`, `grid`, `relative`, `absolute`, `sticky`, `truncate`, `whitespace-nowrap`, `sr-only`, `overflow-auto`, `pointer-events-none` and their kin. Everything with a colour, a length, a weight or a duration goes through a token. A value you cannot find here or on the sheets is a token to propose, not a number to type.

<!-- page: Guidance/Agents (src/stories/docs/Agents.mdx) -->

# Working with Ledger as an agent

This Storybook is the contract. A coding agent that uses Ledger reads it the same way a person does: the family page says what a part is for, the generated props say what it accepts, and the stories show every state the part supports. Nothing about a part is true because another design system does it that way.

## Where the instructions are

| Question                                   | Read                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Which part answers this need?              | Guidance/Choosing a part, then the family's page.                                                                                                                       |
| What is a part for, and what does it take? | The family's page here: Components, Patterns, Layout, Primitives. Its `ArgTypes` table is generated from the source.                                                    |
| I know shadcn or Radix; what is different? | Guidance/Coming from shadcn.                                                                                                                                            |
| How do the parts compose into a screen?    | Guidance/Recipes, and the Layout/Pages stories.                                                                                                                         |
| Which value or class do I use?             | Guidance/Which token for the short answer by job; the Tokens sheets and the Grammar page for everything. Tokens are the only styling.                                   |
| How do I install it and set up the root?   | Getting started: the stylesheet order and the providers (ModeProvider, LedgerProvider, Toaster). Components/Locale for the reader's locale and zone.                    |
| What does the lint reject?                 | The Lint rules page.                                                                                                                                                    |
| How do I add or change a part?             | The package `AGENTS.md`, which points at the "Adding to the kit" checklist in the component library guide; Guidance/Writing stories for the story and page conventions. |
| Which part does the application use here?  | Not this Storybook. The application's composition contract, `docs/guides/product-patterns.md`, decides that; app compositions stay out of these stories.                |

## Through the MCP server

The Storybook serves an MCP endpoint at `/mcp` while it runs (`npm run storybook`, port 6007). The repository's `.mcp.json` registers it as `storybook-mcp`. Use its tools in this order:

1. `get-storybook-story-instructions` before writing or editing a story. Its output is the source of truth for imports, story shape and test conventions.
2. `docs-list` once, then `docs-show` for a family before using any of its props. A prop exists when the family's page or its props table shows it, or the package's `.d.ts` declares it (a Base UI part's inherited props, such as a Dialog's `onOpenChange`, are declared there). A prop none of them shows does not exist; report the gap rather than guessing.
3. `stories-preview` after any change that alters how something looks: a component, a story, a stylesheet or a token. A shared file with no story of its own is previewed through its consumers' stories. Report the returned URLs.
4. `test-run` to run the affected stories, focused while iterating and broad before handoff. Fix failures before reporting completion.

## Without the MCP server

`packages/design-system/llms.txt` is this Storybook's pages, the token sheet and the public export list, generated into one file by `npm run build:llms`. It is committed and the package tests fail when it drifts, so a cold checkout and an agent without MCP access read the same contract. It never replaces the running Storybook for verifying a change.

## What an agent gets wrong most often

- Using a prop from shadcn, Radix or Base UI that Ledger's part does not expose. Look it up first.
- Writing a class the lint will reject: an arbitrary value, a Tailwind colour, a margin, a `dark:` variant. Use a token utility or a primitive prop.
- Copying a kit part into product code instead of importing it. `ledger/no-kit-shadow` names the part to import.
- Importing a story helper. `Matrix`, `Specimens` and `Pair` lay out the stories and are not package exports, even where a snippet's import line lists them; lay out with Stack, Inline and Grid.
- Formatting a date with `toLocaleString` or the host's zone. Dates go through DateTime, `c.date` or `useLedgerLocale()`, in the LedgerProvider's zone.
- Editing `src/generated/` by hand. Change `tokens/` and rebuild.
- Putting an application composition into a package story. The package documents neutral contracts; the application is verified in the running app.
- Rendering both colour modes in one story. The toolbar switches the mode; a story renders once.

<!-- page: Guidance/Coming from shadcn (src/stories/docs/FromShadcn.mdx) -->

# Coming from shadcn, Radix and Base UI

Ledger's families are built from shadcn's Base UI compositions, so most names are the ones you know. The APIs are not identical, and the differences are exactly where an agent invents a prop. Read this page once, then look every prop up on the family's page before using it.

## The three differences that matter most

**`render`, not `asChild`.** Ledger is on Base UI, not Radix. A part composes another element through `render={<a href="…" />}` (or a function). `asChild` does not exist anywhere in the package.

**Tokens, not the shadcn theme.** There is no `bg-background`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-input` from shadcn's CSS variables, and no `dark:` variant. Every colour, space, radius and type value is a Ledger token utility (`bg-surface`, `text-subtle`, `border-default`, `p-200`, `font-body-small`) or a primitive prop. The lint rejects the rest; the Which token page lists what to reach for.

**`cn` from the package.** Import it from `@ledger/design-system/cn`. There is no `lib/utils`.

## Name by name

| You know                                                                          | In Ledger                                                                                                                                         | What differs                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Button                                                                            | **Button**, **IconButton**, **LinkButton**, **LinkIconButton**                                                                                    | A focus-preserving `isLoading` state and `disabledReason`. IconButton needs a `label` and draws its own Tooltip. Navigation is a LinkButton or LinkIconButton: a real link, the router's Link through `render`. |
| Badge                                                                             | **Badge**                                                                                                                                         | Six variants plus semantic `tone`s and two sizes. A status is one Badge per row; severity is **Indicator**, a number is **Count**.                                                                              |
| Label, Field                                                                      | **Field** and its parts: **FieldLabel**, **FieldDescription**, **FieldError**; **FieldSet** and **FieldLegend** for a group                       | No standalone Label. Field is Base UI's Field.Root: it binds the control inside it and takes `invalid`, `required` and `disabled`. **ErrorSummary** lists a failed submission's errors.                         |
| Form (react-hook-form)                                                            | The **Forms** pattern                                                                                                                             | No Form component. TanStack Form owns state and validation; Field, the controls and the primitives are the presentation.                                                                                        |
| Input                                                                             | **Input**; **SearchField** for a query; **NumberField** for a quantity                                                                            | Input wraps Base UI's Input. Labels and errors belong to Field. A search box is SearchField and a stepped number NumberField, not `type="search"` or `type="number"`.                                           |
| Input Group                                                                       | **InputGroup** and its parts                                                                                                                      | Flat shadcn Base UI composition; addons, text, buttons and a textarea variant.                                                                                                                                  |
| Textarea                                                                          | **Textarea**                                                                                                                                      | A native textarea on Base UI's Field.Control, so a Field binds it as it does Input.                                                                                                                             |
| Select, Native Select                                                             | **Select**                                                                                                                                        | Native Select is removed. Select does not filter; a list that needs typing is **Combobox**.                                                                                                                     |
| Combobox, Command as a picker                                                     | **Combobox**; **RecordPicker** for records                                                                                                        | Combobox is flat Base UI composition with chips. A picker of records with ids and statuses is the RecordPicker pattern.                                                                                         |
| Command (cmdk)                                                                    | **Command** parts, **CommandPalette**                                                                                                             | The palette takes plain command objects and stays presentational.                                                                                                                                               |
| Checkbox, Radio Group, Switch                                                     | Same names; **CheckboxGroup** for several                                                                                                         | Base UI underneath; `render` for composition. CheckboxGroup names the group with a FieldLegend and takes **CheckboxGroupSelectAll**.                                                                            |
| Toggle, Toggle Group                                                              | Same names                                                                                                                                        | Icon-only toggles need `aria-label`.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Calendar, Date Picker, date and time inputs                                       | **Calendar**, **DatePicker**, **DateRangePicker**, **TimeField**, **DateTimeField**; **DateTime**, **RelativeTime** and **DateLabel** to show one | react-day-picker underneath. DatePicker holds and reports an ISO day, DateRangePicker `{ start, end }` and TimeField an ISO time; DateTimeField a moment in the LedgerProvider's zone.                          |
| Dialog, Alert Dialog, Sheet, Drawer, Popover, Tooltip, Hover Card, Dropdown Menu  | Same names                                                                                                                                        | All Base UI. The Overlays page says which surface fits which task; Drawer is the gesture bottom sheet, Sheet the side panel.                                                                                    |
| Sonner, Toast                                                                     | **Toaster** and the Toast parts                                                                                                                   | Base UI Toast with a native manager API. Mount once near the root.                                                                                                                                              |
| Alert                                                                             | **Alert** with **AlertAction**                                                                                                                    | Explicit title, description and action parts.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Tabs                                                                              | **Tabs**, `TabsList variant="line"`                                                                                                               | The line variant fills its container with one border and scrolls in one row; do not add wrapping or width classes.                                                                                              |
| Accordion, Collapsible                                                            | Same names                                                                                                                                        | Base UI.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Table                                                                             | **Table** for markup; **DataTable** for state                                                                                                     | DataTable is a TanStack Table 9 instance with columns declared by kind (`defineColumns`), a Toolbar, `fill` and `responsive`.                                                                                   |
| Data Table (shadcn recipe)                                                        | **DataTable**                                                                                                                                     | It is a pattern with a hook, not a page recipe you copy.                                                                                                                                                        |
| Sidebar                                                                           | **Shell** and its areas                                                                                                                           | The whole application frame: Banner, TopNav, SideNav with an icon rail, Main, Aside, Panel. Not a standalone sidebar.                                                                                           |
| Breadcrumb                                                                        | **Breadcrumb**                                                                                                                                    | `BreadcrumbLink` takes a router link through `render`.                                                                                                                                                          |
| Card                                                                              | **Card**                                                                                                                                          | Same parts, token surfaces.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Avatar                                                                            | **Avatar**, **AvatarGroup**, **AvatarBadge**                                                                                                      | Flat shadcn Base UI composition with Ledger sizes and accents.                                                                                                                                                  |
| Skeleton, Spinner, Progress                                                       | Same names, plus **PageSkeleton** and **ProgressStacked**                                                                                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Empty, Item, Kbd, Button Group                                                    | Same names                                                                                                                                        | Same part structure. DataTable draws its own Empty.                                                                                                                                                             |
| Chart                                                                             | **Chart** and its kinds                                                                                                                           | Recharts underneath as in shadcn; Ledger adds the Frame, the table twin, drill-down, export and the chart tokens.                                                                                               |
| Resizable, Scroll Area, Separator, Pagination                                     | Same names                                                                                                                                        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Typography (`<h1 className=…>`)                                                   | **Heading**, **Text**, **Eyebrow**, **Prose**                                                                                                     | Type is a composite token on a primitive, never a class list.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Navigation Menu, Menubar, Context Menu, Carousel, Aspect Ratio, Slider, Input OTP | Not in Ledger                                                                                                                                     | A need for one is flagged in writing before it is built.                                                                                                                                                        |

## Parts Ledger has that shadcn does not

These carry the product's vocabulary and have no shadcn analogue, so nothing you know applies: **Id**, **Count**, **Indicator** and **Dot**, **Fact**, **KeyValue** and **Inspector**, **Stat**, **Absent**, **Eyebrow**, **Prose**, **List**, **Truncate**, **VisuallyHidden**, **Icon**, **Person**, **Attachment**, **FileTrigger**, **DropZone**, **CopyButton**, **Diff**, **KbdShortcut**, **CodeBlock**, **Timeline**, **Stepper**, **Gates**, **Glance**, **Related**, **TaskRow**, **Composer**, **Editable**, **FilterChip**, **Toolbar**, **Scroller**, **PickerSheet**, **RecordBrowser**, **SearchDialog**, **PreviewSheet**, **PreviewNavigation**, **PageHeader**, **Section**, **CollapsibleHeader**, **HeadingLevelProvider**, **Tree**, **Banner**, **Announcer** and **LedgerProvider**. Read their pages; the Choosing a part page says when each one is the answer.

<!-- page: Guidance/Token grammar (src/stories/docs/Grammar.mdx) -->

# Token grammar

Tokens are named on one grammar: **property . role . emphasis . state**.

| Segment  | Examples                                                                                                       | What it says                                                                                                           |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| property | `color.background`, `color.text`, `color.icon`, `color.border`, `elevation.surface`, `space`, `font`, `radius` | What is being painted. Text, icon, border and background are separate properties because they need different contrast. |
| role     | `brand`, `neutral`, `selected`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `information`, `disabled`, `input`, `inverse`  | Why. A role names the meaning, not the colour.                                                                         |
| emphasis | `subtlest`, `subtler`, `subtle`, (default), `bold`, `bolder`, `boldest`                                        | How loud. Default sits in the middle; bold is a solid fill with inverse text.                                          |
| state    | `hovered`, `pressed`, `selected`, `focused`                                                                    | Interaction. A state is always its own token, never alpha on the default.                                              |

Every token has one CSS variable, `--ds-<name with dashes>`, and most have one Tailwind utility.

| Token                                 | CSS                                        | Utility                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `color.background.brand.bold.hovered` | `--ds-color-background-brand-bold-hovered` | `bg-brand-bold-hovered`                   |
| `color.text.subtle`                   | `--ds-color-text-subtle`                   | `text-subtle`                             |
| `color.icon.danger`                   | `--ds-color-icon-danger`                   | `icon-danger`                             |
| `color.border.focused`                | `--ds-color-border-focused`                | `border-focused`                          |
| `elevation.surface.raised`            | `--ds-elevation-surface-raised`            | `bg-surface-raised`                       |
| `elevation.shadow.overlay`            | `--ds-elevation-shadow-overlay`            | `shadow-overlay`                          |
| `space.200`                           | `--ds-space-200`                           | `p-200`, `gap-200`, `h-200` …             |
| `radius.medium`                       | `--ds-radius-medium`                       | `rounded-medium`                          |
| `font.body.small`                     | `--ds-font-body-small`                     | `font-body-small`                         |
| `dimension.control.medium`            | `--ds-dimension-control-medium`            | `h-control-medium`, `size-control-medium` |
| `motion.duration.fast`                | `--ds-motion-duration-fast`                | `duration-fast`                           |

## Tiers

1. **Palette.** Six ramps (neutral, dark neutral, blue, green, orange, red) with numbered step names, plus alpha steps for translucent fills. Never used directly.
2. **Semantic.** Colour and elevation tokens that reference the ramps. Each has a light value and a dark value. This is the only tier a component reads for colour.
3. **Typography, space, shape, dimension, motion.** Mode independent.
4. **Component.** Where a component needs a value no semantic token gives it, the value is added to the tokens, not written in the component.

## Where a value comes from

- **Surface.** `elevation.surface` is the page; `raised` is a card; `overlay` is a menu or dialog; `sunken` is a well. Box sets `utility.elevation.surface.current` when it paints a surface, so children can read the surface they sit on.
- **Text.** `default` for content, `subtle` for secondary, `subtlest` for hints and captions, `disabled` for off. Status text (`success`, `warning`, `danger`, `information`) sits on the matching status background.
- **Border.** `default` for hairlines, `bold` for emphasis, `input` for fields, `focused` and `selected` for those states.
- **Type.** Composite tokens: `body` (13/18) for interface text, `body.small` (12/16) for captions, `body.xsmall` (11/14) for micro labels, `body.large` (15/22) for reading; three heading sizes; `code`.
- **Space.** 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80. A name counts hundredths of an 8px step: `space.100` is 8px, `space.025` is 2px, `space.1000` is 80px.
- **Radius.** `xsmall` 2, `small` 3, `medium` 5, `large` 7, `xlarge` 9, `xxlarge` 12, `full`. Which part takes which is the [Shape](?path=/docs/tokens-shape--docs) sheet's table.
- **Metrics.** Controls are 24, 28, 32, 36 tall; a table row is 40, with `compact` 36, `header` 32 and `menu` 28; icons 14 and 16.

<!-- page: Guidance/Lint rules (src/stories/docs/Lint.mdx) -->

# Lint rules

The package exports an ESLint plugin, `@ledger/design-system/eslint`, whose allowlist is generated by the token build, so the rules and the tokens cannot drift. It has two presets: `package`, what this package lints itself with, and `recommended`, for a product. This is the one table of the rules; the repository's component library guide links here.

| Rule                       | Reports                                                                                                              | Instead                                                                                                            | `package` | `recommended` |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------- | ------------- |
| `no-arbitrary-value`       | `text-[13px]`, `w-[240px]`, `bg-[#eee]`                                                                              | A token utility or a primitive prop.                                                                               | error¹    | error         |
| `no-alpha-token`           | `bg-brand-bold/80`, `text-default/60`                                                                                | The hovered, pressed, subtle or disabled token.                                                                    | error     | error         |
| `no-dark-variant`          | `dark:bg-neutral`                                                                                                    | Nothing. Every colour token flips by itself; a `dark:` class means a token is missing.                             | error     | error         |
| `no-margin`                | `mt-200`, `-mx-100`                                                                                                  | Stack or Inline space, or Bleed. `m-auto` is allowed.                                                              | error²    | error         |
| `no-static-design-value`   | `rounded`, `opacity-50`, `duration-200`, `border-2`, `ring-2`, `bg-white`, `text-transparent`                        | `rounded-small…full`, `opacity-disabled`, `duration-fast`, `border-w-selected`, `outline-focused`, a colour token. | error     | error         |
| `no-non-token-class`       | Any class that is not a token utility or a documented structural utility (`flex`, `truncate`, `sticky`, `sr-only` …) | A token utility.                                                                                                   | error¹    | error         |
| `no-deprecated-token`      | A deprecated token's utility                                                                                         | Its replacement, applied by `--fix`.                                                                               | error     | error         |
| `no-deprecated-name`       | A part's old name (`Shell.Sidebar`, `Shell.NavItem`)                                                                 | Its replacement; `--fix` does the one-to-one renames.                                                              | error     | error         |
| `prefer-text-link`         | A `Link`, `NavLink` or `a` carrying `text-brand` or `hover:underline`                                                | TextLink with the link element through `render`.                                                                   | error     | error         |
| `no-colgroup`              | `<colgroup>`                                                                                                         | `width` or `minWidth` on each Table.Header.                                                                        | error     | error         |
| `button-icon-slot`         | An element with `size-icon-*` inside a Button or an IconButton                                                       | `iconBefore`, `iconAfter` or `icon`, passed bare; the button sizes it.                                             | error     | error         |
| `cell-plain`               | A Table.Cell carrying a neutral colour, weight or type token                                                         | Nothing; only a status colour may differ.                                                                          | off       | error         |
| `id-not-blue`              | An Id with `text-brand` outside a link or a button                                                                   | Wrap it in a link, or drop the class.                                                                              | off       | error         |
| `no-kit-shadow`            | A local component named like a kit part (`Badge`, `Table`, `Stack`)                                                  | Import the kit part.                                                                                               | off       | error         |
| `no-native-confirm`        | `confirm()` or `window.confirm()`                                                                                    | An AlertDialog, which keeps cancellation, the draft and the pending lock.                                          | off       | error         |
| `text-link-navigation`     | A TextLink whose `render` is a Button, an IconButton or a native element other than `a`                              | An anchor or a router link in TextLink; a Button for an action.                                                    | off       | error         |
| `dialog-footer-order`      | Cancel after the primary in a DialogFooter                                                                           | Cancel first, then the primary.                                                                                    | off       | error         |
| `use-primitives`           | A `div` or `span` carrying `flex`, `grid`, padding or gap classes                                                    | Box, Stack, Inline, Flex or Grid.                                                                                  | off       | warn          |
| `product-responsive-table` | A DataTable without `responsive`, or with it before a prop spread                                                    | `responsive` after any spread.                                                                                     | off       | off³          |
| `product-line-tabs`        | A TabsList without `variant="line"`, or with a wrapping, width or overflow class                                     | `variant="line"` after any spread, and no layout override: the kit owns the strip.                                 | off       | off³          |

1. In the package's stories, `no-arbitrary-value` is off and `no-non-token-class` is a warning: a story's own frame may take a fixed width, while the parts it demonstrates stay on the tokens.
2. Off in `primitives/bleed.tsx`, the one place a negative margin is written.
3. Opt-in product layout rules, off in both presets: filled tabs and horizontally scrolling comparison tables remain supported by the kit. A product that adopts the contract turns them on for its product files; this repository's application does. Each required prop must follow any spread so the spread cannot override it.

Inside the package a portability rule also blocks any import from a consumer (`@/…`), from the prototype, or from a router.

## What counts as structural

Display, position, alignment, overflow, text flow and interaction utilities are allowed as written, because they carry no design value: `flex`, `grid`, `relative`, `absolute`, `sticky`, `truncate`, `whitespace-nowrap`, `select-none`, `pointer-events-none`, `overflow-auto`, `overscroll-none`, `sr-only`, `cursor-pointer`, `transition-colors`, `animate-spin` and their kin. Sizes with a token key are allowed on every sizing property: `w-200`, `min-h-800`, `size-150`. The kit's own structural utilities are allowed as well: the layout rules in `layout.css` and `shell.css` (`page-header`, `section-header`, `fill-window`, `sticky-rail` and the shell regions), `stat-grid` with `stat-grid-2` to `stat-grid-6` in `stat.css`, and the hit areas `touch-target`, `touch-target-block` and `touch-target-block-after` in `touch.css`.

## Running it

```js
// eslint.config.js in a product
import ledger from "@ledger/design-system/eslint";

export default [
  ...ledger.configs.recommended,
  // The two opt-in layout rules, for the files that follow the product contract.
  {
    files: ["src/routes/**/*.tsx"],
    rules: {
      "ledger/product-responsive-table": "error",
      "ledger/product-line-tabs": "error",
    },
  },
];
```

```sh
# inside the package
npm run lint

# in a product, after adopting the preset
npx eslint src
```

<!-- page: Guidance/Writing stories (src/stories/docs/Stories.mdx) -->

# Writing stories

The Storybook is the package's test suite and its documentation at once: every story renders in both colour modes with its play function and an axe pass (`npm run test:a11y`) and again at a phone and in a narrow frame (`npm run test:layout`), every exported part must appear in one (`npm run ds:check`), and the family's MDX page draws its examples from the same file. The MCP tool `get-storybook-story-instructions` is the generic Storybook guidance (the package runs Storybook 10); this page is what this package adds to it.

## Shape of a stories file

```tsx
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from "@storybook/react-vite";
import { expect, fn, userEvent, within } from "storybook/test";

import { Badge, Button } from "../../components";
import { Inline, Stack } from "../../primitives";
import * as storyLayout from "../_lib/matrix";

// Story-only helpers, bound locally so the MCP snippet does not list them as package exports.
const { Matrix, Specimens } = storyLayout;

const meta = {
  title: "Components/Badge",
  component: Badge,
  parameters: { layout: "padded" },
  args: { children: "Featured", variant: "default" },
} satisfies Meta<typeof Badge>;
export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>;

/** The usage to copy, first, with the controls. */
export const Playground: Story = {};

/** The six reference variants beside the icon positions. */
export const Variants: Story = { render: () => <Matrix rows={…} cols={…} render={…} /> };
```

- Imports come from `@storybook/react-vite` and `storybook/test`, never the `@storybook/test` or `@storybook/react` names.
- Parts are imported by relative path from `../../components`, `../../primitives`, `../../patterns`, `../../layout`. The package never imports its own root.
- `title` is `<Category>/<Family>`: Primitives, Components, Layout, Patterns, Tokens, Guidance. One family, one file, one `title`.
- The JSDoc comment above a story is its description on the docs page. Write it as the sentence the reader needs, not the story's name again.
- The first story is the usage to copy: plain parts and primitives, no `_lib` helper. MCP `docs-show` returns the first three stories' code, and an agent copies them.
- `_lib` helpers (Matrix, Specimens, Pair) are story layout, not package exports. The MCP snippet lists every relative import under the package name, so a story file binds them locally (`import * as storyLayout from "../_lib/matrix"`, then `const { Matrix, Specimens } = storyLayout`); a locally declared name is left out of the snippet's import line.

## What to cover

- Every named part of the family, rendered. `ds:check` fails on an export with no story.
- Representative states, not every permutation: default, hover and pressed through the tokens, disabled, invalid, loading, empty, error, the sizes that change behaviour. The `_lib/matrix` **Matrix** and **Specimens** helpers lay a family's variants out for comparison. **Pair** in `_lib/pair` puts a Do beside a Don't with one line each on why: give a family a Don't story wherever a misuse is likely (a wrong part, a wrong word, a missing name), not as a required section.
- One playground covers the controls. Keep distinct regression cases as their own stories rather than folding them into the playground.
- A `play` function on every interactive story: drive it with `userEvent`, assert the visible outcome with role and label queries on `canvas`, and assert `fn` callbacks were called. Wait for a menu to mount before asserting `aria-expanded`.
- Render once. Josef switches the mode in the toolbar; a story never renders light and dark side by side.
- A story's frame is fluid: a wrapper takes `maxWidth`, not `width`, so it fits a phone and a panel. Inside a row that sizes its children to their content (Specimens, an Inline), give the width together with `maxWidth: "100%"`. A layout inside a story responds to its container (`@container` with `@md:`), not the window (`md:`). Set Frame to 320px container in the toolbar to see a story in a narrow container.
- A behaviour that exists only at a phone gets a story that pins `viewport` in its `globals` (`ledgerPhone` is 390px, `ledgerSmall` 340px), with a `play` that asserts it: no sideways scroll, the changed element visible, a folded item reachable. Pin only where the behaviour needs it: the layout checks measure a pinned story at the width it pins, not at theirs ([Testing and review](?path=/docs/guidance-testing-and-review--docs) says how).

  ```tsx
  export const Phone: Story = {
    globals: { viewport: { value: "ledgerPhone", isRotated: false } },
    play: async () => {
      const page = document.documentElement;
      await expect(page.scrollWidth).toBeLessThanOrEqual(page.clientWidth);
    },
  };
  ```

## What fails a story

- A console error. `test/storybook.setup.ts` fails any story that emits one.
- An axe violation in either mode. Fix semantic and structural violations directly; a contrast or spacing violation is a design decision, so raise it instead.
- Sideways scroll at a 390px phone, a word broken across two lines, or paint past a 320px frame (`npm run test:layout`). [Testing and review](?path=/docs/guidance-testing-and-review--docs) says what the check measures and when a story is exempt.
- A stale `api/public-api.json`: `npm run ds:api:check` when declarations changed, `ds:api:update` when they changed on purpose.
- Drift in `eslint-plugin/components.json` or `llms.txt`; the package build regenerates both.

## The MDX page

One `<Family>.mdx` beside the stories, attached with `<Meta of={Stories} />`, so its title is the stories file's. It opens with what the part is for in a sentence or two, then `<Canvas of={Stories.X} />` for the examples worth reading, `<ArgTypes of={Part} />` for each named part, and the usage and accessibility guidance that helps. No required heading set and no "Not applicable" filler. A larger migration gets one focused guide the page links to.

`api/axis-policy.json` holds optional notes on package-specific meanings of `variant`, `size`, `tone` and the other shared axes; a new part or prop does not need an entry.

## What does not belong here

An application composition. A screen from the product is verified in the running app, never mounted in a package story; the package documents neutral contracts and the application's pattern contract decides how they are used there.

## After changing a story

Call `stories-changed`, then `stories-preview` for the stories that matter, then `test-run` for the family. Report the URLs. Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry that names the story showing the change.

<!-- page: Guidance/Testing and review (src/stories/docs/TestingAndReview.mdx) -->

# Testing and review

The system should help a person understand the situation, choose an action, complete it, and recover if it fails. A familiar visual style alone does not establish that contract. Test the whole task with realistic content, keyboard input and the conditions people actually encounter.

## Before adding an API

Start with the user's task and the semantic HTML element. Reuse a native control when its behavior answers the task. A new prop needs a distinct consumer need and a documented default, valid combinations, ownership of state, and behavior when absent. Avoid booleans that encode several mutually exclusive modes. Prefer a union when only one mode can apply. Preserve native names for native behavior.

| Question                       | Required evidence                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Who owns the state?            | Controlled and uncontrolled behavior, defaults, reset, and async external updates.                         |
| What reaches the DOM?          | The target for `id`, `name`, `form`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, handlers, and the ref.                            |
| What can fail?                 | Pending, rejected save, retry, cancellation, and stale completion examples.                                |
| What can be composed?          | Compound slots and valid nesting; no interactive element inside another interactive element.               |
| What does a dependency expose? | Explicit adapter types for toast, table and chart APIs; all other implementation internals remain private. |

## State and content

Every collection needs loading, empty, filtered empty, error, ready, and refreshed states where applicable. A filtered empty state keeps filters visible and offers Clear filters. A save failure keeps the draft. Announce success only after the command succeeds; if persistence is local to this browser, say so. Permissions are business rules enforced by commands as well as reflected by controls.

Use sentence case, a specific verb for actions, and an error that says what the person can do next. Name the affected record when ambiguity is possible. Essential guidance belongs beside the control. Disabled actions need a visible reason; an enabled control must navigate or perform its stated action. Do not use a notification to conceal an unimplemented operation.

## Keyboard, focus and targets

Check Tab and Shift+Tab, Enter and Space, Escape, arrow keys, Home/End and typeahead where the widget requires them. Trees maintain one tab stop and expose level, expansion and selection. Closing a modal returns focus to its opener or an explicitly supplied replacement. Failed form submission focuses the first invalid control and exposes all errors. A sticky header or action bar must not fully obscure focused content.

The web minimum target requirement is **24 by 24 CSS pixels**, subject to the WCAG 2.2 spacing, equivalent, inline, user-agent and essential exceptions. Document any exception on the actual control. Native platform point guidance is not a CSS pixel requirement. Prefer larger targets for frequent touch actions. Measure both the target and the distance to neighboring targets; a small icon inside a sufficiently large button is fine.

Inspect 320 CSS pixel width, 200% text enlargement and 400% browser zoom. A dense data table may scroll in its own region; surrounding search, headings, dialogs and actions must reflow. Check focus after scrolling, opening menus, validating a long form, collapsing navigation, and removing the selected item. Reduced-motion preference should remove nonessential movement while keeping pending state understandable through text and semantics.

## Automated checks and their limits

`node scripts/ds-check.mjs` resolves public exports through the TypeScript compiler, counts executable story references, checks story coverage and documentation, and rejects a growing exception baseline. `node scripts/ds-public-api.mjs` prints the full public value/type inventory. A reference proves use, not correctness; interaction assertions establish behavior.

ActionBar and WorkPane have no stories (`RETIRED_STORY_EXPORTS` in `scripts/ds-check.mjs`), so no render, accessibility or layout check reaches them; their exports stay in the API baseline, which checks declarations. Every other family, Inspector included, has stories and a page.

Keep one family page with useful examples, generated props and relevant usage/accessibility guidance. There is no required heading set. Omit sections that add no information, and review the prose against the current examples and implementation. Keep migration guidance in one place and link to it from the changelog.

The package runs its stories through two scripts, from the repository root:

```sh
npm run test:a11y -w packages/design-system
npm run test:layout -w packages/design-system
# one file through both layout checks, from inside packages/design-system
npx vitest run --project storybook-narrow --project storybook-contained src/stories/components/Badge.stories.tsx
```

`test:a11y` runs every story in light and dark Chromium using Storybook’s built-in `test` tag. Each story gets a render check; its `play` function adds interaction assertions. Axe and unexpected-console checks run alongside them. Dark mode also checks reduced motion. A focused forced-colors project runs the existing Switch, RadioGroup, Tabs and Progress stories with system colors enabled.

`test:layout` renders every story twice more, without axe, once its web fonts have loaded: at a 390px phone (`storybook-narrow`) and in a 320px frame on the desktop canvas (`storybook-contained`, the toolbar's Frame: 320px container). A story fails when the page scrolls sideways, a word of four or more letters breaks across two lines, or anything paints past either edge of the frame outside a scroller. At phone width, visible content past the page's left edge fails too, because no one can scroll to it. A story whose overflow is its lesson (a Don't) is listed by id, with its reason, in `test/layout-allow.json`; a fixture that overflows because of a fixed width becomes fluid instead of being listed.

Two things change how a story is measured, both visible in the story. `layout: "fullscreen"` is page-level and gets no frame, so the contained check skips it; the phone check still measures it. A story's `globals` render it at the width they pin: a phone pin is measured at that width in both checks (inside the 320px frame in the contained one), a desktop pin takes it off the phone width, and `frame: "canvas"` takes it out of the frame. Pin a width only for a play function that measures a layout existing at that width. Overlays positioned against the viewport (sheets, dialogs, toasts) are not measured for paint past an edge, but an open one's words are checked at phone width; check an overlay's fit in a render at phone width.

Keep examples and their interaction tests in the same component’s `.stories.tsx` file. Add assertions to an existing example before introducing another render fixture. Use `fn()` from `storybook/test` for callbacks instead of rendering test counters or “check refs” buttons. Add a distinct story only for a distinct useful state or workflow. The Interactions panel shows the test steps; test-only controls do not belong in the component showcase.

Storybook applies `dev` and `test` automatically. No custom tag is needed to opt in. Use `!test` only for a documented case that cannot run automatically; intentional accessibility anti-examples can scope an exception to the demonstrated axe rule, with an explanation beside the story. The other accessibility checks and the render test still run. Do not recreate a separate hidden story catalog.

See [Storybook interaction tests](https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-tests/interaction-testing) and [tags](https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-stories/tags). The package unit suite covers nonvisual logic and token generation. The packed consumer suite verifies installation, declarations, SSR and generated CSS.

Axe does not certify keyboard quality, reading order, useful labels, focus visibility, zoom or screen-reader announcements. Review representative workflows with a screen reader and Firefox/WebKit before release. Contrast results cover the declared pairs, including alpha compositing and interactive states; they do not prove every possible composition. Resting text-field borders keep the intentionally lighter 1.5:1 visibility floor, and meet 3:1 at increased contrast. The Checkbox and Radio boundary (`color.border.bold`) and the Switch's off track (`color.background.input.track`) meet 3:1 against every surface in every mode; focus and danger borders meet 3:1 against their declared adjacent surfaces. Text and non-text checks keep their separate thresholds.

## Reference workflows for review

| Workflow                     | Story or product surface           | Review focus                                                             |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Validate and repair a form   | Patterns/Forms stories             | All errors, first focus, preserved values, custom control wiring.        |
| Pick and submit a date       | Components/DatePicker stories      | Closed picker FormData, external form, reset, disabled omission.         |
| Save inline with failure     | Patterns/Editable stories          | One pending operation, rollback ownership, external updates.             |
| Complete a nested modal task | Components/Dialog stories          | Escape, successful close, return to correct opener.                      |
| Navigate a hierarchy         | Components/Tree stories            | One tab stop, hierarchy, typeahead, selected item removal.               |
| Filter records and recover   | Risks, controls and findings pages | Empty results, clear filters, visible labels, durable supported actions. |
| Read a chart                 | Patterns/Chart stories             | Table equivalent, deterministic formatting and color mode.               |

## Ownership and lifecycle

The repository maintainers own the package contract and review changes to tokens, accessibility behavior and adapters. A contribution names a responsible reviewer and intended consumer. Mark experimental additions and known limitations; promote after the documented checks and consumer review. Deprecations identify the replacement and migration in the changelog. User testing and assistive-technology review remain release work even when all automated checks pass.

<!-- page: Tokens/Color (src/stories/tokens/Color.mdx) -->

# Colour and elevation

Semantic colour is tier 1. Every token references a palette step and carries a light value and a dark value, so a component never knows which mode it is in. Utilities are generated per property: a text token is only reachable as `text-*`, a background as `bg-*`, an icon as `icon-*`, a border as `border-*`. A `default` segment drops out of the name: `color.text.default` in the source is `color.text` on the sheet and `text-default` in a class.

The ramps are on the Palette sheet (Tokens/Palette). No ramp step has a utility. A component reads a semantic token or nothing.

## One accent

The canvas is white: `elevation.surface` is `color.neutral.0` in light. Blue is the only accent. Brand, selected, information and focus all draw on the blue ramp, so blue is spent on action, selection, focus and links and on nothing else.

| Job                                                          | Token                                            | Utility                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| The primary button                                           | `color.background.brand.bold`                    | `bg-brand-bold`                      |
| An active row, a checked menu item, an open dropdown trigger | `color.background.selected`                      | `bg-selected`                        |
| A selected tab's text and underline                          | `color.text.selected`, `color.border.selected`   | `text-selected`, `border-selected`   |
| The focus ring                                               | `color.border.focused` at `border.width.focused` | `border-focused`, `border-w-focused` |
| A link                                                       | `color.text.brand`                               | `text-brand`, or TextLink            |

Ids and counts stay neutral, and so does an avatar by default. An Id is blue only inside a link or a button (`ledger/id-not-blue`). Colour that carries no meaning is the accent family: `color.background.accent.*` in six hues, `subtler` under `color.text.accent.*` and `bolder` under `color.text.inverse`, for an avatar's tint, fill or gradient and, later, a tag. Teal and purple reach only the accent family and `color.chart.*`; a status is never drawn in them.

## Text and icons

| Job                                                        | Text                  | Icon                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------- |
| Content, sentence-case headings, buttons                   | `color.text`          | `color.icon`          |
| Secondary: navigation, field labels, subtle links          | `color.text.subtle`   | `color.icon.subtle`   |
| Tertiary: metadata, breadcrumbs, placeholders, helper text | `color.text.subtlest` | `color.icon.subtlest` |
| Off                                                        | `color.text.disabled` | `color.icon.disabled` |
| On a bold fill                                             | `color.text.inverse`  | `color.icon.inverse`  |

An icon mirrors its text, one step bolder where a thin glyph needs it. Text and Heading take these as `color="color.text.subtle"`; a class says `text-subtle`.

## Status

A tone is one decision. The subtle fill takes the tone's text. The bold fill takes inverse text; warning's bold fill is light, so it takes `color.text.warning.inverse`. A dot takes the tone's icon colour.

| Tone          | Subtle fill                    | Text                     | Bold fill                           | Icon                     |
| ------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `neutral`     | `color.background.neutral`     | `color.text.subtle`      | `color.background.neutral.bold`     | `color.icon.subtlest`    |
| `information` | `color.background.information` | `color.text.information` | `color.background.information.bold` | `color.icon.information` |
| `success`     | `color.background.success`     | `color.text.success`     | `color.background.success.bold`     | `color.icon.success`     |
| `warning`     | `color.background.warning`     | `color.text.warning`     | `color.background.warning.bold`     | `color.icon.warning`     |
| `danger`      | `color.background.danger`      | `color.text.danger`      | `color.background.danger.bold`      | `color.icon.danger`      |

Reach these through the `tone` prop on Badge, Dot, Indicator, Alert, Progress and Stat, never by hand. The `subtler` and `subtle` emphases are for lozenges and non-interactive chips. `hovered` and `pressed` are their own tokens, never alpha on the default (`ledger/no-alpha-token`). What each tone means in the product is in `docs/guides/status-vocabulary.md`.

## Minted, not yet drawn

The matrix is complete on purpose: every fill has `hovered` and `pressed`, every tone has `subtler`, `subtle`, the default and `bold`, the inverse subtle fill exists for a control on a bold fill, and the bolder text colours exist for a word on a tone's label. About forty of them have no part that draws them yet. That is accepted (2026-09-05): a token is minted when its place in the grammar is clear and drawn when the part arrives, so a part never invents a colour. The families still open, and the part each waits for:

| Family                                                                                                       | Waits for                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `color.background.{danger,warning,success,information}.{hovered,pressed}` and `.subtler.{hovered,pressed}`   | A status fill that is pressed: a toned chip that filters, a status pill that opens its record.                                                         |
| `color.background.{warning,success,information}.bold.{hovered,pressed}`, `neutral.bold.{hovered,pressed}`    | A bold button in a tone other than brand and danger.                                                                                                   |
| `color.background.brand.boldest` and states, `brand.subtlest.{hovered,pressed}`, `selected.bold` and states  | A pressed primary, a hovered brand tint, a bold selected control.                                                                                      |
| `color.background.danger.subtler`, `warning.subtler`, the three `.subtle`                                    | A lozenge emphasis between the subtle fill and the bold one.                                                                                           |
| `color.background.inverse.subtle`                                                                            | The resting fill of a control on a bold surface; its `hovered` and `pressed` are drawn by the Banner's action.                                         |
| `color.text.{danger,warning,success,information}.bolder`, `color.border.warning`, `color.border.information` | A word on a tone's label; a 3:1 status border in those tones.                                                                                          |
| `color.icon.warning.inverse`, `color.border.inverse`                                                         | An icon and a border on a bold warning fill; the Box paints its text inverse and icons follow it, so the icon token is reached through `currentColor`. |
| `elevation.surface.pressed`, `elevation.surface.overlay.{hovered,pressed}`, `elevation.shadow.overflow`      | A pressed page surface, a hovered overlay, a scroll edge.                                                                                              |

Drawn this pass: `color.background.input.pressed`, every field on focus; `color.background.inverse.subtle.hovered` and `.pressed`, the Banner's action under the pointer. The chart tokens are reached at runtime through `tone`, which a name scan cannot see; Patterns/Chart.

## Borders

Every border is a 1px hairline: `border.width` is 1px and `color.border` is the default colour. Prefer a rule to a box.

| Job                             | Token                   | Utility                             |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Hairlines, dividers, flat cards | `color.border`          | `border-default`                    |
| Emphasis that must pass 3:1     | `color.border.bold`     | `border-bold`                       |
| Text fields, checkboxes, radios | `color.border.input`    | `border-input`                      |
| Focus ring, 2px                 | `color.border.focused`  | `border-focused border-w-focused`   |
| Selected tab or item, 2px       | `color.border.selected` | `border-selected border-w-selected` |
| Off                             | `color.border.disabled` | `border-disabled`                   |

The field border is light by decision (2026-09-04): `color.border.input` is 1.87:1 on the light page and about 2:1 on the dark one, and the contrast test holds it at 1.5:1 or more on the page, sunken, raised, overlay and input surfaces, including the hovered and pressed input fills. The input surface, the hover tint and the focus and danger borders, which do meet 3:1, carry the affordance. A reader who asks for more contrast gets a field and choice-control boundary of 3:1 or more on every one of those surfaces: see Increased contrast below. Decorative rules and disabled controls use separate tokens; a decorative border must not be the only visible boundary of an interactive control.

The automated contrast contract covers default, hovered and pressed text/fill pairs, selected rows, status fills, focus and input borders, and translucent fills on their actual parent surfaces in both modes, at the standard contrast and the increased one. Alpha blends are composed in encoded sRGB before calculating WCAG luminance. These token checks complement rendered interaction and manual accessibility checks; they do not establish conformance for arbitrary custom combinations.

A status border comes in `default` (3:1) and `subtle` (decorative): `color.border.danger`, `color.border.danger.subtle`, and the same for warning, success and information.

## Increased contrast

The standard values above are the default, low-contrast choices included: a 1.87:1 field border, a 1.22:1 hairline, and selected, pressed and highlighted fills between 1.05:1 and 1.8:1. A reader who asks the system for more contrast gets a second set of values, in light and in dark, where every boundary and every state reads 3:1 against the surface, and a focus ring reads 3:1 on those states too.

| What turns it on                     | Where                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `prefers-contrast: more`             | The reader's system setting, for the whole document, unless the root pins standard.       |
| `data-contrast-mode="more"`          | Pins increased contrast on that element and everything inside it, usually `html`.         |
| `data-contrast-mode="no-preference"` | Pins the standard contrast, whatever the system says.                                     |
| No attribute                         | Follows the reader's setting, as `data-color-mode` absent follows `prefers-color-scheme`. |

The contrast and the colour mode are independent and nest either way: a dark region inside an increased-contrast page, or an increased-contrast region inside a dark one, takes the nearest of each. The mode switch does not set the contrast yet; a product that offers the choice writes the attribute on `html` itself, and the Storybook's Contrast toolbar does the same.

| Family                                                                                                    | Standard                                                 | Increased                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field and choice-control boundary, `color.border.input`                                                   | 1.87:1 light, about 2:1 dark                             | 3:1 or more on every surface and on the hovered and pressed input fills                                                                        |
| Hairline, `color.border`                                                                                  | 1.22:1 light, about 1.3:1 dark                           | 3:1 on every surface                                                                                                                           |
| Pressed and highlighted fills, `color.background.neutral` and `.subtle`, rest, hover, pressed             | 1.13:1 to 1.46:1 light, 1.16:1 to 1.78:1 dark            | 3:1 against the surface they sit on                                                                                                            |
| Selected fills, `color.background.selected`, rest, hover, pressed                                         | 1.05:1 to 1.22:1 light, 1.23:1 to 1.97:1 dark            | 3:1 against the surface                                                                                                                        |
| Text and icons on those fills: `color.text`, `.subtle`, `.selected`; `color.icon`, `.subtle`, `.selected` | 4.5:1 and 3:1 on the standard fills                      | `color.text`, the subtle ones and the selected ones step darker in light and lighter in dark, so they keep 4.5:1 and 3:1 on the stronger fills |
| Focus ring, `color.border.focused`                                                                        | 3:1 on the surface; 2.3:1 to 3.2:1 on the fills in light | 3:1 on the surface and on every fill above, so focus inside a selected or hovered row shows; darker in light, lighter in dark                  |

What it costs: secondary text reads closer to primary text (in dark, `color.text.subtle` is the same step as `color.text`), and a 3:1 fill is a mid tone, so a coloured word (a link, a status) on a hovered or selected row is not promised its 4.5:1 there, nor a coloured boundary (`color.border.selected`, `color.border.danger`) its 3:1 against the fill; each keeps 3:1 against the surface. `color.text.subtlest` steps up too but is held to the surfaces, as at the standard contrast, so a placeholder still reads apart from a value. Every pairing on this page is tested at both contrasts: `test/contrast.test.mjs` runs light and dark at each.

Nothing reads the contrast directly: a part uses the tokens and follows. `tokenValue()` returns the value in effect at the element it is given. For Figma and other DTCG tools the package exports `tokens.dtcg.light-contrast.json` and `tokens.dtcg.dark-contrast.json` beside the light and dark documents. Forced colours (Windows High Contrast) is a different mode, where the system replaces the palette; `forced-colors.css` handles it.

_Example: story `Stories.IncreasedContrast`._

## Blanket and skeleton

`color.blanket` (`bg-blanket`) is the scrim under a dialog, a drawer and the open side nav on a small screen. `color.skeleton` (`bg-skeleton`) is the loading fill; `color.skeleton.subtle` is its shimmer.

## Chart

A series on a chart is a `color.chart.*` token: a status tone when the series is a status, `brand` for the one the reader is asked to look at, `neutral` for context, or the categorical set, six hues in a fixed order validated for colour vision, then Other. Two scales exist for a heatmap: `sequential`, one hue from near zero to the most, and `diverging`, red against blue around grey. Every step is the same in both modes, and every series tone has a `hovered` step (one darker in light, one lighter in dark) for the mark under the pointer. The parts read these through `tone` on a series; `fill-chart-*`, `stroke-chart-*` and `bg-chart-*` let a bespoke SVG take the same paint. How each is used is on Patterns/Chart.

_Example: story `Stories.Chart`._
