<!-- page: Components/Announcer (src/stories/components/Announcer.mdx) -->

# Announcer

One channel for status messages a screen reader should hear while focus stays where it is: a result count after a search, a save, a page change. `announce(message, { politeness })` speaks through the page's two persistent live regions, and `Announcer` renders them, visually hidden.

```tsx
import { announce } from "@ledger/design-system";

announce("3 of 24 records");
announce("The file could not be uploaded. Try again.", { politeness: "assertive" });
```

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Where the regions come from

Shell mounts one Announcer, so a product with a Shell has nothing to add. A product without one mounts `<Announcer />` once near its root. `announce` speaks through the newest Announcer mounted. With none mounted it creates the regions at the end of the body and speaks once they have settled, so a part can announce before the product mounts one. On the server `announce` does nothing, and `Announcer` renders its empty regions into the markup, so they are in the page before the first message.

_Example: story `Stories.WithoutAnAnnouncer`._

## Politeness

`polite`, the default, waits until the reader is idle: the outcome of a search, a filter, a save, a new page. `assertive` interrupts whatever is being read, so keep it for the one failure that stops the task. An error that belongs to a field stays beside the field; the form announces one summary.

_Example: story `Stories.Politeness`._

## When to use it

- A change that is visible but silent: a result count, a page range, a saved state, a new page after client-side navigation (Shell does this with `locationKey`).
- A change whose visible form is far from focus, such as a count in the toolbar after typing in the search.

Not for:

- Text the reader is already focused on, or that a focus move will read. Moving focus is the announcement.
- A toast. Toaster announces its own messages.
- A persistent status the page shows, such as a Saving indicator beside a control. Keep that as visible text in the page; announce only the change.
- A modal decision. Use AlertDialog.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

## Accessibility

The regions are `role="log"` with `aria-live` and `aria-relevant="additions"`. Each message is a new line in its region, so the same words said twice are heard twice, and each line leaves after seven seconds, so the region never becomes a log a reader browses into. Base UI's modal dialogs keep `aria-live` regions exposed when they hide the page, so a message sent while one is open is still heard. Blank messages are dropped. Write the message as the sentence a sighted reader would take from the screen: "3 of 24 records", not "Search complete".

_Example: story `Stories.InADialog`._

## Props

_Props: generated from `Announcer`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

`Announcer` takes a div's native props and ref; it has no children. `announce(message: string, options?: { politeness?: "polite" | "assertive" })` returns nothing.

The model is [React Aria's live announcer](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/tree/main/packages/%40react-aria/live-announcer); see [WCAG 2.2 Understanding 4.1.3 Status Messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html).

<!-- page: Components/Attachment (src/stories/components/Attachment.mdx) -->

# Attachment

One file or image with its name, metadata and optional actions. Experimental; owner: Ledger maintainers. A base component for file presentation. Choosing files is [FileTrigger](?path=/docs/components-filetrigger--docs) or [DropZone](?path=/docs/components-dropzone--docs); the application owns uploading, retries, removal and preview dialogs, and shows each file as an Attachment.

## Anatomy

Compose only the parts the file needs:

| Part                   | Responsibility                                                                                      |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Attachment             | Surface, size, orientation and upload state.                                                        |
| Attachment.Media       | Icon or image preview.                                                                              |
| Attachment.Content     | Groups the name, metadata and optional progress.                                                    |
| Attachment.Title       | Filename, cut in the middle so its end and extension stay in view; read whole.                      |
| Attachment.Description | File type, size, status or a wrapping failure explanation.                                          |
| Attachment.Trigger     | Optional card-wide action button: preview, download a file the page builds.                         |
| Attachment.Link        | Optional card-wide link: a file the server holds (`href`, `download`), or a router link (`render`). |
| Attachment.Actions     | Independent controls above the trigger or link.                                                     |
| Attachment.Action      | IconButton with a required `label` and `icon`.                                                      |
| Attachment.Group       | Horizontally scrollable row.                                                                        |

Each part is also exported by name (`AttachmentTitle`, `AttachmentLink`, …) for its props table.

```tsx
<Attachment>
  <Attachment.Media aria-hidden="true">
    <FileText />
  </Attachment.Media>
  <Attachment.Content>
    <Attachment.Title>quarterly-report.pdf</Attachment.Title>
    <Attachment.Description>PDF · {formatFileSize(file.size)}</Attachment.Description>
  </Attachment.Content>
  <Attachment.Trigger aria-label="Preview quarterly-report.pdf" onClick={openPreview} />
  <Attachment.Actions>
    <Attachment.Action label="Remove quarterly-report.pdf" icon={<X />} onClick={removeFile} />
  </Attachment.Actions>
</Attachment>
```

## Variants

`orientation="horizontal"` places media beside metadata; `vertical` places it above. `Media variant="image"` crops a caller-rendered image into a square preview. Supply `alt=""` when it repeats the filename without adding useful information; otherwise describe the image. The caller owns unavailable-image fallbacks and object URL cleanup.

_Example: story `Stories.Images`._

## Sizes

`medium` is the default, with 12px padding and 40px media. `small` uses 8px padding and 32px media; `xsmall` uses 6px padding and 24px media. Small sizes use the small body token. Metadata remains visible at every size. Action buttons keep their minimum 28px target. Vertical media fills the card width. Override width on the root or constrain its container.

_Example: story `Stories.AttachmentMatrix`._

## States

`idle` uses a dashed border; `uploading` and `processing` set `aria-busy`; `error` changes the border and description to danger; `done` is the default resting surface. These are caller-supplied states, with no internal transitions. Write the status or error in Description so color is never its only signal. Compose Spinner or Progress when useful; filename animation is not imposed. Spinner respects reduced motion.

An upload in progress offers a Cancel named for the file ("Cancel uploading quarterly-report.pdf"); a failure offers a Retry and a Remove. When a result replaces the control that had focus (Cancel goes with the upload), move focus to the control that replaces it. `aria-busy` marks the work but announces nothing when it ends, so say each result through `announce` ("Uploaded quarterly-report.pdf.", "Cancelled the upload of quarterly-report.pdf."). [DropZone](?path=/docs/components-dropzone--docs) shows the whole flow.

_Example: story `Stories.UploadStates`._

## Long names

`Attachment.Title` cuts a plain-text name in the middle: the start ends in an ellipsis and the end, the extension and the ten characters before it, stays whole, so `acas-vulnerability-scan-ws-x90-2026-09-01.pdf` and `…-09-15.pdf` stay apart. Assistive technology reads the whole name once, and copying a selection inside the title gives the name as it is written. The kept end follows the name's own direction, so an English name on a right-to-left page still ends with its extension. `truncate="end"` cuts at the end instead; a Title whose children are elements always does. With a card-wide Trigger or Link over the card, a `title` on the Title is covered: put the full name in the Trigger's or Link's `title` for a pointer, as well as in its `aria-label`.

_Example: story `Stories.LongNames`._

## Links and downloads

Trigger is an action button with `type="button"` by default; use `render` to compose a custom button that forwards its props and ref. For navigation or a file the server holds, use `Attachment.Link`: an anchor with the same overlay, which keeps native link behaviour (open in a new tab, copy the address, `download`) and takes `render` for a router link. A file the page builds (an export, a CSV) is a Trigger that calls `downloadBlob(blob, name)` or `downloadText(text, name, { type, bom })`; they click a hidden anchor and revoke the object URL 40 seconds later (`DOWNLOAD_REVOKE_DELAY`), never in the same task, which can cancel the save in Safari and Firefox. Pass `bom: true` for a CSV a reader will open in a spreadsheet.

The card takes the raised hover surface while its Trigger or Link is hovered (where the pointer can hover) and the pressed surface while it is pressed, so an interactive card looks different from a static one. A disabled Trigger does neither. Hovering an action in Actions leaves the card at rest.

_Example: story `Stories.LinksAndDownloads`._

A card-wide anchor styled with `buttonVariants` and the overlay classes, as earlier pages showed, still works; `Attachment.Link` replaces it. Existing `Attachment.Trigger asChild` navigation migrates to `Attachment.Link`.

## File sizes

`formatFileSize(bytes, { locale })` says a byte count as a reader does: "512 bytes", "840 kB", "2.4 MB". Units are decimal (1 kB is 1,000 bytes), as their names mean and as macOS and iOS report sizes, with at most one decimal in the locale's numerals; pass `useLedgerLocale().locale` in a component. Express a limit in the same units (`50_000_000` for 50 MB) so the Description, a DropZone's refusal and the hint agree.

_Example: story `Stories.FileSizes`._

## Content

Keep the filename recognizable, including its extension. Description supports multiple lines so failure reasons and recovery instructions remain visible. Place all interactive content in Actions when using the card-wide Trigger or Link; avoid wrapping the whole card in a button or link. Actions accepts ordinary Button, IconButton, menus or links when its icon-button shortcut does not fit.

_Example: story `Stories.WithActions`._

## Style

Ledger surface, border, text, spacing, icon, radius and focus tokens. Horizontal cards fit their content; vertical cards default to the rail width. Actions remain in normal flow even on images so they do not cover the preview or its metadata. Group preserves the scrollbar and uses proximity snapping. No external stylesheet, uploader dependency or runtime media inference is required.

_Example: story `Stories.Group`._

## Accessibility

Every Trigger and Link needs `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; it is an empty overlay with no text of its own. Icon actions require a descriptive `label`, such as “Remove quarterly-report.pdf”. The overlay and the actions are sibling controls with independent focus and activation. Put the Trigger or Link before Actions in the DOM for open-then-actions tab order. Return focus to a surviving control after removal; the With Actions example offers Undo.

No live region is imposed. `aria-busy` identifies in-progress content but does not announce completion; say upload results through `announce`, the page's polite status. Give Progress a label. Hide decorative icons explicitly. For a group containing no interactive attachments, add `tabIndex={0}`, `role="group"` and an accessible name to make horizontal scrolling available from the keyboard. Interactive attachments are reached by Tab, which scrolls them into view.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Attachment`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Attachment.Media

_Props: generated from `AttachmentMedia`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Attachment.Title

_Props: generated from `AttachmentTitle`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Attachment.Trigger

_Props: generated from `AttachmentTrigger`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Attachment.Link

_Props: generated from `AttachmentLink`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Every part is exported by name as well as a member (`AttachmentMedia` is `Attachment.Media`), and all compound part prop types are exported. Each part takes its element's native props and ref and names itself last with `data-slot` (`attachment`, `attachment-media` and so on), so a caller's props never replace a part's identity. `Attachment.Action` accepts IconButton props; Trigger supports Button's native attributes, ref and `render` composition. The app's old shadcn copy uses different size and action APIs; import the Ledger component from `@ledger/design-system`.

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._
_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[FileTrigger](?path=/docs/components-filetrigger--docs), [DropZone](?path=/docs/components-dropzone--docs), [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs), [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs), [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs), [Composer](?path=/docs/patterns-composer--docs). Reference: [shadcn Attachment](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/attachment).

## Don't

Do not build upload orchestration or infer preview behavior inside Attachment. Do not nest a remove button inside the card's trigger. Do not communicate upload failure through a red border alone, hide recovery copy with truncation, or force every group into a carousel with hidden scrollbars.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

<!-- page: Components/Avatar (src/stories/components/Avatar.mdx) -->

# Avatar

Represent a person or entity with Base UI image loading and shadcn's flat Avatar parts. Ledger retains its sizes, shapes and accent treatments.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Avatar role="img" aria-label="Dana Whitfield" size="medium">
  <AvatarImage src="/dana.png" alt="" />
  <AvatarFallback>DW</AvatarFallback>
  <AvatarBadge tone="success" />
</Avatar>
```

Compose overlapping avatars with `AvatarGroup` and `AvatarGroupCount`. The caller chooses members and writes the overflow count. `Person` remains the small avatar plus visible name used in record rows.

## Variants and states

Sizes are `xsmall`, `small` (default), `medium`, `large` and `xlarge`. Shapes are `circle` and `square`; treatments are `neutral`, `tinted`, `bold` and `gradient`. Use `avatarHue(name)` when a person's accent should stay stable and `avatarInitials(name, count)` to produce fallback text.

_Example: story `Stories.AvatarMatrix`._
_Example: story `Stories.People`._

Base UI shows the fallback while the image loads or fails. `AvatarFallback.delay` can delay its appearance. Changing Image's `src` retries loading.

_Example: story `Stories.ImageLoading`._

## Accessibility

Name an informative avatar with `role="img"` and `aria-label`, including meaningful presence information. When a visible name already identifies the person, set `aria-hidden="true"` on the avatar. A named group can hide its avatars and count when its accessible name already describes the entire group. Give Image an empty alt when the root supplies the name.

## Props

Root, Image and Fallback preserve their native Base UI props, refs, `render`, and state-based classes/styles. Badge accepts native span props and Ledger's `tone`. Group and GroupCount accept native div props. Ref targets follow each part.

Replace `Avatar name/src` with explicit Image and Fallback children; replace `isDecorative` with native `aria-hidden`. Replace `Avatar.Stack names/max` with caller-owned `AvatarGroup` children and `AvatarGroupCount`. There is one composition API.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Related

[shadcn Avatar](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/avatar) · [Base UI Avatar](https://base-ui.com/react/components/avatar) · [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs)

<!-- page: Components/Badge (src/stories/components/Badge.mdx) -->

# Badge

A compact label built on the shadcn Base UI Badge foundation and adapted to Ledger. One Badge combines six visual treatments with semantic tones, subtle or bold emphasis, two density sizes, optional icons, and rendered-link composition. Every combination uses the same pill anatomy.

`variant` chooses the treatment and its defaults; `tone` chooses the palette; `appearance` adjusts the emphasis of filled treatments; `size` adjusts density. With no props, Badge is the standard brand-filled `default` variant. A `tone` without a `variant` is a status: the `secondary` treatment, the subtle fill in that tone, so `<Badge tone="warning">` never renders a loud bold pill by accident. Bold is asked for, with `appearance="bold"` or an explicit `variant="default"`.

_Example: story `Stories.Matrix`._

## Anatomy

| Export or part  | Responsibility                                                                                                              |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Badge`         | A `span` by default, or the element supplied through Base UI's `render` prop.                                               |
| `badgeVariants` | The shared class recipe for treatment, tone, emphasis, and size. Consumers composing their own element can use it directly. |
| Label           | Concise children that remain meaningful without color or an icon.                                                           |
| Icon            | An optional leading `icon`, or explicit icon children with `data-icon="inline-start"` / `"inline-end"`.                     |

Badge emits `data-slot="badge"` and its resolved `data-variant`, `data-tone`, `data-appearance`, and `data-size`. Palette choices do not select a different component or change the shape.

```tsx
import { Badge, badgeVariants } from "@ledger/design-system";
import { ArrowUpRight, CircleCheck } from "lucide-react";

<Badge>Featured</Badge>;
<Badge variant="secondary" tone="neutral">
  Draft
</Badge>;
<Badge variant="secondary" tone="success" icon={<CircleCheck aria-hidden="true" />}>
  Verified
</Badge>;
<Badge variant="secondary" tone="danger" appearance="bold" size="xsmall">
  Overdue
</Badge>;
<Badge variant="outline" tone="success" render={<a href="/evidence" />}>
  Verified evidence
  <ArrowUpRight aria-hidden="true" data-icon="inline-end" />
</Badge>;

<span className={badgeVariants({ variant: "secondary", tone: "success", size: "xsmall" })}>
  Verified
</span>;
```

The recipe supplies classes only. A consumer using `badgeVariants` directly owns its element, attributes, refs, semantics, and composition.

_Example: story `Stories.Recipe`._

_Example: story `Stories.ToneWithoutVariant`._

## Variants

All six treatments accept the same tone and size axes.

| `variant`     | Default palette / emphasis | Treatment                                                                                      |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`     | Brand / bold               | Filled. A rendered anchor uses the palette's hover fill. The default.                          |
| `secondary`   | Neutral / subtle           | Filled. A rendered anchor uses the palette's hover fill.                                       |
| `destructive` | Danger / subtle            | Filled. Its default danger tone uses the danger focus outline.                                 |
| `outline`     | Neutral                    | Transparent with a visible border; a rendered anchor gains the palette's subtle fill on hover. |
| `ghost`       | Neutral                    | Transparent, with the palette's subtle fill on hover.                                          |
| `link`        | Brand                      | Palette-colored text, underlined on hover. Render an anchor to give it link behavior.          |

`appearance="subtle"` or `"bold"` overrides the filled treatments' default emphasis. Outline, ghost, and link retain their treatment when an appearance is supplied. `tone` overrides the palette across every variant, including outline borders and link text. Semantic colors adapt to light and dark modes; bold warning badges use the dark `color.text.warning.inverse` text token.

| Tone          | Meaning                                                                      |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `brand`       | Branding or a featured label. The default palette for `default` and `link`.  |
| `neutral`     | A category, kind, or state without a judgment: Inspection, Draft, Inherited. |
| `information` | In progress: In review, In remediation.                                      |
| `success`     | Done and good: Verified, Satisfied, Closed.                                  |
| `warning`     | Needs attention soon: Due soon, Partial, Suspect.                            |
| `danger`      | Wrong or late: Overdue, Other than satisfied, Invalidated.                   |

_Example: story `Stories.SemanticMatrix`._

The next matrix applies every status tone to all six variants at the compact size. Outline and link examples render actual anchors. The radius, icon anatomy, and density are shared across the matrix.

_Example: story `Stories.SemanticVariants`._

## Sizes

| `size`   | Height / text | Use                                                 |
| -------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 20px / 12px   | Default. Beside a title, in a rail, or in a header. |
| `xsmall` | 16px / 11px   | A table row, a tab, or a dense list item.           |

Both sizes use the same pill radius and 12px icons. Small badges use 8px horizontal padding, reduced to 6px beside a marked icon; xsmall badges keep 4px padding for density. The width follows the label, which stays on one line. Containers should wrap separate badges when space is limited; keep long labels readable.

_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

_Example: story `Stories.DenseAndLongContent`._

## States

| State           | Behavior                                                                                            |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain label     | Native span semantics. No default tab stop or action.                                               |
| Rendered anchor | Native link semantics, Tab focus, Enter activation, and treatment-specific hover styling.           |
| Focus visible   | Focus border and Ledger's 2px outline with a 2px offset. A danger tone uses the danger outline.     |
| Invalid         | Caller-owned `aria-invalid` selects the danger border and outline color. It does not validate data. |

Badge manages no selection, dismissal, loading, or disabled state. Use an appropriate interactive control for those behaviors. A variant supplies presentation; a rendered element supplies its native interaction semantics.

_Example: story `Stories.States`._

## Composition

### Links

Keep the destination on the rendered anchor or router element. A router adapter must forward every received prop and its ref to the actual anchor so that styles, handlers, and accessibility attributes reach the same element.

```tsx
import { forwardRef, type ComponentProps } from "react";
import { Badge } from "@ledger/design-system";

type RouterLinkProps = Omit<ComponentProps<"a">, "href"> & { to: string };

const RouterLink = forwardRef<HTMLAnchorElement, RouterLinkProps>(function RouterLink(
  { to, ...props },
  ref,
) {
  return <a ref={ref} href={to} {...props} />;
});

<Badge variant="outline" tone="information" render={<RouterLink to="/programs" />}>
  Programs
</Badge>;
```

Base UI merges attributes, classes, styles, event handlers, and both refs onto the same rendered element.

_Example: story `Stories.RenderLink`._

### Icons and conditional content

Use `icon={<CircleCheck aria-hidden="true" />}` for a leading icon, or place icons explicitly among the children. Explicit leading and trailing icons use `data-icon="inline-start"` and `data-icon="inline-end"` to select the corresponding padding. An icon element supplied through the shorthand receives the leading marker. Keep the label meaningful whether an optional icon is present or absent.

_Example: story `Stories.ConditionalIcons`._

## Content

- Use one or two words that remain useful without color: Verified, In review, Overdue.
- Use the state rather than the tone name: Overdue, not Danger.
- Keep categories neutral; their words distinguish them.
- Use one vocabulary for each state throughout the product.
- Keep bold emphasis for the status that needs the most attention.
- Give rendered links labels that make their destinations understandable.

_Example: story `Stories.Categories`._

_Example: story `Stories.OneBold`._

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

_Example: story `Stories.StatusGuidance`._

## Accessibility

- A plain Badge is inline text. A click handler does not make it a keyboard control.
- A link requires an actual anchor with a destination through `render`; `variant="link"` supplies presentation only.
- A badge rendered as an anchor or a button takes a hit area of at least 24px where any pointer is coarse, and stops clipping so the area reaches past the pill. A label badge stays unpositioned.
- Native attributes and refs reach the actual element. Custom router adapters must forward them.
- Pair semantic colors with visible words and hide decorative icons from assistive technology.
- Use native controls for selection or dismissal. Badge does not implement those behaviors.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

## Props

`BadgeProps` combines native span props and Base UI's `render` composition with the shared recipe's variant, tone, appearance, and size axes, plus the optional icon. `React.ComponentProps<typeof Badge>` derives the same component props. The ref receives the actual rendered element; anchor-specific props such as `href` belong on the anchor supplied through `render`.

_Props: generated from `Badge`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Migration

| Previous use                                        | Updated use                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<Badge tone="success">Verified</Badge>`            | Renders as `<Badge variant="secondary" tone="success">`, the subtle status. Spell the variant for clarity. |
| Neutral `<Badge>Draft</Badge>`                      | `<Badge variant="secondary" tone="neutral">Draft</Badge>`. The unconfigured default is now brand/bold.     |
| `appearance="bold"`, `size="xsmall"`, or `icon={…}` | Keep these conveniences on Badge. Use `secondary` for existing status compositions.                        |
| A clickable span                                    | Supply a real anchor through `render` for navigation.                                                      |
| `BadgeProps`                                        | Continue using the same export; it now also includes variants and Base UI render composition.              |

All Badge uses now share the shadcn-derived pill shape, including semantic tones. Existing semantic palettes and compact heights remain, while small labels adopt the shared padding and border anatomy. `Count`, `Dot`, `Indicator`, `Tone`, `tones`, and `toneClasses` keep their existing contracts. `Avatar.Badge` and `AvatarGroupCount` remain separate Avatar parts with their existing APIs. The checked-in shadcn reference and the unrelated reui Badge remain separate code.

## Related

- [Count](?path=/docs/components-count--docs): numeric counts.
- [Indicator](?path=/docs/components-indicator--docs): a status dot and a word.
- [FilterChip](?path=/docs/components-filterchip--docs): a filter the reader can change.
- Reference: [shadcn Base UI Badge](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/badge). The checked-in application reference is the foundation for this adaptation.

<!-- page: Components/Banner (src/stories/components/Banner.mdx) -->

# Banner

A message about the whole site, at the top of the screen in the shell's Banner area: the loss of data or a function, or something site-wide that changes what the reader can do. One at a time, never dismissible, gone when no longer true. It is one line and truncates rather than wraps; the action is one link or button drawn in the banner's own colour. The kit's inline message is the [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs).

An Alert is about the record; a Banner is about the site. Feedback after an act is a toast. If the message would be true for one reader and not the next, it is not a banner.

_Example: story `Stories.BannerMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                  |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bar     | 48px, `dimension.layout.banner`, the tone's bold fill, its content centred, `space.200` inside at each end. |
| Icon    | The tone's icon at `dimension.icon.small`: Info, TriangleAlert, CircleAlert. `icon` replaces it.            |
| Message | One line in `font.body` medium and the inverse text colour. It truncates.                                   |
| Action  | One link or button after the message, underlined, in the banner's own text colour.                          |

## Variants

Banner has one appearance; the tone is what varies, and there are three.

| Tone          | Use                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `information` | Something changed for everyone: the catalogue moved to a new revision, a maintenance window is booked.   |
| `warning`     | The default. Something is about to change what the reader can do: the audit window closes, uploads lock. |
| `danger`      | Something is lost: the connection to the evidence store, the session's writes. Announced at once.        |

There is no success banner and no neutral one: a banner is gone when it is no longer true, and good news is feedback, which is a toast. The kit has the bold fill only, no low-contrast form, since a banner is by definition the one thing on the screen that outranks the page.

Where it lives: `Shell.Banner` is the area, above the top navigation. It holds the Banner and pushes the page down by the banner's height while one is rendered; see [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs).

## Sizes

One: the width of the screen at 48px. On a narrow screen the message truncates and the action stays; the message should be short enough that a phone shows most of it.

## States

Present or absent. A banner is rendered while its condition holds and unmounted when it stops; there is no dismissed state, no hover, and no collapsed form. Its action has the kit's focus outline.

## Modifiers

- **`tone`** as in Variants; `warning` when unsaid.
- **`action`** for the one link or button: an anchor, a button, or the router's Link. The Banner colours it and underlines it; it keeps its own `onClick` or `to`.
- **`icon`** to replace the tone's icon with a more specific one, rarely.
- **`className`** for the shell's layout, not for colour.

_Example: story `Stories.Banners`._

## Content

- **One sentence: the fact and what it changes.** "The audit window closes in three days; evidence uploads lock after that."
- **Present tense, plain.** No "Please note", no "Attention".
- **The action names where it goes:** "See what changed", "Ask for an extension". One.
- **Not feedback, not a greeting, not a record.** Those are a toast, nothing, and an Alert.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                  |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Bar     | `dimension.layout.banner` 48px · `color.background.<tone>.bold` · `space.200` inline · `space.100` gap |
| Text    | `font.body` medium · `color.text.inverse`, `color.text.warning.inverse` on warning                     |
| Icon    | `dimension.icon.small` 14px in the text colour                                                         |
| Action  | Underlined, `radius.xsmall` for its focus outline                                                      |

The bold fills are Badge's bold appearance, so a danger banner and a danger bold Badge are the same red.

## Accessibility

- **A danger Banner is `role="alert"`**, announced at once; the rest are `role="status"`. The shell's Banner area is a region named "Banner".
- **Truncation hides words from sighted readers only;** a screen reader hears the whole line. Keep it short so both get the same message.
- **The action is in the tab order; the banner is not.** It sits first in the page, before the top navigation, so it is the first thing a keyboard reader meets, which is the point.
- **The bold fills pass 4.5:1** with the inverse text in both modes; the contrast test covers them.

Action focus rings inherit the banner’s contrasting text color, keeping the ring visible against every bold tone.

## Props

Native `div` props and refs target the outer message. IDs, ARIA, data attributes, styles and handlers are forwarded; `className` merges with the default layout. The default role remains `status`, or `alert` for danger. An explicit `role` or live-region attribute controls delivery when the enclosing page needs different announcement behavior.

The `action` keeps its own element, ref, ID, attributes, styles and handlers while receiving the banner’s action classes. A root click handler receives the action’s bubbled click. Default icons are decorative.

_Props: generated from `Banner`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs): the message about a record.
- [Toaster](?path=/docs/components-toaster--docs): feedback after an act.
- [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs): the Banner area.
- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): the tone table.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Breadcrumb (src/stories/components/Breadcrumb.mdx) -->

# Breadcrumb

Show where the reader is in the record tree and provide links to its parent levels. Breadcrumb follows the shadcn Base UI component structure, with Ledger's typography, color, spacing, icon, focus, and motion tokens.

Compose the list, items, links, separators, and current page explicitly. The component does not generate separators or infer the current page. The list keeps the trail on one line in any container: when it does not fit, the middle levels fold behind an ellipsis whose menu lists them as links.

_Example: story `Stories.BreadcrumbMatrix`._

## Anatomy

All seven parts are named exports from `@ledger/design-system`.

| Part                  | Default element and responsibility                                                                             |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Breadcrumb`          | A `nav` with `aria-label="breadcrumb"`. Contains the list.                                                     |
| `BreadcrumbList`      | An `ol` that keeps one line and folds levels behind an ellipsis menu, or wraps.                                |
| `BreadcrumbItem`      | An `li` for one level, on the list's line or in its wrapping text. Contains a link, page, or composed control. |
| `BreadcrumbLink`      | An `a`, or the element supplied through Base UI's `render` prop. Always an ancestor: it drops an `aria-current` it is handed. |
| `BreadcrumbPage`      | A `span` with `role="link"`, `aria-disabled="true"`, and `aria-current="page"`.                                |
| `BreadcrumbSeparator` | A decorative `li` between items. A chevron by default; accepts custom children.                                |
| `BreadcrumbEllipsis`  | A decorative `span` containing a horizontal ellipsis. Provides no interaction by itself.                       |

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from "@ledger/design-system";

<Breadcrumb aria-label="Program hierarchy">
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink href="/programs">Programs</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink href="/programs/atlas">Atlas payments platform</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbPage>Controls</BreadcrumbPage>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>;
```

_Example: story `Stories.Basic`._

## Variants

The component has one appearance. Its parts support different compositions without adding variant props.

| Composition       | How to build it                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Standard trail    | Place `BreadcrumbLink` in each parent item and `BreadcrumbPage` in the final item.                                                                                                      |
| Custom separator  | Pass text or an icon to `BreadcrumbSeparator`, such as `<BreadcrumbSeparator>/</BreadcrumbSeparator>`.                                                                                  |
| Collapsed parents | Automatic: the list folds middle levels behind its own ellipsis menu. For a disclosure of your own, set `overflow="wrap"` and put `BreadcrumbEllipsis` inside a named button.           |
| Icon or badge     | Put an icon inside `BreadcrumbLink` with `className="inline-flex items-center gap-050"`, and a badge in the `BreadcrumbItem` beside the link. The level keeps its whole width or folds. |
| Local hierarchy   | Render an actual button through `BreadcrumbLink` for a level that changes state in place.                                                                                               |
| Single page       | One `BreadcrumbItem` containing `BreadcrumbPage`, without separators.                                                                                                                   |

_Example: story `Stories.CustomSeparator`._

### Collapsed parents

The list folds levels by itself when its container is too narrow (see [Sizes](#sizes)). To own the disclosure instead, set `overflow="wrap"` on the list so the two do not compete.

Ellipsis is hidden from assistive technology, including its internal "More" text. Give the enclosing control its own accessible name and implement its behavior. This example uses a disclosure button with `aria-expanded`, reveals the parents inline, and retains keyboard focus on the button.

```tsx
import { BreadcrumbEllipsis, BreadcrumbItem } from "@ledger/design-system";

<BreadcrumbItem>
  <button
    type="button"
    aria-label={expanded ? "Hide parent levels" : "Show parent levels"}
    aria-expanded={expanded}
    onClick={() => setExpanded((value) => !value)}
  >
    <BreadcrumbEllipsis />
  </button>
</BreadcrumbItem>;
```

_Example: story `Stories.Collapsed`._

## Sizes

One default size: `font.body.small`. The trail follows the width of its container, not the window, so it behaves the same on a page, in a panel and on a phone.

With `overflow="collapse"` (the default) the trail stays on one line. When it does not fit, it gives up space in this order:

1. The middle levels fold behind the ellipsis, nearest the root first.
2. The parent's and the current page's names share what is left. The longer one shortens first, down to 80px, so the shorter keeps its whole name while it can.
3. The root folds, and the ellipsis leads the line.
4. The parent folds, leaving the ellipsis and the page.

A shortened name keeps its full text as its title, and a link never shrinks below 80px (or its whole name, when that is shorter). The ellipsis menu lists the folded levels as links in order, and every level returns when the space does. The line never starts or ends with a separator.

Only `BreadcrumbPage` and a `BreadcrumbLink` whose children are text shorten. A level composed from other content, such as an icon beside the name or a plain `span` for a level the reader cannot go back to, keeps its whole width or folds; folded, it appears in the ellipsis menu under its link's name, or as a disabled item when it has no link. The line keeps the height of its tallest level whether that level shows or folds, so the page below does not move as levels fold.

_Example: story `Stories.CollapsesToFit`._

_Example: story `Stories.LongerNameGivesWay`._

_Example: story `Stories.ShortTrailFoldsTheRoot`._

_Example: story `Stories.RootFoldsLast`._

_Example: story `Stories.UnlinkedParentFolds`._

_Example: story `Stories.ComposedLevels`._

The trail folds to the width it is given: a block such as `PageHeader.Lead`, or a flex item with `min-width: 0`, which `Breadcrumb` has by itself. Beside an action it may size to its content; it still follows the row as it narrows and widens. A wrapper around it in a flex row needs `min-w-0` too; without it, the row grows to the whole trail.

_Example: story `Stories.BesideAnAction`._

With `overflow="wrap"` every level shows and the trail wraps at word boundaries; each separator starts its line with the level it leads to.

_Example: story `Stories.LongWrappingTrail`._

_Example: story `Stories.AboveTitle`._

## States

| State             | Behavior                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Parent link       | Subtle text, default text color on hover; native Tab and Enter behavior.                                                      |
| Keyboard focus    | Ledger's focus outline on the rendered link or button.                                                                        |
| Current page      | Regular-weight default text. Announced as the current, disabled link; no `href` or default tab stop.                          |
| Folded levels     | Out of the line and the accessibility tree; listed as links in the ellipsis menu, whose button is named "Show hidden levels". |
| Shortened name    | Ends in an ellipsis; the full name is the link's or page's `title`.                                                           |
| Collapsed parents | With `overflow="wrap"`, application-owned state on the enclosing control; the ellipsis is decorative.                         |

`BreadcrumbPage` preserves shadcn's accessible semantics: it is a noninteractive span exposed as a disabled current link. Its role does not make it an anchor or add keyboard behavior.

## Modifiers

- **`aria-label`** on `Breadcrumb` names the navigation landmark. The default is lowercase `breadcrumb` (the `breadcrumb` message, which a `LedgerProvider` can translate).
- **`overflow`** on `BreadcrumbList`: `"collapse"` (default) keeps one line and folds levels; `"wrap"` shows every level on as many lines as it needs.
- **`render`** on `BreadcrumbLink` composes a router link or another suitable element through Base UI's `useRender` and `mergeProps`.
- **`children`** on `BreadcrumbSeparator` replaces the default chevron.
- **Native props and `ref`** reach each part's rendered DOM element. Use `className` and `style` on the relevant part for a deliberate layout adjustment.

### Router link composition

The custom component must forward its received props and ref to its actual anchor. This allows Base UI to compose event handlers, classes, attributes, and both refs on the same element.

```tsx
import { forwardRef, type ComponentProps } from "react";
import { BreadcrumbItem, BreadcrumbLink } from "@ledger/design-system";

type RouterLinkProps = Omit<ComponentProps<"a">, "href"> & { to: string };

const RouterLink = forwardRef<HTMLAnchorElement, RouterLinkProps>(function RouterLink(
  { to, ...props },
  ref,
) {
  return <a ref={ref} href={to} {...props} />;
});

<BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbLink render={<RouterLink to="/programs" />}>Programs</BreadcrumbLink>
</BreadcrumbItem>;
```

The example below verifies that props and both refs reach the anchor, and that mouse and keyboard activation each invoke the adapter and breadcrumb handlers. Its adapter prevents navigation to keep the demonstration in the canvas.

_Example: story `Stories.RenderLink`._

### The current page and router links

Only `BreadcrumbPage` is the current page. A router link marks itself `aria-current="page"` whenever the current path starts with its own, so on `/programs/atlas/controls` a trail of plain router links announces Programs and the program as the current page too, and a screen reader says so on every level. A trail must have exactly one current page, and it is the last level.

BreadcrumbLink is always an ancestor, so it drops an `aria-current` it is handed. That covers a router that renders through the part. With TanStack Router, create the trail link once:

```tsx
import { createLink } from "@tanstack/react-router";
import { BreadcrumbLink } from "@ledger/design-system";

// The router works out the href and the active state, then renders BreadcrumbLink with them.
export const TrailLink = createLink(BreadcrumbLink);

<BreadcrumbItem>
  <TrailLink to="/programs">Programs</TrailLink>
</BreadcrumbItem>;
```

A router Link given as a `render` element sets the attribute inside itself, after the kit's props, where BreadcrumbLink cannot reach. Give it exact matching instead, so an ancestor is never active:

```tsx
<BreadcrumbLink render={<Link to="/programs" activeOptions={{ exact: true }} />}>
  Programs
</BreadcrumbLink>
```

Either way, compose the trail once in the application, next to its record links, rather than at every page. The kit does not strip the attribute from the DOM after the router sets it: React and the router own it.

_Example: story `Stories.RouterLinks`._

### In-place state

Use an anchor for page navigation. For a hierarchy that updates local state, supply a native button explicitly:

```tsx
<BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbLink render={<button type="button" onClick={() => selectLevel("programs")} />}>
    Programs
  </BreadcrumbLink>
</BreadcrumbItem>
```

The rendered control remains a button, including its Enter and Space behavior. This is a local record hierarchy; use [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs) for sequential tasks.

_Example: story `Stories.InPlaceButtons`._

### Migration from the previous Ledger API

This is a breaking API change. Update complete breadcrumb compositions, including their surrounding layout.

| Previous API or behavior                            | New composition                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Breadcrumb.Item`                                   | Import `BreadcrumbItem` as a named export.                                                                                                                    |
| Root automatically supplied `ol`                    | Place `BreadcrumbList` inside `Breadcrumb`.                                                                                                                   |
| Item automatically supplied its leading chevron     | Place `BreadcrumbSeparator` between items.                                                                                                                    |
| `<Breadcrumb.Item isCurrent>Page</Breadcrumb.Item>` | `<BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Page</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>`                                                                                      |
| `Breadcrumb.Item asChild` around an anchor          | Put `BreadcrumbLink href="…"` inside `BreadcrumbItem`.                                                                                                        |
| `Breadcrumb.Item asChild` around a router link      | Put `BreadcrumbLink render={<RouterLink to="…" />}` inside `BreadcrumbItem`.                                                                                  |
| Item `onClick` implicitly created a button          | Explicitly render a button through `BreadcrumbLink`, or compose a suitable control inside `BreadcrumbItem`.                                                   |
| Root `label="Program hierarchy"`                    | Root `aria-label="Program hierarchy"`.                                                                                                                        |
| Item `className` styled its link or page            | Apply that class to `BreadcrumbLink` or `BreadcrumbPage`; item props now target the `li`.                                                                     |
| Current page used medium weight                     | `BreadcrumbPage` uses regular weight, following shadcn's structure and styling intent.                                                                        |
| Every crumb truncated to keep one line              | The list keeps one line by folding middle levels behind an ellipsis menu; only the current page and the parent shorten, each with its full name as the title. |

`BreadcrumbProps` and `BreadcrumbItemProps` remain exported as aliases for their native `nav` and `li` props. They no longer contain the old custom props. For any part, `React.ComponentProps<typeof BreadcrumbLink>` (or the corresponding component) derives its public props.

## Content

- Use the level's actual name: "Programs", "Atlas payments platform", "Controls".
- Order the trail from the highest relevant parent to the current page.
- Include the record's identifier when it is needed to distinguish that record.
- Keep tabs and browsing history out of the hierarchy.
- Retain readable names at narrow widths; reveal omitted parents through a labeled, working control.

## Style

| Element                     | Ledger tokens and classes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| List typography             | `font.body.small` / `font-body-small`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Parent links and separators | `color.text.subtle` / `text-subtle`; links use `color.text` / `text-default` on hover                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Current page                | `color.text` / `text-default`, `font-regular`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| List gap                    | `space.075` / `gap-075`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Item gap                    | `space.050` / `gap-050`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Chevron                     | `dimension.icon.small` / `size-icon-small`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Ellipsis                    | `size-250` container with a `dimension.icon.medium` / `size-icon-medium` icon; the list's own menu trigger uses `size-200` to keep the line 16px tall                                                                                                                                                                |
| Touch                       | Links and the ellipsis trigger take `touch-target`, a 24px hit area centred on the control wherever a pointer is coarse, without moving the line. With `overflow="wrap"`, links take `touch-target-block` instead: a band the link's own width, so a link that wraps never takes a tap meant for the words beside it |
| Focus                       | `radius.xsmall` / `rounded-xsmall`, `focus-visible:outline-focused`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Link transition             | `duration-fast`, `ease-standard`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

These defaults use the same semantic tokens in light and dark modes. Customize presentation through Ledger tokens while retaining the component anatomy and prop contract.

## Accessibility

- `Breadcrumb` creates a named navigation landmark containing an ordered list supplied by `BreadcrumbList`.
- Use distinct `aria-label` values for distinct breadcrumb landmarks on one page. The matrix does this without disabling the landmark uniqueness check.
- Parent anchors are reached by Tab and activated by Enter. Keep their real destinations so users can open them in another tab.
- Exactly one level is the current page: `BreadcrumbPage`, last. BreadcrumbLink drops an `aria-current` a router hands it; a router link through `render` needs exact matching (see [The current page and router links](#the-current-page-and-router-links)).
- `BreadcrumbPage` identifies the current page through `aria-current="page"`, with `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"`. It has no default tab stop.
- Separators and ellipsis have `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden="true"`. Do not put interactive content inside a separator.
- A folded level leaves the accessibility tree. The list's ellipsis is a menu button named "Show hidden levels" (the `showHiddenLevels` message, which a `LedgerProvider` can translate), and it keeps its place in the reading and tab order when the root folds and it leads the line; its items are links with the folded levels' real hrefs. Choosing one runs the folded link itself, so a router link keeps its client-side navigation; a modified click opens the href in a new tab.
- Ellipsis alone is not an accessible control. Its button or menu trigger needs a name, keyboard behavior, and appropriate state attributes.
- Custom render components must forward props and refs to preserve native attributes and keyboard behavior.

## Props

Each part accepts its native element's props, including DOM attributes, event handlers, `className`, `style`, and `ref`. `BreadcrumbLink` additionally accepts Base UI's `render` prop.

| Export                | Native props                                                       | Ref target                                                  |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Breadcrumb`          | `React.ComponentProps<"nav">`                                      | `HTMLElement` (`nav`)                                       |
| `BreadcrumbList`      | `BreadcrumbListProps`: `React.ComponentProps<"ol">` and `overflow` | `HTMLOListElement`                                          |
| `BreadcrumbItem`      | `React.ComponentProps<"li">`                                       | `HTMLLIElement`                                             |
| `BreadcrumbLink`      | `useRender.ComponentProps<"a">`                                    | Anchor by default; the composed element when using `render` |
| `BreadcrumbPage`      | `React.ComponentProps<"span">`                                     | `HTMLSpanElement`                                           |
| `BreadcrumbSeparator` | `React.ComponentProps<"li">`                                       | `HTMLLIElement`                                             |
| `BreadcrumbEllipsis`  | `React.ComponentProps<"span">`                                     | `HTMLSpanElement`                                           |

_Props: generated from `Breadcrumb`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

<!-- page: Components/Button (src/stories/components/Button.mdx) -->

# Button

Button starts an action. Use a short label that names what happens, such as “Save changes” or “Export report.”

Use it for something that happens on this page: saving, opening a dialog or a menu, changing state. Do not use it to go somewhere: navigation that looks like a button is a [LinkButton](?path=/docs/components-linkbutton--docs), a real anchor the reader can open in a new tab, and a link in text is a [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs). An icon-only action is an [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs); an on/off state is a [Toggle](?path=/docs/components-toggle--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.Matrix`._

Leading and trailing icons use a smaller inset on their own side; icon-only controls stay centered. Open popup triggers retain their pressed surface through `aria-expanded` while the popup is open. Toggle selection continues to use `aria-pressed`.

## Variants and sizes

| Variant | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `secondary` | Default raised action: Export, Edit, Open. |
| `primary` | The main action in a header, form or dialog. |
| `subtle` | Low emphasis actions in toolbars, rows and footers. |
| `danger` | Destructive actions, with confirmation when appropriate. |
| `link` | A text styled action, such as Show more. |

| Size | Height | Typical placement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `medium` | 32px | Default for forms, headers and footers. |
| `small` | 28px | Toolbars and rows. |
| `xsmall` | 24px | Dense inline actions. |

The `link` variant has no fixed height. `iconBefore` and `iconAfter` take an icon element; Button sizes it to 14px and keeps a 6px gap. `isSelected` applies the selected palette and `aria-pressed`.

_Example: story `Stories.Emphasis`._

## Loading and forms

Button defaults to `type="button"`. Set `type="submit"` for a form's submit action. Native form attributes, event handlers and refs reach the button element. `isFullWidth` fills its container.

`isLoading` replaces the leading icon with a decorative spinner and retains the label. It sets `aria-busy`, blocks activation and preserves focus while work is pending. An explicitly `disabled` button remains disabled and leaves the normal tab order. Base UI's `focusableWhenDisabled` is available when a disabled action needs to remain focusable.

_Example: story `Stories.Loading`._

## Disabled with a reason

Keep actions enabled where you can, and explain on use: a form's submit stays enabled and reports what is missing. When an action truly cannot run, say why with `disabledReason` instead of `disabled`. The button takes the disabled face but stays in the tab order with `aria-disabled`, so a keyboard reader reaches it; the reason is its accessible description and shows in a tooltip on hover, on keyboard focus and on a tap. Activation is blocked. Write the reason as what would make the action available: “Add content to this version before publishing it.”, not “Disabled.” A `title` on a disabled button never shows, because a disabled button takes no pointer events.

`disabledReason` disables the button by itself and keeps it focusable even when `disabled` is also set. An empty string is no reason. A Button with a reason owns its tooltip; do not put it inside another TooltipTrigger.

_Example: story `Stories.DisabledWithAReason`._

A reason that comes or goes while the button has focus leaves focus where it is. Publishing a version can make Publish unavailable at once: focus stays on it and its tooltip says why. A scan that finishes while the reader is on Download leaves them on an enabled Download.

_Example: story `Stories.ReasonChangesWhileFocused`._

## Composition

`render` accepts an element or a render function for an action control. Render elements merge native props, handlers, refs, classes and styles. Render functions receive the props and state and must apply those props to their result. Custom components must forward them to their DOM element. Button's root ref describes a native button; put a ref for another target on the render element itself.

Use `nativeButton={false}` when the rendered action is not a native button; it receives button semantics and Enter/Space activation. `className` and `style` also accept callbacks with Base UI's `{ disabled }` state, including while loading.

Navigation is a [LinkButton](?path=/docs/components-linkbutton--docs): an anchor, or the application's router Link through `render`, with Button's variants, sizes, icon slots and insets. Do not render a link through Button's `render`: [Base UI Button enforces button semantics](https://base-ui.com/react/components/button#rendering-links-as-buttons), logs an error for an anchor, and `nativeButton={false}` would give the link `role="button"`.

```tsx
<LinkButton variant="primary" render={<Link to="/requirements" />}>
  View requirements
</LinkButton>
```

`buttonVariants` is the lower-level recipe LinkButton uses. It accepts `variant`, `size`, `isSelected`, `isFullWidth` and `className`, and supplies classes without adding ARIA, icon insets or disabled behavior; reach for it only where a part cannot take LinkButton. Existing `Button asChild` and `IconButton asChild` usages move to LinkButton or LinkIconButton for navigation, or to `render` for an action control.

_Example: story `Stories.AsLink`._

## Accessibility

- Tab reaches an enabled button. Enter and Space activate it; the focus outline appears on keyboard focus.
- Disabled buttons are skipped by Tab by default. For an action that cannot run, `disabledReason` keeps it focusable with `aria-disabled` and gives it the reason as its description; for form validation, keep the submit action available so the form can report errors.
- Loading blocks click, Enter and Space activation, including handlers on the rendered action. It keeps the accessible name stable.
- Use [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs) for an icon only action with a required accessible label, and [Toggle](?path=/docs/components-toggle--docs) for an on/off control.
- `variant="link"` is as tall as its text. Where any pointer is coarse it takes an invisible hit area of at least 24px, centred on it, so nothing around it moves.

_Example: story `Stories.OnTouch`._

_Props: generated from `Button`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

# ButtonGroup

Join related actions, split buttons or controls. Each child keeps its own behavior and accessible name.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Export">
  <Button>Export</Button>
  <ButtonGroupSeparator isDecorative />
  <Button>Print</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

ButtonGroup joins the outer corners of children with `data-slot` attributes. ButtonGroupText adds a label, value or prefix. ButtonGroupSeparator adds a visible rule. Nested groups may separate related sets of actions.

_Example: story `Stories.Composition`._

## Variants and states

`orientation` accepts `horizontal` (default) or `vertical`. Horizontal joins use logical edges in RTL. Child controls choose their size, disabled state and loading behavior. The separator's orientation describes its own line; use a horizontal separator between vertically stacked controls.

_Example: story `Stories.Orientations`._

## Accessibility

Name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Each enabled control remains in the normal tab order. A group does not add arrow-key navigation or selection behavior. Use ToggleGroup for a selection among options. Decorative separators may use `isDecorative`.

ButtonGroupText supports Base UI `render`, including a native label with `htmlFor`. Rendered elements must accept merged attributes, events and refs.

## Props

_Props: generated from `ButtonGroup`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `ButtonGroupText`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `ButtonGroupSeparator`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

The root forwards native div attributes and refs. Text uses Base UI useRender/mergeProps; Separator uses the existing Base UI Separator. `buttonGroupVariants` exports the same orientation classes for composition.

### Migration

Rename `label` to `aria-label`. Compose text and separators with the flat exports. The root is now a div and accepts native props, refs and orientation.

# Calendar

A month to pick a day, several days or a range from, following [shadcn’s Calendar](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/calendar) on React DayPicker, with Ledger tokens and the LedgerProvider's locale.

Use it inside a picker. A day in a form is a [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs), a range a [DateRangePicker](?path=/docs/components-daterangepicker--docs); an inline month takes the room of six fields for one answer. Use Calendar on its own where the month is the content, such as a schedule panel.

```tsx
const [date, setDate] = useState<Date>();
<Calendar mode="single" selected={date} onSelect={setDate} />;
```

Calendar takes DayPicker's own props: `mode` (single, multiple or range), `selected` and `onSelect`, disabled matchers, `startMonth` and `endMonth`, `numberOfMonths`, `captionLayout="dropdown"`, `showWeekNumber`. Custom `components`, `formatters`, `labels` and `classNames` merge with Calendar's defaults; customize a day with the exported CalendarDayButton so DayPicker's focus, selection and events stay intact. `buttonVariant` sets the navigation buttons. Days are 32px cells, above the 24px touch minimum.

_Example: story `Stories.Single`._

## Days and zones

Calendar's Dates stand for calendar days: the local year, month and day, never an instant. They are labelled with `formatCalendarDate`, so a provider's `timeZone` never moves a day. Today is the reader's own day.

## Locale

Under a LedgerProvider the month speaks its locale: `lang` on the root, the first day of the week (Monday in de-DE, Saturday in ar-EG, Sunday in en-US), the caption, weekday names and their spoken names, the day digits, the year dropdown and week numbers. A caller's own date-fns `locale`, `weekStartsOn`, `lang`, `labels` and `formatters` win. Two calendars on one page name their navigation apart through `labels.labelNav`, or the navigation landmark repeats.

_Example: story `Stories.Localized`._

## Ranges

With `mode="range"` the first and last days are the blue budget and the days between take the selected tint; `numberOfMonths={2}` spans a range across months. Below the `sm` window the months always stack; above it the calendar's own space decides, so a range in a 320px panel stacks on a wide screen. The range's ends say which end they are ("Start of range", "End of range") and a completed range is announced once, politely: "September 7, 2026 to October 9, 2026 selected", or "September 7, 2026 selected" for a one-day range.

_Example: story `Stories.CalendarRange`._
_Example: story `Stories.InANarrowPanel`._
_Example: story `Stories.RangeInAPopover`._

## Disabled days

A disabled matcher makes a day unchoosable and skips it in the keyboard order. `describeDay(date, modifiers)` adds the reason to its name ("Weekends are closed."), after the kit's date, today, selected and range words. Keep the rule in the field's hint too; DatePicker and DateRangePicker do both from `min`, `max` and `isDateUnavailable`.

_Example: story `Stories.DisabledDayReasons`._
_Example: story `Stories.DropdownsAndWeekNumbers`._

## Navigation

`navLayout="around"` places Previous beside the first month's caption and Next beside the last, in either direction. The default and `"after"` share one navigation bar; `"after"` puts it later in the keyboard order.

_Example: story `Stories.NavigationLayouts`._

## Accessibility

- DayPicker owns the grid keyboard: arrows by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month, Shift with them by year, Home and End by week, one tab stop. The day button takes focus when DayPicker marks it focused.
- Every day's name is the full date in the locale, with today, selected or its range end, and any reason from `describeDay`.
- Selection is shown by fill and survives forced colours: the selected day and the range keep their own colours there.
- Give a standalone Calendar a visible heading or an accessible name.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Calendar`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CalendarDayButton`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

## Related

[DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs) · [DateRangePicker](?path=/docs/components-daterangepicker--docs) · [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs) · [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs)
