# Card

A raised container for a table, chart, form or set of facts. Compose its header, content and footer as needed.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>
      <h2>Evidence</h2>
    </CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Three linked artifacts</CardDescription>
    <CardAction>
      <Button size="small">Add evidence</Button>
    </CardAction>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>Assessment details</CardContent>
  <CardFooter className="border-t">
    <Button>Save</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>
```

CardHeader arranges the title, description and optional action. The action sits at the end of the title's row while the header has 16rem inside its inset, that is while the card is about 18rem wide or more (about 17.5rem at `size="sm"`), as a full-width card on a 340px phone is. In a narrower card, such as one in a rail or a full-width card on a 320px phone, it takes its own row after the description, at the end, so the title keeps the full width. CardContent supplies the horizontal inset. CardFooter holds actions or secondary content. The root supplies vertical padding and spacing between parts, and records its raised surface so sticky table headers remain opaque.

Headers and footers are undivided by default. Add `className="border-b"` to CardHeader or `className="border-t"` to CardFooter when a rule separates distinct work areas; the part adds padding beside that rule. Form titles usually need spacing only, while a footer with submission actions can earn a divider.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Variants and states

The default size uses Ledger's standard inset; `size="sm"` reduces the inset and gaps. Tables and charts that own their spacing can sit directly inside Card. For a table flush against a divided header and the bottom edge, use `className="gap-0 pb-0"` on Card and `className="border-b"` on CardHeader. Loading, empty and error behavior belongs to the content.

_Example: story `Stories.Sizes`._
_Example: story `Stories.EdgeToEdge`._
_Example: story `Stories.InARail`._

## Accessibility

All parts are native divs. CardTitle does not choose a heading level: compose an h2 or h3 when the card should appear in the document outline. Existing callers retain their h2 headings. Name a region with `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby` when a landmark is useful. Links and buttons inside the card keep their own semantics and focus.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Card`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardHeader`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardTitle`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardDescription`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardAction`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardContent`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardFooter`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Every part accepts native div props and refs. Root `style` overrides merge with the raised-surface default.

### Migration

Replace `Card.Header title/description/action` with CardHeader containing CardTitle, CardDescription and CardAction. Replace `Card.Body` with CardContent. Add a heading inside CardTitle to preserve the original outline. Card now lives in the components layer; application imports still come from the package root.

## Related

[Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs), [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs), [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs), [Related](?path=/docs/patterns-related--docs).

Sources: [shadcn Card](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/card), [Base UI catalog implementation](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/card.tsx).

<!-- page: Components/Checkbox (src/stories/components/Checkbox.mdx) -->

# Checkbox

An independent boolean choice, using the shadcn Base UI root and indicator. The 16px control supplies the check or mixed-state dash; the label and hint come from a horizontal [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs), which ties them to the box with no ids.

```tsx
<Field orientation="horizontal">
  <Checkbox name="pii" value="yes" defaultChecked />
  <FieldContent>
    <FieldLabel>Handles PII</FieldLabel>
    <FieldDescription>The package includes records about a person.</FieldDescription>
  </FieldContent>
</Field>
```

Use [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs) for one selected answer from visible choices, or [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs) for an on/off setting. The caller decides when to save a change.

_Example: story `Stories.CheckboxMatrix`._

## Selection and mixed state

Use boolean `checked` with `onCheckedChange(checked, details)`, or `defaultChecked` for local state. `details.cancel()` rejects a change. `disabled` prevents interaction and removes the control from the tab order; `readOnly` keeps it focusable without allowing changes.

Mixed state uses a separate boolean `indeterminate` prop. [Table.Selection](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) derives it from the rows it selects. For a list of choices with select-all, use a [CheckboxGroup](?path=/docs/components-checkboxgroup--docs): it owns the ticked values and its CheckboxGroupSelectAll derives the checked and mixed states.

_Example: story `Stories.Parent`._

## Labels, Field and forms

In a Field the FieldLabel names the box and toggles it when clicked, the FieldDescription and FieldError describe it, and the Field's `invalid`, `required` and `disabled` reach it; nothing needs an id. Outside a Field, a wrapping label or a sibling label with `htmlFor` and the checkbox's `id` names it, and `aria-describedby` links supporting text. Use `aria-label` only for a box with no visible label. Several related boxes belong in a [CheckboxGroup](?path=/docs/components-checkboxgroup--docs); requiring the group does not require every box. Native `required` on the box is a browser and Base UI constraint; the Field's `required` only announces and marks.

The box's boundary is `color.border.bold`, 3:1 against every surface, so an unticked box can be found (WCAG 1.4.11); text fields keep their lighter `color.border.input`, which increased contrast raises. Invalid is the danger border. The keyboard focus outline stays the focus colour on an invalid box, so focus is visible while the reader moves through a list of errors. A FieldSet's `disabled` disables the boxes inside it, which a native `<fieldset disabled>` alone does not.

_Example: story `Stories.InvalidAndFocused`._

`name`, `value` and `form` control native submission. A checked checkbox submits its value (or `on` when omitted); an unchecked checkbox is omitted unless `uncheckedValue` is supplied. Native form reset is caller-owned in Base UI 1.7: restore controlled `checked` state in `onReset`.

_Example: story `Stories.InField`._

## Native props and keyboard

The default root is a span with `role="checkbox"`, plus a hidden input. `ref` targets the visible control; `inputRef` and `id` target the input. For a native button root, use `nativeButton` with `render={<button />}`; `id` then belongs to that button. The render element's props, classes, styles, handlers and refs are merged. `className` and `style` accept Base UI state callbacks.

Each enabled checkbox is a Tab stop. Space toggles it. Enter does not toggle it; inside a form it activates the default submitter. Mixed state is announced as `aria-checked="mixed"` and drawn with a dash.

## Migration

Move label children into an external label and replace `description` with supporting content linked by `aria-describedby` or FieldDescription. Replace `checked="indeterminate"` with `checked={false} indeterminate`; callbacks now receive a boolean and cancellable event details. Use `render` for composition. The root follows Base UI's default span and input structure.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Checkbox`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

<!-- page: Components/CheckboxGroup (src/stories/components/CheckboxGroup.mdx) -->

# CheckboxGroup

Several choices that can each be true, under one legend. It is Base UI's CheckboxGroup rendered as a FieldSet: it owns the ticked values, names the group by its FieldLegend, and with `allValues` drives a select-all box.

```tsx
<CheckboxGroup defaultValue={["ac"]} allValues={["ac", "au", "cm"]}>
  <FieldLegend variant="label">Control families</FieldLegend>
  <CheckboxGroupSelectAll>Every family</CheckboxGroupSelectAll>
  <Field orientation="horizontal">
    <Checkbox value="ac" name="families" />
    <FieldLabel>AC · Access control</FieldLabel>
  </Field>
  {/* … one horizontal Field per family */}
</CheckboxGroup>
```

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## When to use it

- **Several independent answers** to one question: the channels to notify, the families to include, the parameters that apply.
- **A list with select-all**, where the reader ticks most or all of the items.

Use [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs) when only one answer can be true, [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs) on its own for a single yes or no, a [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs) for a setting that takes effect at once, and the selection column of a [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) or a [PickerSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-pickersheet--docs) for choosing records from a long list.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Values and select-all

The group owns the ticked values as an array of the checkboxes' `value`s: `defaultValue` for local state, or `value` and `onValueChange(value, details)` when the form holds it; `details.cancel()` rejects a change. Each Checkbox takes a `value`, and a `name` for native submission, so `FormData.getAll(name)` returns the ticked values.

`CheckboxGroupSelectAll` needs `allValues`, the value of every checkbox in the group. It is ticked when all are, mixed (`aria-checked="mixed"`, drawn with a dash) when some are, and a press ticks them all or clears them. Its label defaults to the locale's "Select all"; pass children to name what it selects. A disabled checkbox keeps its state when select-all changes the rest.

_Example: story `Stories.DefaultSelectAll`._

## In a form

A CheckboxGroup inside a Field takes the Field's hint and error and its `invalid` state, which marks every box; a required Field shows the asterisk on the legend and requires the group, not each box. No checkbox announces that requirement and a group cannot, so the legend adds the locale's "(required)" for assistive technology, hidden on screen. The form checks "at least one" itself. Put the FieldDescription and FieldError inside the group, after the legend.

_Example: story `Stories.InField`._

`disabled` reaches every box, the select-all box included, and so does the `disabled` of a FieldSet or a Field around the group.

_Example: story `Stories.Disabled`._

## Accessibility

- The group is a `fieldset`, named by its FieldLegend. Start the children with the legend. In a required Field the name ends in "(required)".
- Each box is its own Tab stop; Space ticks it. Give each one its own label: a horizontal Field with a FieldLabel needs no ids.
- A hint or an error describes the group and each box in it.

## Props

_Props: generated from `CheckboxGroup`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CheckboxGroupSelectAll`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

[Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs) · [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) · [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) · [Base UI Checkbox Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/checkbox-group)

<!-- page: Components/CodeBlock (src/stories/components/CodeBlock.mdx) -->

# CodeBlock

Source shown as source: a configuration excerpt, a serialised record, a log, a command the reader will paste. One row per line in the code face, a line-number gutter that stays put when the block scrolls sideways, a cap on the height so a long document scrolls inside the block and not the page, and a Copy when the reader will take the text away. The caller owns highlighting and passes rendered lines.

It is not a field: a value the reader edits is a [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs). It is not prose: a paragraph is [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs). A single identifier in a sentence is an [Id](?path=/docs/components-id--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.Code`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame  | A box in `elevation.surface.sunken` with a 1px `color.border` and `radius.medium`. It scrolls both ways inside itself; it is a tab stop so the keyboard can scroll it.        |
| Gutter | The line numbers, `color.text.subtlest`, tabular, right-aligned, on a column that sticks to the start edge when the lines scroll sideways, with a 1px rule at its end.        |
| Line   | One row per entry of `lines`, `space.150` from the gutter, in `font.code`. A string, or the caller's spans.                                                                  |
| Copy   | With `copy`, the kit's [CopyButton](?path=/docs/components-copybutton--docs), icon-only and subtle, at the top end on the block's own surface. The frame is at least as tall as it, and the lines keep room at their end to scroll out from under it. |

## Variants

One. What changes is what the lines are: a string per line, or nodes the caller has coloured, because a kit tokenizer for every format the product meets is not the kit's job. The export page splits its JSON and colours the keys; a log is strings.

_Example: story `Stories.Highlighted`._

Not built, and why: a highlighted line (the one a validation error points at, the changed lines of a revision), because no screen asks for it yet; a language picker or a tokenizer. Two versions of a text compared line by line are a [Diff](?path=/docs/components-diff--docs).

## Sizes

One face, `font.code`, at the body size. The block is as wide as its container and as tall as its lines up to `maxHeight`, 560px by default; a short excerpt never scrolls. The gutter is as wide as the last line number needs, three digits at least.

## States

| State     | Look                                                                                                         |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Rest      | The lines, the gutter, the frame.                                                                            |
| Focus     | The kit's focus outline on the frame, on keyboard focus, so a keyboard reader can scroll it.                 |
| Scrolled  | Sideways, the gutter stays and the lines pass under it. Down, the gutter goes with the lines.                |
| Copied    | The Copy's icon is a check in `color.icon.success` and its tooltip and a polite status say Copied, for a moment; its name stays Copy. |
| Not copied | When the browser refuses the write, the icon is an alert in `color.icon.danger` and the tooltip and status say Could not copy. |

_Example: story `Stories.CodeBlockMatrix`._

_Example: story `Stories.OneLineCommand`._

## Modifiers

- **`start`**: the number of the first line, for an excerpt of a longer file.
- **`maxHeight`**: pixels before the block scrolls inside itself.
- **`wrap`**: long lines fold at the block's edge. Off by default so code keeps its columns; on for a log or a value with no columns to keep.
- **`copy`**: the text a Copy puts on the clipboard, usually the lines joined. Unsaid, there is no button.
- **`label`**: the block's accessible name, the file or the format. "Code" by default; say which.

_Example: story `Stories.Wrapped`._

_Example: story `Stories.Capped`._

## Content

- **Lines are the source as it is,** indentation included. Do not trim, reflow or re-indent for the page.
- **`label` names the thing:** "control.json", "Ingest log", "Router configuration". Not "Code".
- **`start` is the real line number** when the block is an excerpt, so a reader can find the line in the file.
- **A Copy where the reader will paste:** a command, a configuration, a document. Not on a log they read.
- **Highlighting colours the grammar, in the kit's text colours:** keys in `color.text.brand`, strings subtle, comments subtlest. Never a rainbow.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                   |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame   | `elevation.surface.sunken` · 1px `color.border` · `radius.medium` · `space.050` block inside              |
| Gutter  | `font.code` · `color.text.subtlest` · tabular · `space.100` inline · 1px `color.border` at its end        |
| Line    | `font.code` · `color.text` · `space.150` from the gutter                                                  |
| Copy    | CopyButton, icon-only, `subtle` `small`, at `space.050` from the top and the end on `elevation.surface.sunken` · the frame at least `dimension.control.large` tall · `space.500` at the lines' end · `color.icon.success` when copied |
| Focus   | The kit's focus outline, `color.border.focused`                                                           |

## Accessibility

- **The frame is a group named by `label`** and a tab stop, so a keyboard reader can reach a block that scrolls and move it with the arrows. A block with a bare "Code" name is a block the screen reader cannot tell from the next one.
- **Line numbers are not selectable,** so a copied selection is the code alone.
- **The Copy is a CopyButton:** named Copy, with the kit's tooltip, and a status region says Copied, or Could not copy when the browser refuses.
- **The gutter is hidden from assistive technology,** so browse mode reads the code, not a line number before every line.
- **Contrast:** the gutter's `color.text.subtlest` passes on the sunken surface in both modes; the caller's highlight colours are the kit's text tokens, which do too.
- **The a11y gate** checks the name, the tab stop and the contrast in the matrix.

## Props

_Props: generated from `CodeBlock`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

- [Id](?path=/docs/components-id--docs): one identifier in running text.
- [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs): prose.
- [CopyButton](?path=/docs/components-copybutton--docs): the Copy, on its own beside an identifier or a command.
- [ScrollArea](?path=/docs/components-scrollarea--docs): a region that scrolls with the kit's bar; the CodeBlock uses the platform's, so the gutter can stick.

<!-- page: Components/Collapsible (src/stories/components/Collapsible.mdx) -->

# Collapsible

One independent disclosure: content the reader opens when they need it. Based on [shadcn’s Base UI source](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/collapsible) and [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/collapsible). Ledger retains its tokens and application layouts.

## Anatomy

`Collapsible` holds the state, `CollapsibleContent` the content that folds, and one of two triggers opens it:

- **`CollapsibleHeader`**, the disclosure header: the trigger inside a heading, the title at the start and a chevron at the end that turns while the content is open, the row tint under the pointer and the focus ring on the keyboard. Use it whenever the disclosure has a title: a rail's group, a block of details, a folded list.
- **`CollapsibleTrigger`**, the bare trigger with no heading and no chevron, for a trigger that is something else already (a Button through `render`, a row's own control).

```tsx
<Collapsible>
  <CollapsibleHeader>Provenance</CollapsibleHeader>
  <CollapsibleContent>…</CollapsibleContent>
</Collapsible>
```

_Example: story `Stories.Header`._

Counts and marks are ordinary children of the header: `<CollapsibleHeader>Derivation <Count value={3} /></CollapsibleHeader>`; they are part of the button's name. An action for the block goes after the header in a flex row, where the header grows; never inside it, because a button cannot hold another.

## Heading level

The header's heading takes the contextual level from the nearest [HeadingLevelProvider](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs), a titled Section or a panel's body, and is an h3 when nothing sets one, as Accordion's is. Wrap it in a HeadingLevelProvider for another level: `level={2}` for a page's rail, whose groups sit under the h1. The content under the header is not raised a level; a heading inside it goes one below through a HeadingLevelProvider.

_Example: story `Stories.HeaderLevels`._

## When to use it

- **CollapsibleHeader** for a titled block the reader may not need: provenance, counts, derivation, reference notes. On a page, a collapsible [Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs) (`collapsible`) is the same header with the Section's count, description and action; in a rail of facts, [Inspector.Group](?path=/docs/patterns-inspector--docs).
- **Not** a subtle Button with a chevron as the trigger: it sits outside the outline and its chevron does not turn. **Not** a native `<details>`: its marker and motion are the browser's.
- **Not** for a coordinated set where opening one closes another: that is an [Accordion](?path=/docs/components-accordion--docs). **Not** for a row that discloses more of itself: Item's `isCollapsible` and Table's disclosure column own their chevrons.

## Variants

_Example: story `Stories.RetainedState`._

_Example: story `Stories.IndependentAndDisabled`._

_Example: story `Stories.SearchableContent`._

## Accessibility

Base UI owns expanded state, trigger/panel association, disabled behavior and keyboard activation: Tab reaches the trigger, Enter and Space toggle it, and focus stays on it. CollapsibleHeader's trigger is a button inside a heading, so the block is in the heading outline and its state is announced ("Provenance, collapsed, button"); the chevron is decoration, turned by the same state rather than by colour. Under reduced motion the chevron turns without moving and the content opens without the fold. Retained closed panels stay hidden and unfocusable. `hiddenUntilFound` lets supported browser find-in-page reveal closed content. Nested disclosures keep independent state.

## Props

The parts expose native Base UI props, refs, `render`, state classes and styles, and a cancellable `onOpenChange`. Content uses the measured `--collapsible-panel-height` for Ledger motion and respects reduced motion. It clips only while it folds: settled open, its overflow is visible, so the focus ring of a link or a button at its edge shows whole. CollapsibleHeader passes its props, its ref and `render` to the trigger; its children are the title.

_Props: generated from `Collapsible`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CollapsibleHeader`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CollapsibleTrigger`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CollapsibleContent`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### State selectors

The Root carries `data-open` and `data-closed`; the trigger carries `data-panel-open` while its content is open. Style a trigger's own chevron from the trigger (`group-data-panel-open/…`), not from `data-open`, which the trigger never has, and never from Radix's `data-state`.

### Migration and API

- Replace Collapsible.Trigger/Content with the flat exports. Replace asChild with render and forceMount with keepMounted.
- Use data-open/data-closed on the Root and data-panel-open on the trigger instead of Radix data-state selectors. Item, Section, Stepper, Inspector and DataTable metrics use the same Base UI disclosure behavior.
- A Details block built from a subtle Button and a ChevronDown moves to CollapsibleHeader, or to a collapsible Section on a page.
- The unused LegacyAccordion/LegacyCollapsible adapters are removed; use the current flat Accordion and Collapsible parts.

- [Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs)
- [Inspector](?path=/docs/patterns-inspector--docs)
- [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs)

# Combobox

Search and select predefined values using shadcn's Base UI Combobox composition. Root owns selection, filtering, popup state and form serialization. ComboboxInput composes the shared InputGroup and its trigger/clear controls.

## Anatomy

```tsx
const frameworks = ["React", "Vue", "Svelte"];

<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Framework</FieldLabel>
  <Combobox items={frameworks}>
    <ComboboxInput placeholder="Choose a framework" showClear />
    <ComboboxContent>
      <ComboboxEmpty>No frameworks found.</ComboboxEmpty>
      <ComboboxList>
        {(item: string) => (
          <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
            {item}
          </ComboboxItem>
        )}
      </ComboboxList>
    </ComboboxContent>
  </Combobox>
</Field>;
```

Root renders no DOM wrapper. Content includes Portal, Positioner and Popup. List renders filtered items inside a [Scroller](?path=/docs/components-scroller--docs), so long results show hover arrows at each overflowed edge. Group, Label, Collection and Separator compose categorized results.

## Variants and states

_Example: story `Stories.Searchable`._
_Example: story `Stories.Groups`._

For multiple selection, use an array value with ComboboxChips, ComboboxValue, ComboboxChip and ComboboxChipsInput. Chips include removal controls unless `showRemove={false}`. Use `useComboboxAnchor()` to anchor the popup to the whole chips container.

_Example: story `Stories.Multiple`._

For remote results, own loading/query state and pass `filter={null}` when the server filters. ComboboxStatus presents loading feedback outside the list of options. Disabled options cannot be selected; read-only selection stays submitted without allowing changes.

_Example: story `Stories.AsyncResults`._

## Accessibility

Inside a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) the FieldLabel names the input and the list, the hint and error describe the input, and the Field's `invalid`, `required` and `disabled` reach it, with no ids. Outside one, connect a label to ComboboxInput with `htmlFor`/`id` and put description ids, invalid state and required announcements on the input. Root’s `required` enables native constraint validation separately.

_Example: story `Stories.BoundInField`._

Typing filters, arrows highlight, Enter selects, and Escape closes the popup before the surrounding dialog. Base UI controls focus and nested popup behavior.

_Example: story `Stories.InDialog`._

## Props

`ComboboxProps<Value, Multiple>` is the generic Base UI root contract, with Ledger locale/direction defaults. Root's `value` is one value/null or an array; `onValueChange(value, details)` supports cancellation. Use `name`, `form`, `inputRef`, serialization and equality callbacks on Root. The installed Base UI version is 1.7; reset controlled selections in the owning form's `onReset`.

ComboboxInput forwards native input refs, events, render composition, classes and styles; Ledger retains small/medium sizing. `showTrigger` defaults true and `showClear` defaults false. Its children follow the control addons. Content forwards popup props plus positioning, `portalContainer` and `keepMounted`; the latter two preserve existing advanced integrations. Clear, ChipRemove and Status are additional flat native parts.

Replace `Combobox options/onChange` and `Combobox.Root` with the single root API. Move placeholder, ref, blur and input ARIA to ComboboxInput. Replace the old separate InputGroup/Trigger composition with ComboboxInput, and use ComboboxChipsInput inside chips. Layout owns widths. NativeSelect has been removed; use Select for choices that do not need search.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeForms`._

## Related

[Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs) · [InputGroup](?path=/docs/components-inputgroup--docs) · [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) · [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) · [shadcn Combobox](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/combobox) · [Base UI Combobox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox)

# Command

Based on [shadcn’s Base UI source](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/command) and [cmdk](https://cmdk.paco.me). Ledger retains its tokens and application layouts.

## Anatomy

Keyboard-filtered actions using cmdk, as in shadcn’s Base UI implementation. CommandDialog uses the shared Base UI Dialog. Compose Command, CommandInput, CommandList, CommandGroup, CommandItem, CommandEmpty, CommandSeparator and CommandShortcut.

## Variants

_Example: story `Stories.Filtering`._

_Example: story `Stories.Palette`._

CommandDialog keeps its 80px top inset and limits its height to the space below it. On short screens the command list scrolls while the search and footer remain visible.

_Example: story `Stories.ShortViewport`._

_Example: story `Stories.Loading`._

## Accessibility

Give Command a descriptive `label` (cmdk uses it to name the search input), and give CommandDialog a title. cmdk handles filtering, disabled choices, option navigation and selection. Base UI Dialog handles focus, modality and dismissal. CommandSeparator is presentational within the listbox. Put CommandLoading alongside CommandList, with aria-busy on the list while fetching. Item onSelect owns the action and any palette closing. When showCloseButton is false, compose a DialogClose so touch and screen-reader users have a dismissal control; the palette and record picker make their Escape footer hint a close button.

## Props

Command parts forward their native cmdk props and refs. CommandDialog accepts the native generic Dialog root contract plus title, description, className, style, showCloseButton and finalFocus. CommandLoading, CommandFooter and CommandCount retain their existing loading and result-count roles.

### Migration and API

- Replace Command.Input/List/Group/Item/etc. with flat exports. Put trailing content in children, using CommandShortcut for key hints.
- Replace Command.Dialog with CommandDialog. Compose an explicit Command inside it; command filtering/value props belong on Command.
- Replace onClose with onOpenChange and label with title on the dialog. Use style or className for palette width; finalFocus replaces returnFocusRef.
- Command continues to use cmdk; its modal shell no longer imports Radix Dialog directly.

# CopyButton

Puts a value on the clipboard: an identifier the reader will paste into a ticket, a command, a link, a configuration. It is a [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs), or with `label` an [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs), that copies `text` and says whether it worked. [CodeBlock](?path=/docs/components-codeblock--docs) uses it for its Copy.

Use it where the reader takes a value away. Do not use it for a value they only read, and do not use it to share a record: a link to the record is a [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs) the reader can copy with the browser.

_Example: story `Stories.Labelled`._

## Two forms

| Form       | How                                     | Where                                                                   |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Labelled   | Children, “Copy” (the `copy` message) by default | Beside a command or a block, where there is room for a word.            |
| Icon-only  | `label`, such as “Copy ID”              | Beside an identifier in a line, a row or a details rail.                |

The two are one prop apart and exclusive: with `label` there are no children. `variant` is `secondary` by default, or `subtle` beside an identifier or inside a block; `primary` is available and rarely right. `size` is `medium` for the labelled form and `small` (28px) for the icon-only one by default.

_Example: story `Stories.IdCopy`._

## What the reader sees

- **Copied.** The icon becomes a check, and “Copied” shows in a tooltip for two seconds, which opens by itself, so a touch reader sees it too. A polite status message says “Copied” to a screen reader.
- **Could not copy.** When the browser refuses the write (no permission, an insecure page, no clipboard), the icon becomes an alert, the tooltip and the status say “Could not copy” for four seconds, and `onCopyError` receives the error. A reader never pastes stale contents thinking they copied.
- **Stable.** The button keeps its name and its width through both. Escape or a tap elsewhere closes the tooltip early.
- **Said again.** A second copy while the first result still shows is a new status message, so a screen reader hears it too.

`onCopied` receives the text once the clipboard holds it; announce anything further there. `onClick` runs first, and calling `preventDefault()` in it skips the copy. The messages are `copy`, `copied` and `copyFailed`, which a `LedgerProvider` can translate.

_Example: story `Stories.CopyFails`._

## Accessibility

- The icon-only form is named by `label`, which is also its tooltip. Name what is copied (“Copy ID”, “Copy record id”) so several copy buttons on one screen can be told apart.
- The result is a status message (WCAG 4.1.3), polite, in a region that is always present; the tooltip and the icon are the visible half. The name never changes, so a voice command keeps working.
- Focus stays on the button through the copy.
- The icon change is a shape, check or alert, not only a colour.

## Props

_Props: generated from `CopyButton`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

# Count

A number in a pill: unread items, rows in a group, results behind a filter, findings on a control. It sits after the name of what it counts and is named by it. Anything above `max`, 99 by default, renders as `99+`. Not the notification circle on a corner.

_Example: story `Stories.CountMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                             |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Pill   | 20px tall, at least 20px wide, round, `space.075` at each end: the neutral fill or one of four others. |
| Number | `font.body.small` medium, tabular, centred. Never a word.                                              |

## Variants

| Appearance  | Use                                                                                           |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`   | Rows in a group, results behind a filter, items in a section. The neutral fill.               |
| `primary`   | The one count on the screen that must be seen: unread, new since you last looked. Brand fill. |
| `important` | What needs attention now: overdue, blocked. Danger fill.                                      |
| `added`     | Rows a change adds. Success fill, subtle.                                                     |
| `removed`   | Rows a change removes. Danger fill, subtle.                                                   |

Not built, and why: a corner placement on an avatar or an icon (a notification circle); the shell's navigation has no unread counts yet, and when it does the Count will sit after the item's label, not on its icon. No count in a tone's text colour without a fill; the number alone is a Stat.

## Sizes

One size, 20px, the height of a small Badge, so the two sit on one line. The width grows with the digits and stops at three and a plus.

## States

A Count has one state. A count of zero is usually not shown: a section with nothing in it says so in words, and the consumers that take a `count` hide it at zero.

_Example: story `Stories.InContext`._

## Modifiers

- **`value`** as a number, or a string when the text is not a number the pill should cap ("12 of 40" is not a Count).
- **`max`** for the ceiling: 99 by default; 999 or 9999 on a tab that counts rows.
- **`appearance`** as in Variants; `default` when unsaid.

## Content

- **A number.** Digits only; the word before it says what they count.
- **Named by its label.** "Findings 3", "Evidence 7": the Count follows the label at `space.100`.
- **Capped, not exact.** Past the ceiling the reader needs the order of magnitude; the exact number is a Stat.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                                        |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pill      | `dimension.control.xsmall` 20px tall and at least as wide · `radius.full` · `space.075` ends |
| Number    | `font.body.small` medium · tabular                                                           |
| default   | `color.background.neutral` · `color.text.subtle`                                             |
| primary   | `color.background.brand.bold` · `color.text.inverse`                                         |
| important | `color.background.danger.bold` · `color.text.inverse`                                        |
| added     | `color.background.success` · `color.text.success`                                            |
| removed   | `color.background.danger` · `color.text.danger`                                              |

## Accessibility

- **It is text**, read in the flow after its label: "Findings, 3". The label names it; a Count on its own says only a number.
- **`99+` is read as "99 plus"**, which is the meaning.
- **The appearance is not the only signal.** An important count sits beside a label that says why; the red ranks it.
- **Nothing to focus.** A Count inside a Tab or a Collapsible is part of that control's name.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Count`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Count takes a span's native props and a ref, and names itself last with `data-slot="count"` and its `data-appearance`.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

# DatePicker

One calendar day in a form, held and reported as an ISO day (`"2026-09-18"`, the contract of `input type="date"`) and shown in the LedgerProvider's locale ("Sep 18, 2026"). A day has no time and no zone, so it never shifts between readers. It is Ledger's composition of [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs) and [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-calendar--docs), with Today and Clear under the month.

Use it for a day: a due date, a planned completion, a milestone. For a moment in time (collected at, due at 5 PM) use [DateTimeField](?path=/docs/components-datetimefield--docs); for a time of day alone, [TimeField](?path=/docs/components-timefield--docs); for a range, [DateRangePicker](?path=/docs/components-daterangepicker--docs). An approximate or remembered date ("March 2024") is an [Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs) with the format in its hint.

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Scheduled completion</FieldLabel>
  <DatePicker name="due" value={due} onValueChange={setDue} />
  <FieldDescription>When the milestone is due.</FieldDescription>
</Field>
```

_Example: story `Stories.Open`._

## Picking or typing

`entry` chooses how the reader gives the day.

| `entry`          | What the reader sees                            | For                                                            |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pick` (default) | A button that reads the day and opens the month | A day the reader looks for: the next review, a due date        |
| `type`           | A text field with a button that opens the month | A day the reader already knows: a signed date, a date of birth |

A typed day is read in the provider's locale when the reader presses Tab or Enter, never while typing: "Sep 18, 2026", "9/18/2026" (en-US order), "18.9.2026" (de-DE), "2026-09-18" and "9/18" (this year) all read, in the locale's digits or Latin ones. The field then shows the day in the locale's words. Text that is not a day, or a day outside `min`, `max` or `isDateUnavailable`, stays as the reader typed it, the field reports `""` and says what fixes it under itself: "Enter a date such as Sep 25, 2026.", "Enter Sep 1, 2026 or later." Escape puts back the last day. Alt+Down opens the month from the text.

The message is a FieldError inside the Field, so it describes the input and marks the Field invalid. `onEntryError` receives it (and `null` once the entry reads), for a form library that should show it in place of its own "Required.".

_Example: story `Stories.TypedEntry`._
_Example: story `Stories.TypedInGerman`._

## Days the reader may not choose

`min` and `max` are ISO days; `isDateUnavailable(iso)` returns `true` or the reason as a sentence ("Weekends are closed."). Those days are disabled in the month and their names carry the reason ("Saturday, September 19, 2026, Not available. Weekends are closed."); the month does not page before `min` or after `max`; when today may not be chosen, Today is disabled but stays in the tab order and says why ("The latest date is Dec 31, 2025."), as Button's `disabledReason`; a typed day outside them is an error that names the limit. Say the rule in the hint as well, where every reader sees it before choosing.

`calendarProps` passes the month's own options: `captionLayout="dropdown"` for the year dropdown when the day is a year or more away, `startMonth` and `endMonth`, `showWeekNumber`, `fixedWeeks`.

_Example: story `Stories.MinMaxAndReasons`._
_Example: story `Stories.TodayUnavailable`._
_Example: story `Stories.YearDropdown`._

## Values and forms

Use `value` and `onValueChange` for controlled state or `defaultValue` for uncontrolled; `onChange` is the older spelling of `onValueChange`, deprecated and kept for one version. Choosing reports an ISO day and clearing reports `""`. A value that is not an ISO day warns once in the console: a timestamp is read as its day in the provider's zone, and anything else ("2026-02-30") as empty, so the field never shows one day and submits another. A hidden input carries the day under `name`, including for an owning form named by `form`; a disabled picker submits nothing. A native form reset restores an uncontrolled default; a controlled caller resets its own value.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeForm`._

## Accessibility

- Inside a Field the picker is the Field's control: the FieldLabel names it without ids, and the hint, the error and the Field's `invalid` and `disabled` reach it. Outside one, give it `aria-label`.
- The picking button's name is its label, and it is described by the chosen day first, then the hint and the error, so a reader tabbing through a form hears the value without opening the month. The month is named after its field.
- The month takes focus when it opens. Choosing, Clear and Escape return focus to the field, including inside a Dialog, which stays open.
- A typed field is a text input and announces required; a button cannot carry `aria-required`, so the picking form says required in the label's asterisk and the form's check.
- The month keeps the Calendar's keyboard: arrows by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month, Shift with them by year, Home and End by week, one tab stop.

_Example: story `Stories.InField`._
_Example: story `Stories.FocusIntegration`._

## Props

_Props: generated from `DatePicker`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

_Example: story `Stories.DatePickerMatrix`._

<!-- page: Components/DateRangePicker (src/stories/components/DateRangePicker.mdx) -->

# DateRangePicker

A range of calendar days from one field: a trigger that reads the range ("Sep 7 – 11, 2026") and a popover with two months and, optionally, named presets. It holds and reports two ISO days, `{ start, end }`, both inclusive, and never shifts them across zones. Built on [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-calendar--docs)'s range mode.

Use it for a period the reader thinks of as one thing: a reporting period, a program period, a date filter. A single day is a [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs). A start and an end that the reader sets at different times, or that carry their own rules, are two DatePickers whose `min` and `max` follow each other.

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Reporting period</FieldLabel>
  <DateRangePicker value={period} onValueChange={setPeriod} presets={quarters} />
</Field>
```

_Example: story `Stories.WithPresets`._

## Choosing

The first day the reader chooses starts a new range and the second ends it, in either order; choosing the same day twice makes a one-day range. Until the end is chosen the footer says "Choose the end date." and a screen reader hears it. Once both ends are chosen the popover closes, focus returns to the trigger and `onValueChange` receives the range. Escape or a click outside closes without a change; a half-chosen range is never reported. Clear reports `{ start: "", end: "" }`.

`presets` are named ranges beside the months: choosing one sets the range and closes. The preset that matches the value is pressed and carries a check. On a phone the presets wrap above the month. A preset whose start or end may not be chosen (outside `min` or `max`, or unavailable) is disabled but stays in the tab order, and its reason ("The earliest date is Sep 1, 2026.") is its description and shows in a tooltip, as Button's `disabledReason`.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Limits

`min`, `max` and `isDateUnavailable` work as on DatePicker: those days are disabled with their reason in their names, and the months do not page past the limits. A range may span an unavailable day, such as a weekend inside a reporting week.

_Example: story `Stories.MinAndMax`._

## Values and forms

Each end is an ISO day; an end that is not one warns once and is treated as empty, and ends out of order are no range. `startName` and `endName` put the ends in two hidden inputs for a native form.

## Accessibility

- Inside a Field the trigger is the Field's control: the FieldLabel names it, and the hint, the error and the Field's state reach it.
- The trigger's name is its label and its description is the range in full words, "September 7, 2026 to September 11, 2026", so a screen reader does not read the dash. The popover is named after the field.
- The months keep the Calendar's keyboard and name each range end; the presets are toggle buttons in a group named "Presets".

## Props

_Props: generated from `DateRangePicker`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

# DateTime, RelativeTime and DateLabel

Every date the product shows, through one formatter: the LedgerProvider's locale and time zone. Each renders a `<time>` with its ISO value, and the full value ("Friday, September 18, 2026 at 5:30 PM Pacific Daylight Time") opens in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus and is the description a screen reader hears.

| Part         | Shows                                                 | For                                                      |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| DateTime     | "Sep 18, 2026" or "Sep 18, 2026, 5:30 PM"             | A date or a moment in a property, a cell, a sentence     |
| RelativeTime | "5 minutes ago", "yesterday", "in 3 days"             | Activity, updated and saved times, where recency matters |
| DateLabel    | "Sep 22, 2026 · Overdue", "Due today", "Due tomorrow" | A due date, expiry or milestone the reader acts on       |

Use them wherever the product prints a date, in place of `toLocaleString`, `toLocaleDateString` or a formatter of its own, so one record reads the same day on every screen. Inside DataTable a date column is `c.date`, which reads the same locale and zone; it shows an instant's day by default and its time with `format: "medium"`. A date the reader enters is a [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs) or a [DateTimeField](?path=/docs/components-datetimefield--docs).

```tsx
<DateTime value={record.updated_at} />
<RelativeTime value={comment.created_at} />
<DateLabel value={task.due_on} complete={task.status === "done"} />
```

## Days and instants

An ISO day (`"2026-09-18"`) is a calendar day: it never shifts, whoever reads it. An instant (an ISO timestamp with an offset, a Date or epoch milliseconds) is shown in the provider's zone, UTC unless the product sets one, so the same instant reads Sep 18 in Los Angeles and Sep 19 in Tokyo. Mount one LedgerProvider with the reader's zone near the root and keep it the same on the server and the client. Nothing (`null`, `undefined`, `""`) shows [Absent](?path=/docs/components-typography--docs), with `absentLabel` for a screen reader. A string that is neither warns once and shows as written.

`format` is `date` (a day's default), `datetime` (an instant's default), `time`, or Intl options of your own; `showTimeZone` adds the zone's short name to an instant.

_Example: story `Stories.Formats`._

## The full value

The tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus, never on hover alone. A date standing alone takes a tab stop so a keyboard reaches it; inside a link, a button or a row that takes focus itself (one with a `tabindex`, as in a grid or tree) the host's focus opens it and the date takes none. A row that cannot take focus, as in a plain table, is no host, so the date keeps its tab stop. Turn the tab stop off (`focusable={false}`) in a dense list whose preview or record already shows the full value, and the tooltip off (`isTooltipDisabled`, as on IconButton) where the text is already full.

_Example: story `Stories.FullValue`._

## RelativeTime

Words from `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` in the provider's locale: under a minute either way is "now"; then minutes, hours, days ("yesterday", "tomorrow"), weeks, months and years. The words follow the clock without a reload, updating when they would change. A fixed `now` stops the updates, for a test or a snapshot. A calendar day reads relative to the reader's today. `unitStyle` is `long`, `short` or `narrow`.

_Example: story `Stories.Relative`._
_Example: story `Stories.Updating`._

## DateLabel

A due date that says where it stands. Overdue (danger), due today and due within `soonWithin` days (warning, 2 by default) each carry an icon and words beside the date as well as a tone, so the state never rests on colour and survives forced colours. A later date shows plainly with a calendar icon, and `complete` shows a finished item's date plainly, never overdue. A day is judged against the reader's today; an instant against now, in the provider's zone.

_Example: story `Stories.DueDates`._

## Accessibility

- The `<time>` element carries the machine value; the words are the visible text and the full value is the description on focus.
- The tooltip is a visual copy of that description, hidden from assistive technology.
- DateLabel's state is in its words ("Overdue", "Due today"), which a screen reader reads with the date.

_Props: generated from `DateTime`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props: generated from `RelativeTime`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### DateLabel

_Props: generated from `DateLabel`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

# DateTimeField

A moment: a day and a time together, typed or picked, in the LedgerProvider's time zone, which it names after the time ("PDT"). It holds and reports an ISO instant in UTC (`"2026-09-19T00:30:00.000Z"`), so the moment a reader enters is the moment stored, and every reader sees it in their provider's zone.

Use it for a point in time: evidence collected at, a response due at 5 PM, a scheduled start. A day with no time (a due date, a planned completion) is a [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs); a wall time that repeats is a [TimeField](?path=/docs/components-timefield--docs). It replaces `input type="datetime-local"`, which ignores the provider and leaves the zone unsaid.

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Evidence collected</FieldLabel>
  <DateTimeField name="collected_at" value={collectedAt} onValueChange={setCollectedAt} />
</Field>
```

_Example: story `Stories.InField`._

## The two halves

The day is a typed [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs) input with its month, and the time a [TimeField](?path=/docs/components-timefield--docs) input with its stepping; each reads what the reader types in the locale, and the time shows the zone's short name. Where the field's container holds them they sit side by side; below 256px the time goes under the day.

The field reports an instant once both halves read, and `""` while either is missing or not valid. `defaultTime` (an ISO time such as `"17:00"`) fills the time when the reader picks a day first. When focus leaves the field with one half filled, it says "Enter both a date and a time." A day and a wall time become an instant in the provider's zone: a time a daylight-saving change skips moves forward by the gap, and a time that happens twice takes the earlier moment.

_Example: story `Stories.DefaultTimeAndIncomplete`._

## Limits

`min` and `max` are instants. Days outside them are disabled in the month with their reason; a time before `min` on its first day is an error that names the limit: "Enter Sep 21, 2026, 9:00 AM or later." `isDateUnavailable` works as on DatePicker.

_Example: story `Stories.MinAndMax`._

## Values and forms

`value` is an instant with an offset or `Z`. A value with no offset (`"2026-09-18T17:30"`, what `datetime-local` holds) is read as a wall time in the provider's zone, which makes moving a native field over a one-line change; anything else warns once and is treated as empty. A hidden input carries the instant under `name`; put `name` here, not on the Field. A native form reset puts the field back as it was, a half entry and its message included. One message under the field speaks for both halves: a day or time that does not read, a moment outside the limits, or a missing half.

_Example: story `Stories.FormReset`._

## Accessibility

- Inside a Field the day input is the Field's control, so the FieldLabel points at it. The whole field is a group named by the label; the day input is named "Evidence collected Date" and the time "Evidence collected Time Pacific Daylight Time", so a screen reader hears the zone that the eye reads as "PDT".
- The Field's hint and error describe both inputs, and its invalid state reaches both.
- Keep `showTimeZone` on. A time without its zone reads as two moments to readers in two offices.

## Props

_Props: generated from `DateTimeField`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

# Density

Row density belongs to each table. `default` gives rows 40px of height; `compact` gives them 36px. Headers, controls and typography keep their sizes.

## Usage

Set `density` on a plain Table. The frame sets `data-density="compact"`, which changes the row-height token for its contents. Keep that attribute on the table frame so nearby lists and cards retain their spacing.

_Example: story `Stories.Tables`._

## Reader preference

A DataTable's Columns menu offers Compact rows. With a `view` name, the choice persists with its column settings; Reset view restores the author's default.

_Example: story `Stories.RegisterStory`._

For a compact default, pass `density: "compact"` to `useDataTable`. The reader can still change it.

_Example: story `Stories.ByDesign`._

## Accessibility

Changing row height preserves labels, focus order and control targets. The Columns menu exposes the current choice as a checkbox item. Offer density per table, so a choice in one view does not change unrelated content.

## Migration

The former global density provider, switch, hook, storage helpers and scripts are removed. Remove their imports and unwrap the provider's children. Use `Table density` or the DataTable view setting; no document-wide storage key or before-paint script is needed. The `Density` type remains exported.

## Related

- [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs): native table structure and density prop.
- [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs): view preferences, Columns menu and reset.

# Dialog

A focused task over the page: a create or edit form, a review, a choice that needs more than a sentence. Built on [Base UI Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog) with [shadcn’s composition](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/dialog) and Ledger's tokens.

_Example: story `Stories.Form`._

## When to use it

- **A create or edit form**, titled with the operation: Create task, Edit member. The trigger, the title and the primary say the same words.
- **A task the reader finishes or abandons** before going back to the page.

Not for a decision that needs one sentence: that is an [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs). Not for a task at its button (a filter, a reason): that is a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs). Not for work beside a list the reader keeps using: that is the Shell's panel. A modal edge panel is a [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs), and a phone's bottom sheet a [Drawer](?path=/docs/components-drawer--docs).

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} pending={pending}>
  <DialogContent width="medium" initialFocus={firstField}>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Create task</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>Describe the work.</DialogDescription>
    </DialogHeader>
    <DialogBody>
      <form id={formId} noValidate onSubmit={submit}>
        …fields
      </form>
    </DialogBody>
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose render={<Button variant="subtle" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>
      <Button type="submit" form={formId} variant="primary" isLoading={pending}>
        Create task
      </Button>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
```

- **DialogContent** brings its portal, the blanket and a close button at the top end, an IconButton named Close with no tooltip. It records the overlay surface as the current one, so a sticky header, a pinned cell or a scroll arrow inside paints the dialog's colour, not the page's.
- **DialogHeader** holds the title and the description; the title is the dialog's h2, and headings inside the dialog start at h3.
- **DialogBody** is the one scrolling region, with the dialog's inset. Put the form in it and the buttons in the footer; never make a `fieldset` or a hand-written `div` the scroller.
- **DialogFooter** stays outside the scroll, with Cancel, a subtle button, before the primary.
- DialogPortal and DialogOverlay are exported for a custom popup.

## Widths

`width` on DialogContent picks a step; do not set pixels in `style`.

| `width`      | Size                           | For                                  |
| ------------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| `small`      | 400px                          | A short question with a field or two |
| `medium`     | 520px, the default             | A form of a few fields               |
| `large`      | 760px                          | A form in two columns, or a table    |
| `xlarge`     | 960px                          | A table beside a preview             |
| `fullscreen` | The window, less a 1rem gutter | A task that needs the whole window   |

Every step narrows to the window less the gutter, so a dialog on a phone is the phone's width. Choose the width by the task, so dialogs of the same kind open at the same size.

_Example: story `Stories.Widths`._

## Scrolling and short windows

The body takes the height the header and footer leave, at least 80px, and scrolls. Read-only content that overflows makes it a tab stop, named "Content, scrolls", so the keyboard can scroll what a pointer can.

_Example: story `Stories.Scrollable`._

In a window under 30rem tall (a landscape phone, or a laptop at 200% to 400% zoom) the popup becomes the one scroller: the header scrolls away with the body, the footer stays at the bottom, and every field and the primary can still be reached and seen.

_Example: story `Stories.LongForm`._

_Example: story `Stories.ZoomedWindow`._

## Pending

`pending` on the Dialog holds it while a save or another command runs. Every request to close is cancelled before `onOpenChange` hears of it (Escape, the blanket, the close button, any DialogClose), the close controls are disabled, the built-in close button and a DialogClose rendered as a kit Button stay focusable while they are (`aria-disabled`), and the popup is `aria-busy`. Close the dialog yourself when the command succeeds, with `open={false}`. `pending` does not disable the form: wrap the fields in `<FieldSet disabled={pending}>`, give the submit button `isLoading`, and move focus to that button before the fields lock, since it stays focusable while it loads.

_Example: story `Stories.PendingAndNestedPopup`._

A failed save keeps the dialog and the draft, ends the pending state and says what to change.

_Example: story `Stories.FormSaveFails`._

## Accessibility

- **A title names the dialog**; a DialogDescription, when there is one, describes it.
- **Focus moves in and comes back.** The first field takes focus through `initialFocus` on DialogContent, never through `autoFocus` on the field: an `autoFocus` inside a dialog opened from state becomes the place focus returns to, and focus falls to the page when it closes. Base UI returns focus to the element that had it before the dialog opened; when that element goes away with the task, pass `finalFocus`.
- **Base UI owns** the focus trap, Escape, the outside press and nested popups: a Select or a DatePicker inside closes on its own Escape first.
- **One stack is allowed:** an AlertDialog over the Dialog that owns the decision, such as the discard prompt for a dirty draft. An independent record workflow replaces the dialog instead of stacking.

## Content

- The title is the operation and the singular noun; the primary says the same words, never OK, Submit or Save alone.
- Validate on submit with the primary enabled. Errors say what fixes the field; an [ErrorSummary](?path=/docs/components-errorsummary--docs) lists them all when the form is longer than a few fields.
- Button labels stay on one line.

## Props

Dialog takes Base UI Dialog's root props, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` (its details say why: `reason` is `escape-key`, `outside-press`, `close-press` or another, and `cancel()` keeps the dialog open), `onOpenChangeComplete`, `modal`, `disablePointerDismissal`, `actionsRef` and `handle`, and Ledger's `pending`. DialogContent takes the popup's `initialFocus`, `finalFocus`, `render`, `className` and `style`, and Ledger's `width` and `showCloseButton`. DialogTrigger, DialogClose, DialogTitle and DialogDescription take Base UI's part props, `render` among them. The types are in [Base UI's API reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog#api-reference).

_Props: generated from `Dialog`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### DialogContent

_Props: generated from `DialogContent`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### DialogBody

_Props: generated from `DialogBody`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### DialogFooter

_Props: generated from `DialogFooter`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### DialogTrigger

_Props: generated from `DialogTrigger`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### DialogClose

_Props: generated from `DialogClose`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

<!-- page: Components/Diff (src/stories/components/Diff.mdx) -->

# Diff

What changed between two versions of a text: a revised statement, a library update against the copy in use, a tailored narrative against its baseline. Removed lines are marked −, added lines +, the words that changed inside an edited line are struck through or underlined, and unchanged runs fold behind a button so the reader sees the change, not two full copies.

It compares; it does not edit or decide. The caller owns what the two texts are and what happens next (accept the update, keep the tailoring). One text on its own is [CodeBlock](?path=/docs/components-codeblock--docs) for source or [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs) for prose; what happened to a record over time is a [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs); two values per record across many records is a [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) column, with a Diff in the row's preview when the reader needs the change.

_Example: story `Stories.Inline`._

## Anatomy

| Part       | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame      | A group named `Changes from {beforeLabel} to {afterLabel}`, on `elevation.surface` with a 1px `color.border` and `radius.medium`.                                                           |
| Header     | The legend (− and the earlier text's label, + and the later's) and the summary at the end: "3 changed, 1 added, 1 removed", or "No differences". Side by side, each label heads its column. |
| Line       | A row: optional line numbers, the marker (+, − or blank) and the text, which keeps its spacing and wraps. Removed lines on `color.background.danger.subtler`, added on `.success.subtler`.  |
| Word marks | Inside an edited line, the removed words in a `<del>`, struck through on `color.background.danger.subtle`; the added words in an `<ins>`, underlined on `color.background.success.subtle`.  |
| Fold       | An unchanged run, behind a subtle xsmall button: "Show 4 unchanged lines", then "Hide 4 unchanged lines".                                                                                   |

## How it compares

Lines first, then words. A line is what sits between line breaks, so in a narrative a paragraph is a line: pass the text as it is stored, not wrapped at a width, or every reflow reads as a change. The comparison is the shortest edit script (Myers' algorithm, in the component, no dependency), so the unchanged lines are as many as they can be.

A block of removed lines is then paired with the added lines that replaced them, in order, by how much text they share. A pair that keeps at least half its characters is an **edited** line and gets word marks; a pair that keeps less is a **rewrite**, shown as a removed and an added line with no word marks, because marking every word of a rewritten paragraph says nothing. A space between two changed words joins them, so "shall enforce" to "must require" reads as one change; the spaces at the ends of a changed run are left unmarked, so no mark hangs at a line's edge, and a change of spacing alone marks its line but no words. Words are runs of letters and digits, each punctuation mark, and each CJK character, cut by the same rule on the server and in the browser so hydration matches. Past 1,000 line edits, or 500 word edits in one line, it stops searching for the shortest script: it anchors on the lines each version has exactly once, in order, and compares the gaps between them, so a long text with many scattered edits keeps its unchanged lines. Only a gap with nothing to anchor on is shown replaced whole.

The same comparison is exported as `diffText(before, after)`: the rows of the side-by-side view and the counts (`changed`, `added`, `removed`, `unchanged`), for a section's count or for deciding whether a Diff is worth showing.

_Example: story `Stories.Counts`._

## Layouts

`layout="inline"`, the default, is one column: each edited line's earlier version directly above its later one, then any lines only one version has. `layout="side-by-side"` puts the earlier text beside the later, row for row, and suits a wide page where the reader compares long paragraphs.

_Example: story `Stories.SideBySide`._

Side by side measures its own width, not the window's. Below 36rem of its own (a panel, a rail, a phone), the halves stack and the view reads as inline: the second copy of each unchanged line and the empty halves go. Nothing is lost, and the reader's place does not change.

_Example: story `Stories.InANarrowContainer`._

The Diff fills the width it is given. It measures itself for that fallback, so its own lines never size it: in a flex row it takes the row's free width, and in a box that shrinks to its content (a popover, a table cell with no width), give it a width.

_Example: story `Stories.BesideOtherContent`._

## States

| State          | What shows                                                                                   |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Changed        | The marked lines, the unchanged context and the folds, with the counts in the header.        |
| No differences | "No differences" in the header and the whole text behind one fold.                           |
| New text       | Every line added (`before=""`); no word marks.                                               |
| Removed text   | Every line removed (`after=""`).                                                             |
| Rewritten      | A removed and an added line with no word marks, counted as one change.                       |
| Fold open      | The unchanged lines in place, and the same button, now Hide, keeping focus.                  |
| Blank lines    | A blank line keeps a full line's height; one added or removed is marked like any other line. |

_Example: story `Stories.States`._

_Example: story `Stories.BlankLines`._

## Modifiers

- **`beforeLabel`, `afterLabel`**: what the two texts are, "Version 3" and "Now", "Library" and "This program". They head the legend and name the group. "Before" and "After" by default; say which.
- **`context`**: unchanged lines kept on each side of a change, 3 by default. A longer unchanged run folds, unless the fold would hide a single line. `Infinity` shows every line.
- **`lineNumbers`**: a gutter with each version's numbers, both inline and each side's own side by side. Off by default, because a narrative's lines are paragraphs.
- **`code`**: the code face, for source and configuration.
- **`label`**: the group's name when the default does not say enough ("Access policy, Version 3 to Now").

Long unbroken text, such as a link or a hash, wraps at the frame's edge instead of widening it.

_Example: story `Stories.LongUnbrokenText`._

_Example: story `Stories.Code`._

## Content

- **Name both versions** in the labels: a version number, a date, "Library" or "Now". "Before" and "After" leave the reader to work out which is which.
- **Compare what the reader will decide on.** Pass the statement, not the whole record serialized; field-by-field changes belong in labelled properties.
- **Keep paragraphs as lines.** Text hard-wrapped at a width turns one edited sentence into several changed lines.
- **One Diff per text.** Several fields that changed are several Diffs under their own headings, or a DataTable with a preview.

## Accessibility

- **Never colour alone.** Every change is marked three ways: the + or − marker, a visually hidden "Added:" or "Removed:" before the line, and a text decoration on changed words (struck through for removed, underlined for added) in native `<del>` and `<ins>` elements. In forced-colours mode the tints go and the markers and decorations stay.
- **The group is named** `Changes from {beforeLabel} to {afterLabel}`, and a visually hidden legend says which version the removed and added lines come from.
- **A fold is a disclosure:** a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. Opening it keeps focus on the same button, which now hides the lines again, so focus is never dropped. Folded lines are `hidden="until-found"`, so the browser's find-in-page reaches them and opens their fold.
- **Read once:** side by side, the second copy of an unchanged line is hidden from assistive technology; line numbers and markers are hidden too, and are not selectable, so a copied selection is the text alone.
- **Touch:** the fold buttons are 24px tall; nothing depends on hover.
- **Direction:** the gutter, marker and column rule use logical properties, so a right-to-left page mirrors them: the line numbers, the marker and the earlier column sit at the right. Each line of prose takes its direction from its own text (`dir="auto"`), so a Latin statement on a right-to-left page keeps its full stop at its end; with `code`, every line reads left to right, so a brace never mirrors.
- **Contrast:** text and line numbers on the tinted rows meet 4.5:1 in both modes; the a11y gate checks every story.

_Example: story `Stories.RightToLeft`._

_Example: story `Stories.Localized`._

The legend, the summary, the hidden prefixes and the fold's words come from the locale's messages (`diffLabel`, `diffLegend`, `diffChangedCount`, `diffAdded`, `diffShowLinesOne`, `diffShowLinesOther` and the rest), and the counts from its number and list formats.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Diff`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

<!-- page: Components/Drawer (src/stories/components/Drawer.mdx) -->

# Drawer

A gesture-driven panel using [shadcn’s Base UI composition](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/drawer) and [Base UI Drawer](https://base-ui.com/react/components/drawer). Use Sheet for a side panel that needs no swipe gestures.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Drawer showSwipeHandle>
  <DrawerTrigger render={<Button />}>Quick actions</DrawerTrigger>
  <DrawerContent>
    <DrawerHeader>
      <DrawerTitle>Control actions</DrawerTitle>
      <DrawerDescription>For the selected control.</DrawerDescription>
    </DrawerHeader>
    <DrawerBody>Actions</DrawerBody>
    <DrawerFooter>
      <DrawerClose render={<Button />}>Done</DrawerClose>
    </DrawerFooter>
  </DrawerContent>
</Drawer>
```

Content composes Portal, the modal Overlay, Base UI Viewport/Popup and the text-selectable Content region, and records the overlay surface as the current one, so a sticky header or pinned cell inside matches the drawer. Header, Body, Title, Description, Footer and Close are explicit parts; the title is the drawer's h2 and headings inside start at h3. Portal, Overlay and SwipeHandle are also exported for custom native compositions.

DrawerBody is the one scrolling region between the header and the footer, with the drawer's inset, at least 80px tall. Base UI lets a swipe that starts in it scroll it, and dismiss once it is at its edge. Read-only content that overflows makes it a tab stop, "Content, scrolls". In a window under 30rem tall the drawer scrolls as one, with the footer held at the bottom.

_Example: story `Stories.Actions`._

## Variants and states

`swipeDirection` is `down` by default; `up`, `left` and `right` use physical edges. `showSwipeHandle` defaults to false. Root supports controlled or uncontrolled open state, native snap points and modal modes. Put long content in DrawerBody. Side drawers default to 75% of the viewport, capped at 24rem; vertical drawers leave space above the panel.

_Example: story `Stories.Positions`._
_Example: story `Stories.SnapPoints`._

Drawer has no `pending` prop. For pending work, cancel the native `onOpenChange` event details while the command runs, and disable the close controls; the same callback receives Escape, outside press, close button and swipe requests. Dialog, Sheet and AlertDialog have `pending`.

_Example: story `Stories.NestedPopups`._

## Accessibility

Supply a Title or an accessible name. Description is optional and creates its relationship only when rendered. Include an accessible Close action; the swipe handle is decorative. Base UI handles focus trapping, restoration, Escape, scroll locking and nested popups. Content accepts native `initialFocus`, `finalFocus`, refs, render and state callbacks. Specify a surviving finalFocus target if the opener disappears.

Nested drawers must be nested in the React tree. Ledger’s CSS follows Base UI’s measured swipe, snap and stack variables and honors reduced motion.

_Example: story `Stories.NestedDrawers`._

## Props

Drawer takes Base UI Drawer's root props, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` (with the change's `reason` and `cancel()` in its details), `onOpenChangeComplete`, `modal`, `disablePointerDismissal`, `actionsRef`, `handle`, `swipeDirection`, `snapPoints`, `snapPoint`, `defaultSnapPoint`, `onSnapPointChange` and `snapToSequentialPoints`, and Ledger's `showSwipeHandle`. DrawerContent takes the popup's `initialFocus`, `finalFocus`, refs, `render` and `className`. The types are in [Base UI's API reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/drawer#api-reference).

_Props: generated from `Drawer`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `DrawerContent`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `DrawerBody`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `DrawerTrigger`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `DrawerClose`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
