<!-- page: Components/DropdownMenu (src/stories/components/DropdownMenu.mdx) -->

# DropdownMenu

Actions and view options anchored to a button, using shadcn's Base UI Menu composition. Ledger supplies the menu surface, row geometry, colors and motion. A choice of one value in a form is a [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs), a searchable list of commands is a [Command](?path=/docs/components-command--docs), and a destination in a menu is a LinkItem, not an item that navigates from `onClick`.

```tsx
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Actions</DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent>
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={edit}>Edit</DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem variant="danger" onClick={archive}>
      Archive
    </DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

## Composition and states

Root owns controlled or uncontrolled open state, modality, generic trigger payloads and cancellable `onOpenChange(open, details)`. Trigger defaults to a native button and composes existing buttons through `render`. Custom rendered components must accept merged props and refs; use `nativeButton={false}` only when replacing a button with a non-button action target.

Content includes its portal and positioner. It defaults to bottom/start, with a 4px side offset and zero alignment offset. Its width fits its contents and is at least the trigger width or 128px, within the available viewport. A narrow trigger never forces action labels to wrap. It scrolls when the available space is smaller than its contents, inside a [Scroller](?path=/docs/components-scroller--docs) whose hover arrows mark each overflowed edge. Native `style`, `className`, `render` and refs target the popup; classes and styles accept state callbacks. Content's `dir` overrides Ledger's inherited positioning direction.

Use Group around related items and Label inside that Group. Items compose icons, text and Shortcut as children. An action that destroys or cannot be undone uses `variant="danger"`, the word Button uses, so a Delete button and the Delete item beside it say the same thing; a disabled danger item fades like any other, so it never looks ready to run. `variant="destructive"` is the deprecated spelling, kept for one version: it renders as `danger` and `ledger/no-deprecated-name` renames it. `inset` aligns labels and items without icons. The row uses Ledger's 28px menu height. Action labels stay on one line.

_Example: story `Stories.DropdownMenuMatrix`._

## Descriptions and disabled reasons

`description` on DropdownMenuItem adds a second line under the label, in smaller subtle text that wraps inside the menu: what tells two similar actions apart (“Keeps the current version as the baseline”), or a prerequisite. The label and the line share one column between the item's icon and its Shortcut. The line is the item's accessible description, not part of its name, so the arrow keys and typeahead still find the label alone. Keep it to a short phrase; a menu that needs a paragraph per item is a dialog.

An action that cannot run takes `disabledReason` instead of `disabled`: the item is disabled, the arrow keys still reach it, a screen reader announces it as unavailable and reads the reason, and the reason shows as its description line, readable on the faded row. Write what would make it available: “Add content to this version before publishing it.” A tooltip cannot do this job inside a menu, and a disabled item without a reason leaves the reader guessing.

_Example: story `Stories.DescriptionsAndReasons`._

## Choices and closing

Use CheckboxItem with `checked` and `onCheckedChange` for independent options. Use RadioGroup with `value` and `onValueChange`, and RadioItem with `value`, for exclusive options. A change callback's `details.cancel()` rejects the change. The installed Base UI radio value contract is not generic; callers can validate values against their own options.

Ordinary Item actions use `onClick` and close by default. CheckboxItem and RadioItem stay open by default; set `closeOnClick` when selecting should close the menu. Columns keep the menu open while toggling visibility; saved views and sorting close after a choice. Essential form values still belong in labeled form controls.

_Example: story `Stories.Toggles`._

## Submenus and links

Sub, SubTrigger and SubContent create a nested menu. SubContent defaults to start alignment, -3px alignment offset, zero side offset and a 96px minimum. Its logical `inline-end` side and chevron follow the locale. Escape closes the submenu first; Root's `closeParentOnEsc` can change that behavior.

LinkItem is Base UI's native anchor part. Give it `href`, or `render` a router Link, to retain navigation and modified clicks. It stays open by default; `closeOnClick` closes after navigation. Item with a rendered action button instead uses `nativeButton`. The public Portal part is available for custom Base UI compositions; Content already includes one.

_Example: story `Stories.Submenus`._

## Accessibility and dialogs

The trigger exposes `aria-haspopup="menu"` and expanded state. Items use `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` or `menuitemradio`, with checked state where appropriate. Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens from the trigger; arrows, Home, End and typeahead navigate; Enter or Space activates an action. Disabled items remain focusable and announce their disabled state, but cannot activate; give them a `disabledReason` so the reason is announced with them. Root defaults to modal with looping keyboard navigation.

A row-action button must remain keyboard-reachable. Use `opacity-0 focus-visible:opacity-100 group-hover/row:opacity-100 data-popup-open:opacity-100` for visual concealment, rather than `visibility: hidden`, which removes it from keyboard navigation.

Content owns `finalFocus`. Ledger's modal wrappers resolve an activating menu item to its stable menu trigger, so closing the dialog returns there. For custom modal compositions, give the dialog an explicit return ref and use `finalFocus={false}` if menu focus return must be suppressed. A menu inside a Base UI dialog shares its portal boundary; Escape dismisses the menu before its parent dialog.

_Example: story `Stories.Dialogs`._

## Migration and API

Replace the configured `trigger` prop with Trigger's `render`; move placement and width into Content. Replace `DropdownMenu.Item`, `.Label` and `.Separator` with the flat exports. `onSelect` becomes `onClick` for actions; `isSelected` becomes CheckboxItem or RadioGroup state; `closeOnSelect` becomes `closeOnClick`; `tone="danger"` becomes `variant="danger"`; `trailing` becomes Shortcut children. Remove children-as-`close` callbacks: items close through Base UI, and Root exposes controlled state or `actionsRef` for imperative dismissal.

See [shadcn Dropdown Menu](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/dropdown-menu) and [Base UI Menu](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu) for the native APIs. Content adds the four positioning props to Popup. Ledger adds token styling and locale/dialog integration; reference catalogs remain independently refreshable.

# DropZone

A region files can be dropped on, with a [FileTrigger](?path=/docs/components-filetrigger--docs) inside for the keyboard, a screen reader and a touch screen, which cannot drag. Every drop and every choice is checked against `accept`, `maxSize` and `multiple`; accepted files go to `onSelect`, each refused file gets a message, and the result is announced.

Use it where attaching files is the task: an upload form, an import, a record's files. For an attach button in a compact spot (a composer, a toolbar), use a FileTrigger on its own. DropZone chooses files and checks them; it does not upload them. Show the accepted files as [Attachment](?path=/docs/components-attachment--docs) rows and run the upload yourself.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Field required>
  <FieldLabel>Supporting files</FieldLabel>
  <DropZone accept="application/pdf,image/*" maxSize={5_000_000} multiple onSelect={upload}>
    <FieldDescription>PDF or image, up to 5 MB each.</FieldDescription>
  </DropZone>
</Field>
```

- **Title**: the instruction for a pointer, "Drag a file here" or "Drag files here" with `multiple`; `title` replaces it.
- **Children**: the constraints, as a FieldDescription, under the title. In a Field they describe the trigger.
- **Trigger**: a FileTrigger with the zone's `accept`, `multiple` and `disabled`, labelled "Choose a file" or "Choose files"; `triggerLabel` replaces the words and `triggerRef` reaches the button.
- **Refusals**: one line per refused file (a drop of too many files is one line), under the trigger.

Put the zone in a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs). The FieldLabel names the trigger, the FieldDescription describes it, `required` adds "(required)" to its name, and a FieldError of your own, for a problem found on submit, describes it too. Leave the Field's `invalid` unset unless a form library owns it: a FieldError that shows marks the Field invalid by itself, the zone's or yours. Outside a Field the trigger is named by its own words alone (give it `triggerLabel` words that say what to choose), and a refusal still describes it and marks it invalid.

_Example: story `Stories.WithoutAField`._

## Checking files

The zone reads `accept` as the file input does: a media type matches the file's type, a wildcard (`image/*`) its family, an extension (`.pdf`) the end of its name, and `*/*` any file. `maxSize` is bytes per file; write it in decimal units (`5_000_000` for 5 MB), since the message formats it with `formatFileSize`. Without `multiple`, a drop of several files refuses them all with one message.

| Reason  | Message (locale key)                                            |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`  | "notes.docx is not an accepted file type." (`fileTypeRejected`) |
| `size`  | "survey.pdf is larger than 5 MB." (`fileTooLarge`)              |
| `count` | "Add one file at a time." (`fileCountRejected`)                 |

Accepted files in the same drop still go to `onSelect`; `onReject` receives the refusals, each with its `file`, `reason` and `message`. The refusals show in the zone as the Field's FieldError: they describe the trigger, turn the Field invalid (the label and the border take the danger colour, and the trigger `aria-invalid`), and stay until the next drop or choice replaces them. A Field's explicit `invalid={false}` keeps the label at rest, but the trigger and the border still show the refusal.

_Example: story `Stories.Validation`._

## Dragging

While files are dragged over it the zone's border turns solid and takes the selected colour, and its title reads "Drop the file to add it" or "Drop the files to add them", so the state does not rest on colour and survives forced colours. Text or a link dragged across the page does not light it. A click on the zone's surface opens the picker, for a pointer; the trigger is still the only tab stop.

_Example: story `Stories.DragAndDrop`._

`disabled`, on the zone, its Field or a FieldSet, disables the trigger and refuses drops; the zone still takes the drag, so the browser does not open a file dropped on it.

## The upload flow

The caller owns what happens to the files. The pattern the stories show:

- Each accepted file becomes an Attachment row in `uploading`, with a labelled [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs) and a Cancel named for the file ("Cancel uploading plan.pdf").
- A failed upload keeps its row in `error` with the reason in the Description, a Retry and a Remove, each named for the file.
- A finished row is `done`, with the type and the size (`formatFileSize`) and a Download.
- Each result is announced (`announce`: "Uploaded plan.pdf.", "Could not upload scan.png."). After a removal, focus goes to the trigger (`triggerRef`).
- The primary stays enabled. On submit, say what is missing in a FieldError and move focus to the trigger: no file yet, a file still uploading, a failed upload not yet retried or removed.

_Example: story `Stories.UploadFlow`._

## Accessibility

- One tab stop, the trigger. Enter or Space opens the picker; a click on its label does too.
- The result of a drop or a choice is announced politely, since focus stays on the trigger: "Added plan.pdf.", "Added 2 files.", and each refusal. The messages are in the locale (`fileAdded`, `filesAddedOne`, `filesAddedOther`, `dropFileHere`, `dropFilesHere`, `dropFileRelease`, `dropFilesRelease`, `chooseFile`, `chooseFiles` and the three above), so a LedgerProvider can translate them.
- The drag state is a border style and a title as well as a colour. The icon is decorative.
- A refusal is text in the zone and the trigger's description, never only the danger border.
- The zone responds to its own width: its content is one centred column that wraps, and a long file name in a refusal breaks inside it.

## Props

_Props: generated from `DropZone`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

Reference: [Carbon file uploader](https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/file-uploader/usage/), [React Aria DropZone](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/DropZone.html), [Polaris DropZone](https://polaris-react.shopify.com/components/selection-and-input/drop-zone).

# Empty

A region with nothing in it says why, and offers the next step. The picture, the message and the actions sit at the centre of the region; the caller composes them from the parts. A [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) draws its own, so a register never needs to.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Empty>
  <EmptyMedia aria-hidden>
    <EmptyIllustration kind="records" />
  </EmptyMedia>
  <EmptyHeader>
    <EmptyTitle>No programs yet</EmptyTitle>
    <EmptyDescription>Create one to define its systems and their work.</EmptyDescription>
  </EmptyHeader>
  <EmptyContent>
    <Button variant="primary" iconBefore={<Plus />}>New program</Button>
    <Button variant="secondary">Import</Button>
  </EmptyContent>
</Empty>
```

| Part                | What it is                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Empty`             | The region: a column, centred, on a dashed frame. `size="compact"` for the rail's row; `frame="none"` on a surface that already bounds it.                                     |
| `EmptyMedia`        | The picture. Holds an `EmptyIllustration`, or `variant="icon"` draws a Lucide icon in the neutral circle. Anything else fits: an avatar, a chart's ghost.                    |
| `EmptyIllustration` | The kit's picture, on the surface tokens: a scene of ghost records the shape of what the region will hold, sometimes with a badge that says why it is empty. Twelve kinds, below. Decorative. |
| `EmptyHeader`       | The title and its description, at a readable measure.                                                                                                                        |
| `EmptyTitle`        | A heading in the default size, at the contextual level (an h2 when nothing sets one); body text in a div in compact. `render` sets another element.                          |
| `EmptyDescription`  | One or two lines: why there is nothing, what creates it.                                                                                                                     |
| `EmptyContent`      | The actions, centred, wrapping. A second `EmptyContent` holds a quieter row: a link, suggested searches.                                                                     |

## Variants

Which empty this is decides the picture and the action. The picture is the shape of what the region will hold, so a reader who has never seen a record still learns what one is:

| The region                          | `kind`     | Action                                       |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Nothing exists yet                  | `records`  | The primary: create the first, import        |
| A search or a filter left nothing   | `search`   | Clear filters; suggestions under it          |
| Empty because the work is finished  | `done`     | A link to the closed items, or none          |
| Nothing assigned or waiting for you | `inbox`    | None, or a link to everything                |
| The reader may not see this         | `locked`   | Request access                               |
| No controls or requirements yet     | `shield`   | Allocate, map, import a catalog              |
| No files, evidence or documents     | `document` | Upload, attach                               |
| No tasks or work items              | `tasks`    | Add a task                                   |
| No people, owners or assignees      | `people`   | Assign, invite                               |
| No systems, components or parts     | `tree`     | Add the first node                           |
| No data to chart                    | `chart`    | None; the records make the chart             |
| Nothing scheduled                   | `calendar` | Schedule                                     |
| A tab or a card body with no items  | an icon    | One small action                             |
| A rail's related list               | compact    | One link                                     |

A [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) with no records at all is only its Empty: the toolbar, the header and the hairline go, the frame stays, and the action in it creates the first record. While a search or a filter is what emptied it, the toolbar and header stay and the Empty sits under them without a frame.

_Example: story `Stories.NoMatches`._

_Example: story `Stories.Illustrations`._

_Example: story `Stories.Icon`._

_Example: story `Stories.Compact`._

## Sizes

`default` is the hero: the picture, a small heading, body copy, medium buttons, `space.300` between the three, `space.600` above and below. `compact` is the rail's row: `EmptyMedia` beside the message, a medium-weight body title, small body copy, a small link. In compact, place `EmptyMedia` before `EmptyHeader` and keep `EmptyContent` a direct child, so the grid puts media in the first column and the message and actions in the second.

## States

Empty has no states of its own. Loading is [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs) or [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs); an error is an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs). A DataTable chooses between its two empties itself: the caller's message when there are no records, the kit's **Nothing matches** with **Clear filters** while a search or a column filter is active.

## Modifiers

- **`size`**: `default` or `compact`.
- **`frame`**: `dashed` (the default region) or `none`, for a table cell, a page body, a panel that has its own edges. Compact never draws a frame.
- **`kind`** on `EmptyIllustration`: the twelve above. Every scene is 128 by 84px, so empty states sit at one height across a page.

_Example: story `Stories.OnAPage`._

## Content

- **The title says what is missing, in the reader's words**: "No programs yet", "Nothing matches", "Nothing open". Not "Empty", not "No data".
- **The description says why, or what creates it**, in one or two lines. Never advice that points at another control ("Choose another tab").
- **One primary action**, the same verb as the page's own; a secondary beside it at most. In a filtered table the action is **Clear filters**.
- **Suggestions are small secondary buttons** in a second row, after a "Try" in `color.text.subtlest`.

## Style

| Element       | Token                                                                                       |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame         | `color.border` dashed · `radius.large` · `space.300` × `space.600`                          |
| Gaps          | `space.300` between picture, message and actions · `space.100` between title and description |
| Title         | `font.heading.small` · `color.text`                                                         |
| Description   | `font.body` · `color.text.subtle` · 400px measure                                           |
| Icon circle   | `dimension.control.large` · `color.background.neutral` · `color.icon.subtle`                |
| Illustration  | 128 × 84px · `elevation.surface.raised` and `.sunken` · `color.border` and `.bold` · `color.skeleton` · `color.background.neutral` |
| Badge         | `dimension.control.medium` · `color.background.neutral.bold`, `.success.bold` or `.brand.bold` · `color.icon.inverse` · `elevation.shadow.raised` |
| Compact       | no frame · `space.150` between media and message · `font.body` medium · `font.body.small`   |

## Accessibility

The parts are divs with no automatic landmark or announcement, except the title. In the default size EmptyTitle is a real heading at the contextual level, so a page whose content is an Empty (a first run, a missing record, a route that failed) keeps it in the heading outline: an h2 under the page's h1 when nothing sets a level, one below a titled Section. Where the Empty is the page's only content and there is no PageHeader, give it the page's level with `render={<h1 />}`; where it must not be in the outline, `render={<div />}`. In compact, a rail's row, the title is body text. Give the root `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby` the title when the region is a page's main content; inside a table the cell is enough.

_Example: story `Stories.TitleLevel`._

The illustration and the icon circle are decorative: `EmptyIllustration` hides itself, and `EmptyMedia` takes `aria-hidden`. Text precedes the actions in reading order, so a screen reader hears why before what.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Empty`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `EmptyMedia`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `EmptyIllustration`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `EmptyHeader`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `EmptyTitle`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `EmptyDescription`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `EmptyContent`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Every part accepts native div attributes, events, styles and refs; EmptyTitle takes its heading's and `render`. Icon children retain their own props, classes and refs.

### Migration

The default was left-aligned with a body-weight title; it is now centred with a heading, the description at a measure, and the actions under it. A caller that wanted the old row keeps `size="compact"`. `Related`, `Item.Group` and `DataTable` compose the parts themselves; a DataTable's `empty` now takes `illustration`, `secondary` and `filtered`, and draws **Nothing matches** with **Clear filters** on its own while a search or a filter is active.

_Example: story `Stories.EmptyMatrix`._

<!-- page: Components/ErrorSummary (src/stories/components/ErrorSummary.mdx) -->

# ErrorSummary

Every issue with a submitted form in one place. A danger Alert titled "There is a problem" that lists each issue as a button; the button moves focus to the field, with its label in view. The summary takes focus when it appears, so a reader who submits lands on the list of what to fix.

```tsx
<ErrorSummary
  focusKey={attempts}
  issues={[
    { message: "Enter a task title.", target: titleId },
    { message: "Choose a program.", target: () => programRef.current },
  ]}
/>
```

_Example: story `Stories.OnSubmit`._

## When to use it

- **A long form or a dialog that scrolls**, where some invalid fields are out of sight after a submission.
- **A multi-step flow**, on the last step, for issues on earlier steps.

Each field still shows its own [FieldError](?path=/docs/components-field--docs). A short form whose fields all fit on screen needs no summary: focus the first invalid control instead. A failure that is not about a field (a lost connection, a refused permission) is an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs) with `role="alert"`.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Issues

- **`message`** says what fixes the field and names it, in the same words as its FieldError: "Enter a task title.", not "Required.".
- **`target`** is the control: its `id`, the element, or a function that finds it. A RadioGroup or a FieldSet focuses its first focusable control; a Checkbox or Switch `id`, which names the hidden input, focuses the visible box.
- **`onSelect`** runs before focus moves, to open the step or tab that holds the field; the summary then focuses the field once it has rendered.
- An issue with neither `target` nor `onSelect` (a rule across two fields) is listed as text, not a button, because it leads nowhere.

List the issues in the order the fields appear, and pass the ones found at the last submission. Recomputing them on every keystroke re-announces the alert while the reader types; the fields' own errors update as the reader repairs them.

_Example: story `Stories.EarlierStep`._

## Focus

The summary focuses itself when it appears. Change `focusKey` on each failed submission (a submit count) to bring focus back to a summary already showing. `autoFocus={false}` leaves focus where it is, for a summary rendered on arrival at a step. With no issues it renders nothing, so it can stay in place above the form.

With TanStack Form, an error returned from `onSubmitAsync` is cleared on the field's next blur, and the summary taking focus is that blur: keep a server rejection in your own state until the reader changes the value, as the Forms recovery story does.

_Example: story `Stories.NoIssues`._

## Accessibility

- `role="alert"` announces the summary when it appears; focus lands on it, named by its title, and Tab reaches the first item.
- The title is a heading at the contextual level (an h2 outside every HeadingLevelProvider, an h3 under a level-3 provider), so the summary is in the page's outline.
- Items are buttons, because they act on the page; each moves focus with the keyboard focus ring showing and brings the field's label into view.
- The icon is decorative; the title and the danger surface say it is an error, not the colour alone.

_Example: story `Stories.InSection`._

## Props

_Props: generated from `ErrorSummary`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

# Fact

An inline label and value on one baseline: Owner Dana Whitfield, Frequency Quarterly. A row of them is a `Fact.Group`, the facts strip under a record's title: the four to six facts the reader acts on, above the fold, so that needing to open a panel to find out who owns a thing is never the problem. The rest belong in the rail as [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs) rows. The strip most page headers write by hand.

_Example: story `Stories.FactMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part  | What it is                                                                                                                   |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label | `dt` in `font.body.small` and `color.text.subtle`, one or two words.                                                         |
| Value | `dd` after it, `space.075` away, `font.body` medium in `color.text`: a word, a number, a date, a Person, a Badge, an Absent. |
| Group | A `dl` that wraps: `space.300` between facts, `space.075` between lines, every fact whole on its line.                       |

## Variants

Fact has one appearance. What varies is where the strip is:

| Where                  | What it holds                                                         |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Under a record's title | The facts the reader acts on: owner, due, method, count. At most six. |
| In a Sheet's header    | The same, for the record the sheet shows.                             |
| In a Glance            | Three or four, for the record previewed.                              |

Not built, and why: a stacked label-over-value grid (the prototype draws one by hand on several pages), because that shape is a decision still open; a Fact that edits in place, because the value is an [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs) and the Fact only frames it.

## Sizes

One size: the label `font.body.small`, the value `font.body`. The strip is as wide as its header and wraps when narrower; a fact never breaks across lines.

_Example: story `Stories.UnderHeader`._

## States

A Fact has one state. Its value may: a Badge is a state, a Person is a person, an Editable value opens. The Fact does not.

## Modifiers

- **The value** is the modifier: text, a Person, a Badge at `xsmall`, an Id, an Absent, an Editable.
- **Group `className`** for the rule above the strip under a header.

## Content

- **The label is one or two words, a noun:** "Owner", "Next due", "Open findings".
- **The value is one thing that fits on a line:** a name, a number, a date, a state. A sentence is Prose or a wrapping KeyValue.
- **Four to six facts, the ones acted on.** Reference joins (created by, framework, family) go in the rail.
- **A missing value stays, as an Absent**, so the strip says what is missing.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                     |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label   | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle`                                   |
| Value   | `font.body` medium · `color.text` · `space.075` after the label           |
| Group   | `space.300` between facts · `space.075` between wrapped lines · baselines |

## Accessibility

- **A group is a definition list** and each Fact a `dt` and `dd`, so a screen reader hears "Owner, Dana Whitfield" as a pair. A Fact belongs inside a Fact.Group; the headers and sheets that take a `facts` slot wrap it.
- **The strip is read in order**, so the order is the order of importance.
- **An Absent is read as a dash**, which says "nothing here" in one character.
- **Contrast:** the label in `color.text.subtle` passes 4.5:1; the gate runs the matrix.

_Props: generated from `Fact`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

<!-- page: Components/Field (src/stories/components/Field.mdx) -->

# Field

One control with its label, hint and error. Field is Base UI's Field underneath, so the parts tie themselves to the control: no ids, no `htmlFor`, no `aria-describedby` and no `aria-invalid` written by hand. The form still owns values and validation; the Field carries what the form decided.

```tsx
<Field invalid={invalid} required>
  <FieldLabel>Owner</FieldLabel>
  <Input value={owner} onValueChange={setOwner} />
  <FieldDescription>Use the full name.</FieldDescription>
  <FieldError errors={errors} />
</Field>
```

The label names the control and its click focuses it; the hint and the error describe it, in that order; `invalid` reaches the control as `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid` and turns the label and the error to the danger colour; `required` announces the requirement and adds the label's asterisk, which is hidden from the accessible name. The same binding reaches Input, Textarea, InputGroupInput, the Select trigger, the Combobox input, Checkbox, RadioGroup and Switch.

_Example: story `Stories.EveryControl`._

## Parts

`FieldLabel`, `FieldDescription` and `FieldError` bind inside a Field and stay plain elements outside one. `FieldSet` and `FieldLegend` group related controls, and a RadioGroup inside a FieldSet is named by its legend. `FieldGroup` spaces fields; `FieldContent` stacks text beside a control; `FieldTitle` is visual text when a wrapping label already names the control, as in a choice card. `FieldSeparator` divides sections, with optional text; its rules stop on either side of the text, so it works on any surface.

_Example: story `Stories.Composition`._

## States

- **`invalid`** comes from the form library (TanStack Form: `isTouched && !isValid`). A FieldError that shows a message also marks the Field invalid, so `<FieldError errors={errors} />` is enough when the errors are already filtered. `data-invalid`, which earlier callers set by hand, is still read as `invalid`.
- **`required`** is announced (`aria-required`) and marked; it is not a native constraint, so a form library that checks it is not second-guessed by the browser. Put native `required` on the control itself when Base UI or the browser should check it. `FieldLabel required={false}` hides the asterisk where most of a form is required and only the optional fields say so. A group Field requires the group, not each checkbox in it.
- **`disabled`** disables the control and dims the label. A Field or a FieldSet inside a disabled Field is disabled too, so a disabled group's legend and choices follow it. `disabled` on a FieldSet reaches every control inside, including the Checkbox, Radio and Switch roots that a native `<fieldset disabled>` leaves live.

_Example: story `Stories.Disabled`._

A focused invalid text field thickens its danger border to the 2px focus edge; a focused invalid Checkbox or Radio keeps its danger border with the focus outline around it, and a Switch swaps its danger outline for the focus outline, so focus is always visible. A FieldLabel wrapping a Field becomes a choice card with hover, checked and keyboard-focus feedback; disabled choices keep a quiet surface.

## Validation

With a form library, pass `invalid` and the messages. Validate on submit, then on change; focus the first invalid control after a failed submission, or an [ErrorSummary](?path=/docs/components-errorsummary--docs) when the form is long.

_Example: story `Stories.Validation`._

Without one, Base UI validates: native constraints on the control, `validate` on the Field for your own rules, `validationMode` for when (`onSubmit`, then on change, by default), and a FieldError with `match` for each message. A FieldError with no children shows Base UI's own message whenever the Field fails.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeValidation`._

FieldError takes children or an `errors` array of message objects, drops duplicates and empty entries, and renders nothing when none remain; children win. It is not a live region: focus and the control's description carry it, and a form-level failure belongs in an Alert or an ErrorSummary.

_Example: story `Stories.Errors`._

## Groups

A group of choices is a Field around a FieldSet: the legend names the group, the Field's hint and error describe it, and `invalid` and `required` reach the RadioGroup (or the checkboxes of a [CheckboxGroup](?path=/docs/components-checkboxgroup--docs)) once; `disabled` reaches every choice. Each choice is its own horizontal Field with a FieldLabel, so it keeps its own name. A RadioGroup announces the requirement itself; a CheckboxGroup's legend says "(required)" to assistive technology, since a group cannot.

```tsx
<Field invalid={invalid} required>
  <FieldSet>
    <FieldLegend variant="label">Review frequency</FieldLegend>
    <RadioGroup value={frequency} onValueChange={setFrequency}>
      <Field orientation="horizontal">
        <RadioGroupItem value="quarterly" />
        <FieldLabel>Quarterly</FieldLabel>
      </Field>
    </RadioGroup>
    <FieldError errors={errors} />
  </FieldSet>
</Field>
```

## Accessibility

- The label names the control through `htmlFor` and `aria-labelledby`, and a Select or Combobox list inside the Field is named by it too. Ids are generated per instance, so a form can appear more than once.
- Hint and error ids reach `aria-describedby` in the order they render; ids the caller already references are listed once.
- Explicit ids, `htmlFor` and ARIA on the parts still win, and wrappers between Field and control do not break the binding.
- DatePicker does not take the binding yet: give its trigger `id`, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`, as the Forms Pickers story does.

_Example: story `Stories.ExplicitAssociations`._

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Props

_Props: generated from `Field`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `FieldLabel`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `FieldError`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `FieldSet`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `FieldLegend`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Every part forwards the native attributes and ref of its element: Field, FieldGroup, FieldContent, FieldTitle, FieldError and FieldSeparator are divs, FieldLabel a label, FieldDescription a paragraph, FieldSet a fieldset and FieldLegend a legend. Field and FieldSet take `render`.

### Migration

Hand-written ids, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid` keep working. To shorten a field, drop them: pass `invalid` and `required` to Field, and remove the label's hand-written asterisk. FieldError is no longer `role="alert"`; a test that finds it by that role finds it by its text or `data-slot="field-error"`.

<!-- page: Components/FileTrigger (src/stories/components/FileTrigger.mdx) -->

# FileTrigger

A [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs) that opens the browser's file picker and hands the chosen files to `onSelect`. The native file input is in the document, hidden, so it takes no space, no focus and no place in the accessibility tree; the button is the control, and the picker returns focus to it when it closes.

Use it where the reader attaches a file from a compact spot: a form row, a composer, a toolbar. Where files can also be dropped, or where the files must be checked against a type or a size, use [DropZone](?path=/docs/components-dropzone--docs), which puts a FileTrigger inside a drop region and does the checking. Do not use `<Input type="file">`: its button loses its frame and the control reads as a line of text.

_Example: story `Stories.InAField`._

## Choosing files

- `accept` is the input's own attribute, as a string or a list: media types (`application/pdf`), wildcards (`image/*`) and extensions (`.csv`). The picker filters by it, but a reader can still pick another file, so check what you receive (DropZone does).
- `multiple` lets the reader choose several files at once; one by default. The label follows: "Choose a file" or "Choose files" (the `chooseFile` and `chooseFiles` messages).
- `onSelect` receives the files as an array once the picker closes with a choice. Cancelling calls nothing. The input is emptied after each choice, so choosing the same file again, after a removal or a failed upload, calls `onSelect` again.
- `capture` offers the camera directly on a phone: `environment` the rear one, `user` the front.
- `onClick` runs first; calling `preventDefault()` in it keeps the picker shut.
- The files are the caller's: FileTrigger does not submit them with a form. Show them as [Attachment](?path=/docs/components-attachment--docs) rows and upload them.

_Example: story `Stories.ChosenFilesAsAttachments`._

## In a Field

Inside a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) the button is the Field's control, as Base UI's own controls are:

- The FieldLabel points at it (`for`), so a click on the label opens the picker, as a native file input's label does.
- It is named by the label and then its own words, "Signed agreement Choose a file", so a speech command can use what the reader sees. `required` on the Field adds "(required)" to the name; a button cannot carry `aria-required`.
- The FieldDescription and FieldError describe it, and the Field's `invalid` reaches it as `aria-invalid`.
- The Field's or a FieldSet's `disabled` disables it.

An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` of your own replaces the composed name.

## States

Every Button prop applies. `isLoading` keeps focus and blocks the picker while a choice is being read; `disabledReason` keeps the button reachable and says why it is unavailable; `disabled` takes it out.

_Example: story `Stories.States`._

In a [ButtonGroup](?path=/docs/components-buttongroup--docs) a FileTrigger is a segment like any Button: the hidden input is not counted, so the group rounds the trigger when it comes last.

_Example: story `Stories.InAButtonGroup`._

## Accessibility

- One tab stop: the button. The hidden input cannot be reached by Tab, is not read, and does not count as a second control.
- Enter and Space open the picker; the browser's picker is keyboard operable and returns focus to the button.
- Say the constraints next to the button in a FieldDescription ("PDF, up to 10 MB"), so they are read with it.
- What happens after the choice is the caller's to say: add the files as rows the reader can reach, and announce the result through a status (the `announce` helper, or a `role="status"` line) if nothing else changes where focus is.

## Props

_Props: generated from `FileTrigger`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

Reference: [React Aria FileTrigger](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/FileTrigger.html).

<!-- page: Components/FilterChip (src/stories/components/FilterChip.mdx) -->

# FilterChip

A filter the reader adds to a [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs): dashed with a plus until it is on, then solid and selected, with the chosen value after its label. A chip is one question of the register, Owner or Status or Gaps; the chips together are the question the table answers.

A chip asks; a [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs) tells. A coordinated set of single or multiple choices is a [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs); a thing to do is a [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.FilterChipMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                                          |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plus   | "+" before the label while the chip is off: add this filter. Hidden from a screen reader; gone once the chip is on. |
| Label  | The column or the question, `font.body`, `color.text.subtle` at rest and `color.text.selected` on.                  |
| Value  | After the label, `font.weight.medium` in `color.text`: the value chosen, or "3 chosen". Truncates past 20ch.        |
| Border | Dashed `color.border.bold` at rest; solid `color.border.selected` on `color.background.selected` once on.           |

## Variants

FilterChip has one appearance. What varies is what a click does:

| The question                                | Use                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Yes or no about the rows: Gaps, Hide closed | A toggle: `isActive` flips, no value.                                                                                                                                                          |
| A column with a value: Owner, Status, Due   | The trigger of a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs); the DataTable's `Filter` builds one from the column (checkboxes, a range, a contains field) and the value reads on the chip. |
| Three values the reader steps through       | A toggle that cycles, the value showing which. Past three, a popover.                                                                                                                          |
| Exclusive choices: All, High, Medium        | A ToggleGroup, not chips.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| A saved question with its count             | The DataTable's `Presets`, a ToggleGroup with Count children.                                                                                                                                  |

There is no remove cross on the chip: a click on an active toggle turns it off, and a popover chip has Clear. There is no chip with an icon, and no chip with a count: the rows a question would leave belong to a preset's Count.

## Sizes

One: `dimension.control.small` 28px, the Toolbar's height, `space.100` each side.

A chip is one line at every width, and it never shrinks below its plus and its label. A value longer than about twenty characters truncates with an ellipsis; its full text is the value's title and stays in the chip's accessible name. In a frame narrower than the chip, the value gives way first.

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

_Example: story `Stories.InToolbar`._

## States

| State        | What changes                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rest         | Dashed `color.border.bold`, the plus, `color.text.subtle`.                                                    |
| Hover        | The border to `color.border`, the text to `color.text`.                                                       |
| Active       | Solid `color.border.selected` on `color.background.selected`, `color.text.selected`; no plus; pressed.        |
| With a value | The value after the label in `color.text` at `font.weight.medium`.                                            |
| Open         | As a Popover's trigger, `aria-expanded`; the chip is active only while it holds a value.                      |
| Focus        | The focus outline.                                                                                            |
| Disabled     | `color.border.disabled`, `color.text.disabled`, no pointer: a filter with nothing to choose. Better left out. |

## Modifiers

- **`label`** and **`value`**.
- **`isActive`** paints the chip on and says pressed.
- **`disabled`**.
- **`onClick`** and the rest of a button's props. A Popover passes `aria-expanded` to its trigger, and the chip stops saying pressed.

## Content

- **The label is the column or the question as a noun**, sentence case: Owner, Status, Gaps, Hide closed. Not "Filter by owner".
- **The value is what was chosen, as the cell shows it**: "Dana Whitfield", "Overdue", "≥ 10", "3 chosen". Never a count of rows.
- **A toggle reads as what it turns on**: Gaps shows the gaps, Hide closed hides them; both are true while the chip is on.
- **Four or five chips** in a toolbar. Past that the table has too many questions, and the answers are presets.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                           |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Chip     | `dimension.control.small` · `radius.medium` · `space.100` sides · gap `space.075` · `font.body` |
| Rest     | border dashed `color.border.bold` · `color.text.subtle` · hover `color.border`, `color.text`    |
| Active   | border `color.border.selected` · `color.background.selected` · `color.text.selected`            |
| Value    | `font.weight.medium` `color.text`                                                               |
| Disabled | `color.border.disabled` · `color.text.disabled`                                                 |
| Focus    | The focus outline                                                                               |
| Motion   | `motion.duration.fast` on the colours                                                           |

## Accessibility

- **A button.** On its own it is a toggle: `aria-pressed` follows `isActive`, so a screen reader hears "Gaps, toggle button, pressed". As a Popover's trigger it takes the popover's `aria-expanded` and does not say pressed; the value in its text says what is applied.
- **Named by its text**, label and value together: "Owner Dana Whitfield".
- **Keyboard.** Tab reaches it; Space or Enter flips it or opens the popover; Escape closes the popover and returns focus to the chip.
- **Not colour alone.** The plus and the dashed border say off; the solid border and the pressed state say on.
- **Disabled is the last resort.** A filter with nothing to choose is left out of the row.

## Props

Native button props, including `ref`, pass through to the button. Refs target `HTMLButtonElement`;
when composed with `PopoverTrigger render={<FilterChip label="Status" />}`, both parts' refs and
event handlers reach the same button. The Popover owns opening, dismissal and focus return.

_Props: generated from `FilterChip`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs): where chips live.
- [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs): `Filter` builds a chip and its popover from a column; `Presets` are saved questions.
- [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs): single or multiple toggle buttons. [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs): what a value chip opens.
- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): a status told, not asked.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/HoverCard (src/stories/components/HoverCard.mdx) -->

# HoverCard

A supplementary preview of a link's destination, built from shadcn's Base UI PreviewCard composition. The trigger stays a link; the preview can contain a [Glance](?path=/docs/patterns-glance--docs) or other supporting content available at that destination.

```tsx
<HoverCard>
  <HoverCardTrigger href="/controls/CTRL-0412">CTRL-0412</HoverCardTrigger>
  <HoverCardContent style={{ width: 300 }}>
    <Glance id="CTRL-0412" title="Segregation of duties, payables" />
  </HoverCardContent>
</HoverCard>
```

## Composition and placement

`HoverCard` owns the open state. `HoverCardTrigger` renders an anchor and accepts native link props, a ref, state callbacks and `render` for a custom link. `HoverCardContent` includes the portal and positioner; its native props, ref and `render` target the popup.

An action trigger can use `render={<button type="button" />}`. Its native button owns click and keyboard activation; Trigger has no `nativeButton` prop.

Content is 256px wide by default. Override its width through `style`, including a state callback. Placement defaults to `side="bottom"`, `sideOffset={4}`, `align="center"` and `alignOffset={4}`. These four props belong to Content. The positioner handles collisions; logical sides and alignment follow the Ledger locale, with Content's `dir` available as an override.

The surface uses Ledger's overlay, border, text, radius, spacing and motion tokens, and records the overlay surface as the current one, so a child painted with `bg-surface-current` (a sticky label, a fade at an edge) matches the card. Content `className` and `style` callbacks receive Base UI popup state; render props, classes, styles and refs are merged.

_Example: story `Stories.HoverCardMatrix`._

## Interaction

The trigger opens the preview after pointer hover or keyboard focus. `delay` defaults to 600ms and `closeDelay` to 300ms, both on Trigger. Pointer passage from trigger to popup keeps the preview open. Leaving both, moving focus away, an outside press or Escape dismisses it. Escape leaves focus where it was.

Clicking or pressing Enter on the trigger follows the link. A trigger press does not itself guarantee dismissal; navigation or caller-controlled state may close the card. Touch follows the link without the mouse-hover behavior.

Use Root's `defaultOpen`, or controlled `open` with `onOpenChange(open, details)`. `details.cancel()` rejects a change. Multiple triggers can share one Root: pass `payload` on each trigger and render the active payload through Root's children function.

_Example: story `Stories.OnAnId`._

## Accessibility

Keep the preview supplementary. Essential information and actions belong at the linked destination or in a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs). Opening the preview does not move focus or add a popup Tab stop, and it is not a dialog announcement. The link remains the way to navigate for keyboard, touch and assistive-technology users.

## Migration

Replace the wrapper's `content` prop with `HoverCardContent` children. Compose an existing link through `HoverCardTrigger render`, or pass `href` and link text directly to Trigger. Move `delay` to Trigger; move placement to Content and replace `width` with `style={{ width }}`. Root retains controlled open state and now provides Base UI event details. The old 280px width and 400ms/120ms timing defaults become 256px and 600ms/300ms.

## Props

HoverCard inherits Base UI's [Root props](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card#root), and HoverCardTrigger inherits its [Trigger props](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card#trigger). HoverCardContent inherits [Popup props](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card#popup) plus the four positioning props described above.

_Props: generated from `HoverCardContent`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

<!-- page: Components/Icon (src/stories/components/Icon.mdx) -->

# Icon

A Lucide glyph with its size, colour and name decided in one place. With a `label` the icon is an image with that name, for a mark that stands for something on its own: an authorization boundary on a tree row, a met check in a cell, an overdue clock. Without one it is decoration beside the word that says the same, and it is hidden from assistive technology. The sizes and colours are the ones on [Tokens/Icons](?path=/docs/tokens-icons--docs).

```tsx
<Icon label="Authorization boundary" color="color.icon.subtle">
  <Shield />
</Icon>
```

_Example: story `Stories.IconMatrix`._

## When to use it

- **A mark that carries meaning with no word beside it** takes an Icon with a `label`. The label is the value, not the glyph: "Met", not "Check"; "Authorization boundary", not "Shield".
- **An icon beside its word** takes an Icon without a label, or no wrapper at all where the part draws it (Button `iconBefore`, Item `leading`, a Badge's icon). Those parts already hide it.
- **A clickable icon is an [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs)**, whose `label` is its name and its tooltip. An Icon is never a target.
- **A status with a word** is an [Indicator](?path=/docs/components-indicator--docs) or a Badge; colour alone never carries the meaning.

_Example: story `Stories.Named`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                               |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Wrapper | A `span` (or the element `render` names), `inline-flex`, the icon's size. `role="img"` and `aria-label` with a `label`; `aria-hidden` without one. |
| Glyph   | The Lucide element passed as the child, sized by the wrapper to `dimension.icon.small` (14px) or `.medium` (16px), at Lucide's stroke.         |
| Colour  | A `color.icon` token, or the surrounding text colour when left out.                                                     |

## Accessibility

- **A named icon is an image with a name.** A screen reader says "Authorization boundary, image"; a generic element with `aria-label` is ignored, which is the mistake this part replaces.
- **A decorative icon is hidden**, so the word beside it is not read twice.
- **A sighted reader needs the meaning too.** A named mark with no word beside it is fine in a dense row where the column or legend says what it means; elsewhere put the word beside it. An Icon has no tooltip, because a tooltip on something that cannot take focus is hover-only.
- **Forced colours**: the glyph is drawn in `currentColor`, so it takes the system text colour.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Icon`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

- [VisuallyHidden](?path=/docs/primitives-visuallyhidden--docs): hidden words beside a mark, read inline with the text.
- [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs): an icon that acts.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/IconButton (src/stories/components/IconButton.mdx) -->

# IconButton

A square [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs) with an icon, a required `label` and a tooltip. Name the action, such as “Search” or “Close.” Use a labelled Button when the icon alone would be unclear, a [LinkIconButton](?path=/docs/components-linkbutton--docs) when the icon goes somewhere (opening a record in a new tab), and a [CopyButton](?path=/docs/components-copybutton--docs) with `label` to copy a value.

_Example: story `Stories.IconButtonMatrix`._

## Variants and sizes

| Variant | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `secondary` | Default raised action. |
| `subtle` | Toolbars, rows and header controls. |
| `primary` | Emphasized actions, including the options beside a primary split action. |

| Size | Button | Icon |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `small` | 28px square, the default | 14px |
| `medium` | 32px square | 16px |

Pass the icon element with `icon`. IconButton sizes it and hides it from assistive technology; `label` provides the accessible name. `isSelected` applies the selected palette and `aria-pressed`. `isLoading` replaces the icon with a decorative spinner while retaining the label and focus.

_Example: story `Stories.InPlace`._

## Composition and accessibility

IconButton shares Button's native props, form behavior, refs and Base UI `render` support. The rendered component must forward props and refs to its DOM element. Use `nativeButton={false}` for a custom action that is not a native button. For navigation, use [LinkIconButton](?path=/docs/components-linkbutton--docs), never an IconButton that navigates from `onClick`: a real link can be opened in a new tab.

`disabledReason` works as on Button: the action is disabled but focusable with `aria-disabled`, and one tooltip shows the label and then the reason, on hover, focus and a tap. The reason is the button's accessible description. With `isTooltipDisabled` the label's tooltip goes, and the reason still shows alone. A reason that comes or goes while the button has focus leaves focus on it.

_Example: story `Stories.DisabledWithAReason`._

- The tooltip shows `label` on hover and when keyboard focus arrives. Escape closes it.
- Focus that comes back from a popup the button opened, a menu closed with Escape or by choosing a command, or a dialog closed, leaves the tooltip shut, so one Escape closes the menu and the next reaches whatever holds the button.
- A disclosure's content is not a popup, even inside a dialog, menu or listbox that also holds the button: focus that comes back from it, or from anywhere else in that surface, shows the tooltip.
- `isTooltipDisabled` suppresses the tooltip when a parent supplies one or the label is already visible; the accessible name remains.
- Tab reaches an enabled control; Enter and Space activate it. Disabled controls leave the normal tab order unless `disabledReason` or `focusableWhenDisabled` is set.
- Loading sets `aria-busy`, blocks activation and retains focus. An explicitly disabled control stays disabled.
- Keep sufficient space around compact controls; choose a larger labelled Button when a touch interaction needs a larger target.
- A row that sizes the button down to 20px keeps a hit area of at least 24px, centred on it, where any pointer is coarse; the row keeps its height.

_Example: story `Stories.InADenseRow`._

_Example: story `Stories.OpensAMenu`._

_Example: story `Stories.InADialog`._

## Props

_Props: generated from `IconButton`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

# Id

An identifier: CTRL-0412, AC-2(3), FND-2231, a hash. One typeface app-wide, so an Id inherits the font, the size and the colour of wherever it sits and adds only tabular numerals, which is what makes a column of ids line up. It is kept as a component for the semantics, and so every id in the product can be found. A code snippet is for code, which an id is not.

_Example: story `Stories.IdMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is                                                                                                             |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Id   | A span with tabular numerals. Nothing else: no fill, no face, no colour of its own.                                    |
| List | `Id.List`: a wrapping run of ids at `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`, `space.050` apart; or the `empty` word. |

## Variants

| Variant   | Use                                                                           |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Id`      | One id, in text, in a title, in a link, in a cell.                            |
| `Id.List` | Several ids: the controls a requirement traces to, the CCIs a package covers. |

Not built, and why: a monospace face (the old habit; the kit has one typeface and tabular numerals do the aligning); a copy button, because an id is selected like any word; a link inside the Id, because the link is outside it, a TextLink whose text is an Id.

## Sizes

None of its own. An Id is the size of its line: `font.body` in a sentence, `font.body.small` in a row, `font.heading` in a title. `Id.List` is `font.body.xsmall`, the size of a list of references.

_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

## States

None. An Id is text. The link around it hovers; the cell around it is selected; the Id does neither.

## Modifiers

- **`className`** for the colour or the size it takes from its place: `text-subtle` in a row's id column, `font-body-small` in a rail, `break-all` for a hash that must break anywhere.
- **List `empty`** for the word that stands where there are no ids; a muted dash by default.

## Content

- **The id as the record writes it:** "CTRL-0412", "AC-2(3)". Never a prose rendering ("Control 412", "AC 2.3").
- **One id per Id.** Several are an `Id.List`, never a comma-joined string.
- **A hash is an Id** too, with `break-all` so it wraps inside its column.
- **Subtle beside a name, default alone.** In a row the id column is `color.text.subtle` and the name is `color.text`; in a sentence the Id takes the sentence's colour.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                              |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Id      | Tabular numerals; the surrounding font, size and colour            |
| List    | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · `space.050` between ids |
| Empty   | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtlest`                          |

## Accessibility

- **An Id is text**, read as its characters. Nothing to focus, nothing to operate.
- **A screen reader spells an id as it reads it.** Punctuation inside it, the parentheses in AC-2(3), is read or skipped by the reader's own rules; the kit does not rewrite an id to help.
- **The colour is not the meaning.** An Id in `color.text.subtle` is an id; an Id in the link colour is a link, because a TextLink is around it.
- **`break-all` is for a hash**, so a long id never widens its column past the viewport.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Id`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Id.List

_Props: generated from `Id.List`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

- [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs), [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs): the id column.
- [PageHeader](?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs): the id above a title.

<!-- page: Components/Indicator (src/stories/components/Indicator.mdx) -->

# Indicator

A Dot with a word: severity or health beside a label, in a row or a rail. High, Medium, Low; Healthy, Degraded. Never a pill, so the status column stays the only pill in the row and the eye can tell the rank from the state. The Dot alone is a 6px circle in the tone's icon colour, tuned to read at small sizes, for a status in a spot too small for a word. A status indicator is usually an icon per state; this uses the Dot.

_Example: story `Stories.IndicatorMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is                                                                                                                |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dot  | 6px, round, `color.icon.<tone>`. It never shrinks.                                                                        |
| Word | `font.body` after the Dot, `space.075` away: `color.text`, or `color.text.subtle` when the tone is neutral. It truncates. |

## Variants

| Variant     | Use                                                                                                        |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Indicator` | Severity or health with its word: a column in a table, a fact in a rail.                                   |
| `Dot`       | The status alone: a cell 24px wide, a name in a tree, a mark in a timeline. With `label` it says its name. |

The tone is a rank, not a state: `danger` High, `warning` Medium, `neutral` Low, `success` Healthy, `information` Informational. Neutral mutes the word as well as the Dot, so a scale reads from loud to quiet. A record's state, Verified or Overdue, is a [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs).

Not built, and why: an icon per tone (failed, warning, in progress), because the Dot is the kit's one status mark and the word says the rest; a large Dot; an Indicator in a pill.

## Sizes

One size. The Dot is 6px whatever the text beside it; the word is `font.body`, the row's size, and in a `font.body.small` line it takes that size from the parent. An Indicator is as wide as its word and truncates when the column is narrower.

_Example: story `Stories.Truncation`._

## States

An Indicator has one state and does not hover, focus or disable. The tone is the whole variation.

_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

## Modifiers

- **`tone`** as in Variants; `neutral` when unsaid.
- **Dot `label`** for a Dot with no text beside it: the status as a word, spoken and not shown.
- **`className`** for placement, never for colour.

## Content

- **The word is the rank:** High, Medium, Low; Healthy, Degraded, Down. One word, two at most.
- **The same scale everywhere.** A severity is High, Medium or Low on every screen, never Critical on one and Severe on another.
- **A Dot's label is the same word** the Indicator would show: "Suspect", "Blocked".

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                         |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dot     | 6px · `color.icon.<tone>` · `color.icon.subtlest` at neutral                  |
| Word    | `font.body` · `color.text` · `color.text.subtle` at neutral · `space.075` gap |

The icon colours are Badge's, so a danger Dot and a danger Badge's text are one red, and the icon colour is the step tuned for a 6px mark.

## Accessibility

- **The word carries the rank**; the Dot reinforces it and is hidden from a screen reader, so "High" is read once.
- **A Dot alone is colour alone.** Give it `label`: it becomes an image named "Suspect", and the cell is no longer silent. Without a label it is hidden, which is right only when text beside it says the same thing.
- **Neutral is muted, not disabled.** `color.text.subtle` passes the contrast test; the gate runs every tone.
- **Nothing to focus.** An Indicator is a span in the row's reading order.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Indicator`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Dot

_Props: generated from `Dot`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Indicator takes a span's native props and a ref, Dot an svg's; each names itself last with `data-slot` (`indicator`, `dot`) and its `data-tone`.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

# Input

One line of free text, using shadcn's Base UI Input implementation with Ledger control styling. Labels and validation messages belong to Field.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Field invalid={invalid} required>
  <FieldLabel>Program name</FieldLabel>
  <Input name="program" value={name} onValueChange={setName} />
  <FieldDescription>As it appears on the authorization package.</FieldDescription>
  <FieldError errors={errors} />
</Field>
```

Inside a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) the Input takes the label, the hint and the error with no ids, and the Field's `invalid`, `required` and `disabled`.

_Example: story `Stories.BoundInField`._

Use `InputGroupInput` inside InputGroup when the field has addons. Input itself remains a single input element.

## Variants and states

`medium` is 32px; `small` is 28px beside toolbar actions. Native `type`, `inputMode`, `readOnly`, `disabled`, `maxLength` and form attributes retain their meanings. The layout sets width. Disabled controls leave the tab order; read-only values remain focusable and copyable.

Focus draws one continuous 2px edge over the field border, without a gap or a second ring. Invalid fields keep that edge in the error color. The field and its text stay in place when focus changes; InputGroup owns the edge when the input has addons.

_Example: story `Stories.InputMatrix`._
_Example: story `Stories.InField`._
_Example: story `Stories.Kinds`._

## Accessibility

In a Field the label, hint, error, invalid state and requirement reach the input without ids. Outside one, use a label with `htmlFor` and the input’s `id`, `aria-describedby` for hints, and `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` on the input. The Field's `required` only announces; native `required` on the Input is a browser and Base UI constraint. A placeholder gives an example and never replaces the label.

Native `onChange` remains supported. Search clearing and application shortcuts are caller-owned; Input does not install an Escape handler. Use an accessible InputGroupButton when a clear action is needed.

## Props

`InputProps` extends Base UI Input with Ledger's `size`. Refs and events target the native input; `render`, state callbacks for `className`/`style`, and `onValueChange(value, details)` are forwarded. A value change may be cancelled with `details.cancel()`.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeComposition`._
_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Related

[InputGroup](?path=/docs/components-inputgroup--docs) · [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs) · [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) · [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs) · [shadcn Input](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/input) · [Base UI Input](https://base-ui.com/react/components/input)

# InputGroup

Compose an input or textarea with icons, units and actions using shadcn's InputGroup parts. The group supplies the shared border and focus/invalid appearance.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Retention</FieldLabel>
  <InputGroup>
    <InputGroupInput type="number" defaultValue="90" />
    <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
      <InputGroupText>days</InputGroupText>
    </InputGroupAddon>
  </InputGroup>
</Field>
```

InputGroupInput inside a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) takes the label, hint and error with no ids, and the whole group draws the Field's invalid border.

_Example: story `Stories.BoundInField`._

Replace `leading` and `trailing` props with InputGroupAddon children. Replace a direct Input/Textarea child with InputGroupInput/InputGroupTextarea. Set width through native style or the surrounding layout.

## Variants and states

Addon alignment is `inline-start` (default), `inline-end`, `block-start` or `block-end`. Inline positions follow text direction. Block addons create a header or footer around the control. InputGroupButton supports `xs`, `sm`, `icon-xs` and `icon-sm`, with Ledger Button variants.

The actual input or textarea supplies focus, invalid, read-only and disabled surface states. Disabling an addon button does not disable or dim the editable field. Focused invalid groups keep their error border and a separate focus outline, matching Input and Textarea.

_Example: story `Stories.Units`._
_Example: story `Stories.Multiline`._
_Example: story `Stories.States`._

## Narrow

A keyboard hint, an InputGroupText holding a [Kbd](?path=/docs/components-kbd--docs), shows while the group is 256px or wider and steps aside below that, so the input keeps the room; units, prefixes and buttons stay at every width. A group with a hint measures itself as a size container, so give it a definite width (the layout's, `w-full` or a style width), not a shrink-to-fit parent. Squeezed narrower than its addons, the group clips them at its own edge and never paints over its neighbours, but the field is unusable at that width: a row that crowded takes the search as an icon button instead, as the [Shell's top nav](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs) does below `md` (see Don't).

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

## Accessibility

Label the control with Field or an explicit accessible name. Decorative icons use `aria-hidden`; explanatory text and actions remain available to assistive technology. Give icon buttons accessible names. Addon buttons are real keyboard stops and default to `type="button"`. Clicking non-interactive addon space focuses the input or textarea; custom click handlers can cancel this.

_Example: story `Stories.SearchBox`._

## Props

Group and Addon accept native div props and refs; Text accepts span props. Input and Textarea parts preserve their control contracts and refs. Button preserves Ledger Button's native Base UI composition, loading and disabled behavior. There are no configured content slots.

## Related

[Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs) · [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs) · [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs) · [shadcn InputGroup](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/input-group)

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

# Item

A compact record row with aligned identifiers, descriptions, dates and independent actions. Item retains Ledger's record-list layout; Base UI owns link composition and disclosure behavior.

## Anatomy

Item.Group renders an ordered list inside a div. Rows share a six-column grid: disclosure, leading mark, record id, title/body, trailing value and actions. Expanded content starts under the title. A group can supply its heading, count, trailing action and empty message.

_Example: story `Stories.Lists`._

## Variants and states

Use `link` to navigate, `onSelect` for an action, or neither for a plain row. `isActive` marks the selected record. A link takes precedence over onSelect. Secondary actions and disclosure buttons remain outside the title link/button.

`children` display below the row; add `isCollapsible` to fold them. Use `defaultOpen` or controlled `open` with Base UI's `onOpenChange(open, details)`. Call `details.cancel()` to reject a change.

Group `size="compact"` reduces vertical padding. `flush` extends separators and hover backgrounds to the card edges. `idWidth` defaults to 72px; align it across related rows.

_Example: story `Stories.ItemMatrix`._
_Example: story `Stories.Nested`._

## Accessibility

The title is a real anchor or button. Enter follows links; Space activates buttons. Disclosure buttons announce expanded state and reference the linked title's id. The chevron sits above the title's stretched link, so a click or a tap on it opens the row and never follows the link; where any pointer is coarse its hit area is 24px. Actions are independent tab stops. Plain rows stay out of the tab order unless the caller explicitly supplies tabIndex for programmatic focus.

A group title names the list. It is a heading at the contextual level: an h3 when nothing sets one, one below a titled Section, an h2 in a rail that starts its outline at 2 with `HeadingLevelProvider level={2}`. When a surrounding card or section already draws the heading, point `aria-labelledby` at it; with no visible heading, `aria-label` names the list. Both reach the `ol`, not the wrapper, and the group's own `title` wins over them. `labelledBy` is the deprecated name of `aria-labelledby`, kept for one version. A compact `empty` message is body text, not a heading.

_Example: story `Stories.GroupHeadingLevel`._

_Example: story `Stories.GroupNamedFromOutside`._

Keep link titles descriptive; meta and trailing values are separate from the link's accessible name.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeIntegration`._

## Props

_Props: generated from `Item`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `ItemGroup`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Item forwards native li attributes, styles, events and refs. Its existing `id`, `title` and `onSelect` props keep their record-content/action meanings. Item.Group forwards native div attributes and refs to the outer wrapper, except `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`, which name the list; its `title` remains the visible group heading. Each part names itself last with `data-slot` (`item`, `item-group`). Styles merge with the standalone row grid.

`link={<Link to="/record" />}` uses Base UI useRender to preserve the supplied link's attributes, ref, handlers and id. Leave the link empty to use Item's configured title. Explicit link children follow Base UI's rendered-element precedence. No router dependency is added.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._
_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._
