# TimeField

A time of day, typed, held and reported as an ISO time (`"17:30"`, the contract of `input type="time"`) and shown on the LedgerProvider locale's clock: "5:30 PM" in en-US, "17:30" in de-DE. It has no date and no zone.

Use it for a wall time that stands on its own: a daily stand-up, office hours, a reminder time. A moment (evidence collected, due at 5 PM on a day) is a [DateTimeField](?path=/docs/components-datetimefield--docs), which pairs this input with a day and names the zone. A duration ("90 minutes") is a number field, not a time.

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Start time</FieldLabel>
  <TimeField name="start" value={start} onValueChange={setStart} min="08:00" max="18:00" />
  <FieldDescription>Between 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM.</FieldDescription>
</Field>
```

_Example: story `Stories.TypedEntry`._

## Entry

The reader types on either clock and the field reads it on Tab or Enter: "5pm", "5:30 p", "17:30", "1730", "9.15 Uhr" in German, the locale's own day periods ("오후 5:30") and its digits. The field then shows the time on the locale's clock, or on `hourCycle` (`"h12"` or `"h23"`) where a product sets one clock. A time with no day period is read on the 24-hour clock, so "5:30" is 5:30 AM, shown as such.

Text that is not a time, or a time outside `min` and `max`, stays as typed, the field reports `""` and says what fixes it under itself ("Enter a time such as 5:30 PM.", "Enter 8:00 AM or later."). The message is a FieldError inside the Field, so it describes the input and marks the Field invalid; `onEntryError` receives it too. Escape puts back the last time.

## Stepping

The input is a spinbutton that also takes typing. Up and Down move by `step` minutes (15 by default) on that grid, so 5:07 goes up to 5:15; Page Up and Page Down move an hour; both stay within `min` and `max`, and wrap at midnight without them. From empty they start at the step nearest the reader's clock. Its value is the minutes since midnight with the time's words as `aria-valuetext`, so a screen reader hears "5:15 PM" as it changes.

_Example: story `Stories.Clocks`._

## Values and forms

Use `value` and `onValueChange` for controlled state or `defaultValue` for uncontrolled. A value that is not an ISO time warns once and is treated as empty. A hidden input carries the time under `name`; put `name` on the TimeField, not on the Field, whose control is the visible text. A native form reset restores an uncontrolled default.

## Accessibility

- Inside a Field it is the Field's control: the FieldLabel names it, and the hint, the error and the Field's `invalid`, `disabled` and `required` reach it. Outside one, give it `aria-label`.
- The clock icon is decorative; the input's name and value carry everything.
- Nothing is validated while the reader types; the entry is read when they leave it or press Enter.

_Example: story `Stories.TimeFieldMatrix`._

## Props

_Props: generated from `TimeField`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

<!-- page: Components/Timeline (src/stories/components/Timeline.mdx) -->

# Timeline

Events in order along one rail: a record's activity, a scope's history, an audit trail, a pipeline, a line of releases, a feed of what people did. Each event is a marker on the rail, what happened, who and when, and under it what the event carries: a sentence, a file, a note, two buttons. Vertical reads down, newest first, with sticky group labels over a week or a month; horizontal reads across, oldest first. The anatomy follows [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs): a row that opens is its title stretched over the row, and everything beside it is a separate stop.

A timeline is for events; things with a date are an Item list, and a fixed path with a current step is a [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.TimelineMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part        | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rail        | A hairline, `color.border`, through the centre of every marker. Each row draws its own piece of it in the marker column, so it runs from the first marker to the last whatever the rows hold and wherever the time sits.                                                                       |
| Marker      | On the rail, at the list's size: a bare Dot in the tone at `small`; a ring on `elevation.surface.raised` holding a Dot at `medium` and `large`. With `icon`, a disc in the tone with the icon on it (a check, a cross, a play). Anything the slot holds as `marker`: an Avatar for who did it. |
| Title       | What happened, `font.body` in `color.text`, one line unless the list says `wrap`; medium weight when emphasised. It may be a sentence: the name in medium weight, the verb subtle, the record as a link. On a row that opens, this is the link or button, stretched over the row.              |
| Time        | `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`, as the reader would say it, where the list puts it: at the end of the title's line, above the title as a dated line, first in the footer, or in a column before the rail. Across, above or below the marker. A `<time>` when `dateTime` is given.   |
| Meta        | Under the title, one line, `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`: who, and the kind.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Description | Under the meta, `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`, wrapping: what the event amounts to, in a sentence.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Body        | Under the description, `font.body`: the note, the diff, what was said; a file; two buttons; who is on it; a collapsible detail.                                                                                                                                                                |
| Footer      | The last line: Badges for the kind and the state, or who did it; the time first, when it sits below.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Trailing    | At the end of the title's line, beside the row's control: an unread Count, a chevron, a menu button.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Group       | A run of events under a sticky Eyebrow with a count, on the current surface and on the title's column; the rail runs to its edge.                                                                                                                                                              |

## Variants

| Variant      | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vertical`   | The default. Reads down, newest first, the rail on the left: a feed, a history, a log, a pipeline. Groups live here.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `horizontal` | Reads across, oldest first, the rail on top: releases, a project's journey, a workflow's stages on a record header. `center`, the default, puts each marker mid-column with the time above, like a Stepper; `start` puts it at the column's start with the time below and the text under it, for stages with a body. |

A horizontal list is at least 420px wide; narrower than that it scrolls inside its container, with an arrow at each edge where a pointer can hover (the Narrow story).

Where the time sits, `timePosition` on the list:

| Position | Use                                                                                                                           |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `end`    | The default: at the end of the title's line. A history, an audit trail, anywhere the rows are one or two lines.               |
| `above`  | A dated line above the title: a log where the date is the point, and the rows carry a sentence and a file.                    |
| `below`  | First in the footer, with the kind and the state: a feed of people, where the title is who did what and the when is a detail. |
| `start`  | A column before the rail, on the title's line: releases by month, a changelog, where the reader scans the dates.              |

What a row does:

| The row        | Use                                                                                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Opens a record | `link` with the router's Link: the title is the link, stretched over the row.                    |
| Opens in place | `onSelect`: the title is a button over the row; `isActive` marks the event open beside the list. |
| Only reads     | Neither: a plain row.                                                                            |
| Is unread      | `emphasis`: the title in medium weight, and an unread mark in `trailing`.                        |

_Example: story `Stories.People`._

_Example: story `Stories.Log`._

Not built, and why: alternating sides, because the rail is a list, not a poster; a collapsed "show more", because the group's count says how many and the page scrolls; a rating on an event, because a rating is a record's fact, not an event's; markers in the accent hues, a colour per row to tell rows apart, because the marker's colour is the tone and a colour that says nothing is a colour the reader tries to read.

## Sizes

| Size     | Slot | Marker                                                  | Row                         | Where                                                                                  |
| -------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 16px | A bare 8px Dot; an `xsmall` Avatar; a 16px disc         | `space.050` above and below | A dense log, a changelog, a rail's recent activity.                                    |
| `medium` | 20px | A 12px ring with a Dot; an `xsmall` Avatar; a 20px disc | `space.075` above and below | The default: a record's history, an audit trail, a pipeline.                           |
| `large`  | 24px | A 16px ring with a Dot; a `small` Avatar; a 24px disc   | `space.100` above and below | A feed of people, where the avatar is the marker; a workflow's stages across a header. |

The size is the list's, not the row's: every marker in a list sits on the same rail. The title stays `font.body` at every size; what scales is the marker and the room around it. A vertical timeline is as wide as its container; in a rail it is the rail's width, on a record page a measure. A horizontal one gives each event an equal column, 420px in all at least, like a Stepper; in a scrolling area it can be as wide as its stages need.

_Example: story `Stories.Releases`._

_Example: story `Stories.Runs`._

_Example: story `Stories.Activity`._

## States

| State          | What changes                                                                                         |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain          | No hover. Text on the surface.                                                                       |
| Link or button | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` on hover across the row; the focus outline around the row. |
| Active         | `color.background.selected`, and its hovered step on hover: the event open beside the list.          |
| Emphasised     | The title medium: unread, or the current one.                                                        |

The feed in a Sheet, the count in its title, is the [In a sheet](?path=/story/components-timeline--in-a-sheet) story.

## Modifiers

- **`orientation`**, **`size`**, **`timePosition`** and, across, **`align`**, as in Variants and Sizes. All four are the list's, so every row agrees. **`wrap`**, also the list's, lets every title wrap: a feed whose sentences name a task or a file.
- **`tone`** colours the default marker's dot by the event's kind; **`icon`**, passed bare, turns the marker into a disc in the tone with the icon on it; **`marker`** replaces it.
- **`time`** as said, **`timeTitle`** as the full stamp on hover, **`dateTime`** as the machine stamp, which makes it a `<time>`.
- **`meta`** for who and the kind, one line; **`description`** for the sentence under it; **`children`** for what the event carries; **`footer`** for the Badges and the name last.
- **`link`**, **`onSelect`**, **`isActive`**, **`emphasis`**, **`trailing`** as in Variants.
- **Group `label`** and **`count`**; the label sticks to the top of the scrolling surface.
- **`label`** on the list names it: "Activity", "History", "Releases".

## Content

- **Newest first** down a page; oldest first across. The reader wants what just happened; the beginning is at the bottom.
- **The title says what happened**, in one line: "Verified", "Due date moved", "Evidence linked". As a sentence, who first: "Nadia Flores approved payout batch ACH-4182", the name in medium weight, the verb subtle, the record a link.
- **The meta says who and what changed**: "Dana Whitfield · 14 Sep → 18 Sep". **The description says why**, in one sentence.
- **The footer is the kind, then the state**: "Payout · Same day", "Risk · High". Or the name, when the title is the thing done: "Maya Brooks · Done".
- **The time matches its place**: "2h ago" and "Yesterday" at the end of the line or in the footer; "6 May 2026" above; "May 2025" in the column. The full stamp is the tooltip.
- **Group by period**: "This week", "August", "Earlier". A count on the group when there are more than a few.

## Style

| Element     | Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rail        | 1px · `color.border` · through the marker column's centre, each row its own piece, the first row's top and the last row's bottom hidden                                                                                                             |
| Marker      | slot 16, 20 or 24px · ring 12 or 16px `color.border` on `elevation.surface.raised` · Dot in the tone · disc the slot's size in `color.background.{tone}.bold` with a 12 or 16px icon in `color.text.inverse`, neutral in `color.background.neutral` |
| Row         | `space.050`, `space.075` or `space.100` block by size · `space.050` inline · `space.100` between marker and text · `space.150` between the time column and the marker · `radius.medium` when it clicks                                              |
| Across      | rail 1px `color.border` between markers, from the marker when start-aligned · time `space.050` above the marker or first under it · text `space.075` below · equal columns, 420px in all at least                                                   |
| Title       | `font.body` · `color.text` · medium when emphasised                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Time        | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular · right-aligned in the column                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Meta        | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · one line                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Description | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Footer      | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · `space.075` between its parts · `space.025` above                                                                                                                                                        |
| Group       | Eyebrow · on the title column · `space.050` below, `space.150` above after the first · `elevation.surface.current` behind                                                                                                                           |
| Hover       | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered`                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Active      | `color.background.selected` · `color.background.selected.hovered`                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Down the page the list is one CSS grid the rows share, time · marker · body, and each row a subgrid of it: the time column is as wide as its widest stamp, the marker column as wide as the size's slot, and the rail is drawn inside the marker column, so it is centred by construction.

## Accessibility

- **The list is an ordered list**, named by `label`, and every event an `li`; a group is an `li` holding a heading and its own list, labelled by the heading.
- **The title is the control.** A row that opens is a link or a button named by the title alone and stretched over the row; the time, the meta, the description and the footer are read as the text beside it. Nothing interactive sits inside it: the trailing slot, a file's download, a menu and the buttons in the body are their own stops beside it.
- **The time is a `<time>`** when `dateTime` is given, so the machine stamp travels with the words; the full stamp is the tooltip.
- **Tone is never alone.** The marker's colour says the kind; the title says what happened. A footer Badge says the state in a word.
- **An Avatar as the marker is decorative** when the name is in the title, so the name is read once.
- **A plain row is not focusable.**

## Props

_Props: generated from `Timeline`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Each part takes its element's native props, a `className` and a ref, and names itself last with `data-slot` (`timeline`, `timeline-group`, `timeline-item`): the list, the group's row and the event's row. Across, the list sits inside a scroller.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

# Toaster

Short feedback after an action. This family follows shadcn's Base UI Toast implementation, with Ledger surfaces, typography, motion and localized labels.

## Anatomy

Mount one Toaster near the application root. It composes ToastProvider, ToastPortal, ToastViewport and a stack of Toast / ToastContent / ToastTitle / ToastDescription / ToastAction / ToastClose parts. The default stack is at the bottom end edge, bounded on narrow screens.

```tsx
<Toaster />;
// After the provider mounts, from a workflow:
const id = toast.add({ title: "Evidence linked", type: "success" });
toast.update(id, { description: "Bank reconciliation, July" });
toast.close(id);
```

## Variants and states

Set `type` to success, info, warning, error or loading for the standard icons. Toaster defaults to a 4000ms timeout and four visible toasts. Set `timeout: 0` for persistent feedback. Application errors explicitly use 8000ms; the native manager does not infer timeouts from type.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

Supply `actionProps` with `children` and `onClick`. The action does not close automatically: call `close(id)` when it should dismiss. This lets an action update a toast or keep it visible while work continues.

_Example: story `Stories.WithAction`._

`promise` replaces loading feedback with the resolved or rejected result and returns a promise with the original value. Await or handle its rejection as usual.

_Example: story `Stories.Working`._

## Accessibility

Base UI owns announcements, timers, stack focus and swipe dismissal. F6 focuses the notification viewport; Shift+Tab from that viewport returns to the previous element. Hover and focus pause timers. Each default toast includes a localized Close button. Loading icons are decorative because the toast already announces the work.

Keep essential record state in persistent page content. Toast portals participate in Base UI popup accessibility, including while a dialog is open.

_Example: story `Stories.InDialog`._

## Props

Toaster accepts native Provider props: `children`, `timeout`, `limit` and `toastManager`. It is state-only and has no DOM ref. For custom placement or presentation, compose the exported parts; ToastViewport owns native div props/ref, direction and accessible name. Styled parts retain native `render`, refs and class/style state callbacks. `createToastManager` isolates stacks, and `useToastManager` reads the nearest provider's toasts and actions.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeOptions`._

Migration: replace `toast.success(message, options)` with `toast.add({ title: message, type: "success", ...options })`; use `close` instead of `dismiss`, `timeout` instead of `duration`, zero instead of Infinity, and `actionProps.children` instead of `action.label`. The callable Sonner adapter and Sonner Toaster options are removed. Independent stacks use separate managers. A manager must have a mounted provider before feedback can be shown.

## Related

[Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs), [Banner](?path=/docs/components-banner--docs), [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs), [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs).

Sources: [shadcn Toast](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/toast), [implementation](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/toast.tsx), [Base UI Toast](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toast).

<!-- page: Components/Toggle (src/stories/components/Toggle.mdx) -->

# Toggle

A two-state button built on Base UI with the shadcn composition API. Put icons and labels in `children`; give an icon-only toggle an `aria-label`.

```tsx
<Toggle aria-label="Bold">
  <Bold aria-hidden />
</Toggle>
```

_Example: story `Stories.ToggleMatrix`._

## Variants and state

`variant="default"` is unbordered; `variant="outline"` adds a border. Sizes are `sm` (28px), `default` (32px) and `lg` (36px). The default size is `default`.

Hover is the neutral tint. Pressed is the selected palette, `color.background.selected` with `color.text.selected`, and a 1px `color.border.selected` edge at 3:1 on that fill, so a pressed toggle never reads as a hovered one and its state does not rest on a faint fill. The default variant draws the edge out of the flow, so pressing never changes the toggle's size; the outline variant recolours its own border. In forced colours a pressed toggle is Highlight.

_Example: story `Stories.PressedAgainstHover`._

Use `defaultPressed` for local state, or `pressed` and `onPressedChange(pressed, details)` for controlled state. Calling `details.cancel()` rejects a change. `disabled` blocks activation and removes the toggle from the normal tab order.

Native attributes, event handlers and refs reach the button. `render` composes another action element; it must forward props and refs. Set `nativeButton={false}` for a non-button action. `className` and `style` accept callbacks with `{ pressed, disabled }`. `toggleVariants({ variant, size, className })` exposes the shared styling recipe.

## Accessibility

The native button reports `aria-pressed`. Enter and Space toggle it; Tab moves to the next control. Keep its name stable when the pressed state changes. Icons supplied as children should be decorative when the label already names the action.

For coordinated selection, use [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs). It provides one tab stop and arrow-key navigation among its items.

## Migration

Replace `icon={<Bold />}` with `<Bold aria-hidden />` inside the toggle. Size names are now `sm`, `default` and `lg`; use `sm` for a former 28px `small` toggle and `default` for a former 32px `medium` toggle. There is no 24px size preset. The appearance follows the shared shadcn toggle recipe rather than the previous recessed control.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Toggle`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs) · [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs) · [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs) · [Base UI Toggle](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toggle)

<!-- page: Components/ToggleGroup (src/stories/components/ToggleGroup.mdx) -->

# ToggleGroup

A group of toggle buttons with shared selection and keyboard navigation. Compose each choice with `ToggleGroupItem`, using a unique `value` and explicit children for its label, icon or count.

```tsx
<ToggleGroup aria-label="View" defaultValue={["table"]} variant="outline">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="table">Table</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="board">Board</ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
```

_Example: story `Stories.ToggleGroupMatrix`._

## Selection and layout

Selection is an array in both modes. By default, at most one item can be pressed; pressing it again clears the selection. Add `multiple` to allow several pressed items. A pressed item takes Toggle's pressed look, the selected fill with a 1px `color.border.selected` edge that follows a joined group's corners, so the current view never looks like a hovered one; in forced colours it is Highlight. `defaultValue` initializes local state; `value` and `onValueChange(values, details)` control it. Call `details.cancel()` to reject a change, such as clearing a required view.

Group `variant` and `size` pass to its items. Variants are `default` and `outline`; sizes are `sm` (28px), `default` (32px) and `lg` (36px). Default `spacing={2}` leaves an 8px gap; `spacing={0}` joins the items. `orientation="vertical"` stacks them and changes arrow navigation.

The group and items support native attributes, refs, `render`, and state callbacks for `className` and `style`. Use `disabled` on an item or the whole group to block selection.

_Example: story `Stories.ViewsStory`._

A spaced group wraps its items onto the next line when its row is too narrow for them, so every choice stays in view and in reach. A joined group, a group in a table cell and a group in a horizontal Scroller keep one line, and the table's frame or the Scroller scrolls. Put a joined group in a horizontal [Scroller](?path=/docs/components-scroller--docs) when its row can be narrower than its items.

_Example: story `Stories.NarrowRow`._

## Accessibility

- The root has `role="group"`; each item is a button with `aria-pressed`. Name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and give icon-only items an accessible name.
- Tab enters and leaves the group as one stop. Arrow keys move focus; Enter or Space changes selection. Disabled items are skipped.
- Horizontal arrows follow the Ledger locale direction; `dir` on the group overrides it. Vertical groups use Up and Down. Home and End reach the first and last enabled items.
- Focus wraps by default. Set `loopFocus={false}` to stop at the ends.
- Add [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs) explicitly when an icon needs a visible explanation.

## Migration

Replace `items` with `ToggleGroupItem` children, scalar `value` with an array, and `onChange` with `onValueChange`. The old required single-selection rule now belongs to the consumer: ignore or cancel an empty selection when one choice must remain active. `small` becomes `sm`; `medium` becomes `default`. Counts are explicit Count children, and icons are ordinary children. `isIconOnly` and automatic item tooltips are removed.

This uses the installed Base UI array API with `multiple`; it does not use Radix's `type="single"` or `type="multiple"` API.

## Props

_Props: generated from `ToggleGroup`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props: generated from `ToggleGroupItem`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[Toggle](?path=/docs/components-toggle--docs) · [Count](?path=/docs/components-count--docs) · [shadcn Toggle Group](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/toggle-group) · [Base UI Toggle Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toggle-group)

<!-- page: Components/Tooltip (src/stories/components/Tooltip.mdx) -->

# Tooltip

A supplementary visual label on hover or keyboard focus, using shadcn's Base UI composition. IconButton already draws one from its `label`; only compose a separate tooltip when its content differs, such as a keyboard shortcut.

```tsx
<TooltipProvider delay={300} timeout={300}>
  <Tooltip>
    <TooltipTrigger render={<IconButton label="Search" icon={<Search />} isTooltipDisabled />} />
    <TooltipContent>Search <Kbd>K</Kbd></TooltipContent>
  </Tooltip>
</TooltipProvider>
```

## Composition

Root owns open state. Trigger renders a button by default; `render` composes an existing button, link or span with its native props, handlers and ref. It does not give a rendered link or span button semantics, and has no `nativeButton` prop. A custom trigger must accept merged props and its ref.

Content includes the portal, positioner and decorative arrow. Native props, `ref`, `render`, and state callbacks for `className` and `style` target the popup. Placement defaults to top/center with `sideOffset={4}` and `alignOffset={0}`; those four positioning props belong on Content. Logical sides follow the Ledger locale or Content's explicit `dir`.

The surface retains Ledger's bold neutral fill, inverse text, small body text and spacing tokens. Its maximum width is 320px, constrained by available space; use native `style` to override it. The arrow uses Ledger's 8px size and small radius. Content stays inside an enclosing dialog's portal boundary so it remains visible and hoverable there.

_Example: story `Stories.TooltipMatrix`._

## Timing and interaction

TooltipProvider shares hover timing across a group. Its shadcn default is `delay={0}`; Base UI's `timeout` defaults to 400ms. Shell and Storybook explicitly use `delay={300}` and `timeout={300}` to preserve the product's timing. Without a provider, Base UI uses a 600ms trigger delay and no shared group; no local fallback provider is created.

Trigger accepts `delay`, `closeDelay` and `closeOnClick`. An adjacent tooltip opens immediately during the provider's timeout. Keyboard focus opens without the hover delay. Pointer passage into the popup keeps it open; leaving both, moving focus away, clicking the trigger or pressing Escape dismisses it. Trigger clicks close by default; `closeOnClick={false}` changes that behavior. Touch retains the trigger's action without opening a hover tooltip.

Use Root's `defaultOpen`, or controlled `open` with `onOpenChange(open, details)`. `details.cancel()` rejects a state change. Generic payloads let several triggers share one Root and provide content through its children function.

_Example: story `Stories.IconButtons`._

## Accessibility and disabled actions

Give the trigger its own accessible name and keep essential instructions visible. Base UI 1.7 does not automatically add `role="tooltip"` or `aria-describedby`; the popup is a visual supplement, not the control's accessible name or description. Keep controls and links out of the popup; use Popover for content the reader needs to interact with.

Trigger's `disabled` disables tooltip interaction; it does not disable the rendered button. Put the native `disabled` prop on the rendered Button. To explain an unavailable action on hover and keyboard focus, render a focusable span around its disabled button, and expose the reason independently in text or the wrapper's accessible name. The application uses this composition in UnavailableAction.

Inside a Dialog, Escape dismisses an open tooltip first while keeping focus on its trigger. A subsequent Escape can dismiss the dialog.

_Example: story `Stories.Unavailable`._

## Migration and API

Move `content` into TooltipContent, the old child trigger into `TooltipTrigger render`, timing onto Trigger or Provider, and placement/styles onto Content. The old 260px maximum and 6px offset become 320px and 4px, with an arrow. Remove redundant outer tooltips around IconButton; use `isTooltipDisabled` when composing custom content.

Props follow Base UI's [Provider](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip#provider), [Root](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip#root), [Trigger](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip#trigger) and [Popup](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip#popup), with the four positioning props added to Content. See [shadcn Tooltip](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/tooltip) for its source composition.

[IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs) · [Kbd](?path=/docs/components-kbd--docs) · [HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-hovercard--docs) · [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs) · [Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs)

# Tree

A hierarchy the reader opens and closes: control families, a system's composition, a folder of evidence. The caller owns the data, the open set and the selection and renders one row per visible node; the tree draws the indent guides, the chevron on rows that have children, and owns the keyboard: one tab stop, the arrows move and open, Enter selects. The ARIA tree pattern is the model.

A tree is for two or more levels. One level is a collapsible [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs) list; a hierarchy with columns is [Table.Tree](?path=/docs/components-table--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.TreeMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part     | What it is                                                                                                                              |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row      | One visible node, 32px (`small`) or 24px (`xsmall`), the tree item itself: focusable, selected on a click.                              |
| Guides   | One 16px column per ancestor level, a hairline down it while that ancestor's branch continues (`lines`).                                |
| Chevron  | On a branch: right while closed, down while open. A click on it opens or closes without selecting. A leaf has a small dot in its place. |
| Icon     | Optional, before the label, 16px: a folder for a branch, a document for a leaf. On every row, or on none.                               |
| Label    | `font.body` in `color.text`, one line. It is the row's accessible name.                                                                 |
| Trailing | At the end: a Count of what is beneath, a Badge for the row's state, a Dot.                                                             |

## Variants

Tree has one appearance. What varies:

| Variant    | Use                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Selectable | Rows with `onSelect` and one `isSelected`: the tree is a navigator, and the selected row is where the reader is. The composition browser, the families rail. |
| Read-only  | No `onSelect`: the tree only shows shape. Rare; a hierarchy worth drawing is usually worth opening.                                                          |
| With icons | An icon on every row, so labels at one level align; see Don't.                                                                                               |

Not built, and why: multi-select with checkboxes, because bulk work on nodes is a table; drag to reorder, because nothing here is rearranged by hand; a tree that owns its data, because the callers already flatten a tree with rolled-up posture on every row.

## Sizes

| Size     | Row  | Where                                                           |
| -------- | ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 32px | The default: a composition browser, a families rail.            |
| `xsmall` | 24px | A deep tree that must show more at once; a tree inside a panel. |

Rows stack with no space between them. The indent is 16px per level, the guide down its middle.

_Example: story `Stories.Families`._

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                   |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain    | Text on the surface.                                                                                                                           |
| Hover    | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` across the row.                                                                                      |
| Selected | `color.background.selected` and a 2px bar at the row's start edge in the selected colour (`color.background.selected.bold`, 3:1 on the fill); `aria-selected`. The row is the initial tab stop; focus can move independently. If its branch is closed, the parent shows the selection instead. In forced colours the row is Highlight. |
| Focus    | The focus outline around the row, on keyboard focus.                                                                                           |
| Open     | The chevron down; `aria-expanded="true"`; the children rendered under it by the caller.                                                        |
| Closed   | The chevron right; `aria-expanded="false"`; a Count in `trailing` says how many are beneath.                                                   |

## Modifiers

- **`depth`** and **`lines`**: how deep, and which ancestors' guides to draw. A last child under each ancestor clears that ancestor's line.
- **`hasChildren`**, **`isExpanded`**, **`onToggle`** on a branch; **`isSelected`**, **`onSelect`** on a selectable row. `expanded` is the deprecated name for `isExpanded` and is still read for one version.
- **`trailing`** for a Count, a Badge or a Dot. A button there is a tab stop of its own, outside the tree's keyboard model.
- **`size`** on the tree; **`label`** names it.

## Content

- **Branch labels say what kind of children they hold**: "Finance", "Payables", "Ground segment".
- **Leaf labels say what the node is**: "CTRL-0412 Segregation of duties", "mission-api:2.1.4".
- **Icons on every row or none**: a folder and a document, and nothing else.
- **The count beneath a closed branch goes in `trailing`**, so a closed tree still says how big it is.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row      | `dimension.control.medium` 32px `small` · `dimension.control.xsmall` 24px `xsmall` · `radius.medium` · `space.100` end padding · `space.075` between parts |
| Guide    | 16px column (`space.200`) · 1px `color.border`                                                                                                             |
| Chevron  | 20px · `color.icon.subtle`, `color.icon` on hover · `radius.small` · rotates in `motion.duration.fast`                                                     |
| Leaf dot | 4px · `color.background.neutral.pressed`                                                                                                                   |
| Label    | `font.body` · `color.text`                                                                                                                                 |
| Hover    | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered`                                                                                                                  |
| Selected | `color.background.selected` · a 2px (`space.025`) bar in `color.background.selected.bold` at the start edge, `space.050` from the top and bottom            |
| Focus    | The focus outline                                                                                                                                          |

The selected fill is the one a table row and a list row take, so a selection reads the same everywhere; the bar at the start edge is its second cue, because the fill alone is about 1.1:1 against the surface. A table row's selection is carried by its checkbox instead. In a right-to-left tree the bar sits on the right and a closed branch's chevron points left.

_Example: story `Stories.SelectedAndRightToLeft`._

The tree retains one entry tab stop as rows are selected, removed or collapsed. Typing a label prefix moves focus without selecting. Flat visible rows receive inferred `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize`; for partial or virtualized sibling sets, supply `posInSet` and `setSize` with the complete sibling position and count.

## Accessibility

- **It is a tree**: `role="tree"` named by `label`, every row a `treeitem` with `aria-level`, `aria-selected`, and `aria-expanded` on a branch: the ARIA pattern.
- **One entry tab stop per tree.** Initially the selected row is tabbable, or the first row when none is. Arrow navigation moves that tab stop without selecting; returning to the tree retains the last focused row. Removing that row restores focus to a preceding visible row when focus would otherwise be lost.
- **Keyboard:** Down and Up move between visible rows; Right opens a closed branch, or moves into an open one; Left closes an open branch, or moves to the parent; Home and End go to the ends; Enter or Space selects.
- **The chevron is for the pointer.** It focuses and toggles the branch without selecting it. It is hidden from the keyboard and screen readers, which have Right and Left. Where any pointer is coarse its hit area is 24px, centred on the 20px chevron.
- **Trailing controls are outside the model.** A button in `trailing` is its own tab stop; keep to a Count, a Badge or a Dot where the tree is long.
- **The selection is never hidden.** When the selected row's branch is closed, the caller selects the parent, so the reader does not lose their place.

_Example: story `Stories.Keyboard`._

Tree and Tree.Item accept native div attributes, styles, events and refs. Caller handlers run before their built-in handler; `preventDefault()` cancels that behavior. Use `onKeyDownCapture` on the root to reserve keys before row handling. Item’s `onSelect` is the existing node-selection callback, not the native text-selection event. Tree roles and row levels stay component-owned. An explicit `aria-label` overrides the root’s `label` shorthand; `posInSet`/`setSize` or native sibling metadata overrides inferred counts.

Embedded trees keep separate arrow navigation, typeahead and entry tab stops. Trailing controls keep their own actions and do not select the containing row.

_Example: story `Stories.NestedTrees`._

The keyboard behavior follows the [WAI-ARIA tree view pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/). Root refs compose through [Base UI useRender](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/use-render#merging-refs).

_Props: generated from `Tree`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

# Truncate

Text cut to one, two or three lines (`maxLines`, as on Text) with an ellipsis, and the whole of it in a tooltip while it is cut. The tooltip opens on hover, and on keyboard focus of the link or button the text sits in or of a control inside it, so a keyboard reader can see a long record name from the list. Nothing opens while the text fits. The full text never leaves the DOM, so a screen reader reads all of it; the tooltip is a visual copy and is hidden from assistive technology.

```tsx
<TextLink render={<Link to="/controls/ac-2" />}>
  <Truncate>Automated temporary and emergency account management</Truncate>
</TextLink>
```

_Example: story `Stories.TruncateMatrix`._

## When to use it

- **A name in a row, a rail or a list** that must stay on its line: a record name in a register, a value in a KeyValue, a title in a narrow panel. KeyValue and a clamped [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs) (`maxLines`) already reveal themselves; use Truncate where neither applies.
- **Not for a sentence.** A statement, an objective, an error or a notification wraps: give Text no `maxLines`, or KeyValue `wrap`. A tooltip is for a name that does not fit, not for reading.
- **Not for a heading.** A page, section or dialog title wraps.
- **An identifier or a hash** wraps anywhere rather than being cut, where the row allows it (KeyValue `wrap`).

## How it reveals

| The reader           | What happens                                                                                                           |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hovers the text      | The tooltip opens after the tooltip provider's delay, only while the text is cut.                                      |
| Tabs to its link     | A Truncate inside a link, button, tab, menu item, option or tree item opens as the host takes keyboard focus.          |
| Tabs into it         | A Truncate that holds a control (a TextLink in a KeyValue value) opens as the control takes keyboard focus.            |
| Presses Escape       | The tooltip closes; focus stays where it was.                                                                          |
| Taps it              | Nothing opens: a touch has no hover. Where the whole name matters on a phone, let the row open the record, or wrap.     |
| Uses a screen reader | The whole text is read in place. The tooltip is `aria-hidden`.                                                          |

A `title` of your own replaces the tooltip rather than stacking a second one on it. `fullText` sets what the tooltip says when the element's own text is not the words to show.

_Example: story `Stories.RevealsOnKeyboardFocus`._

## The element

A `span` set as a block by default. `render` makes it another element with its own props (`<dd />`, `<p />`), which keeps its own display; the one-line clamp needs a block or a flex item to cut. One line clips across only (`overflow-x: clip`), so a focus ring and a touch area inside it reach above and below the line; two and three lines clamp, which clips both ways.

_Example: story `Stories.RenderedAs`._

## useIsTruncated

`useIsTruncated(ref, { maxLines })` reports whether an element you truncate yourself is cut right now. It measures after every render and whenever the element resizes or its text changes, so it follows a panel opening or a column resizing. Use it for a decision that depends on the cut (showing a "Show more", say); Truncate itself measures when it is about to reveal and needs no hook.

_Example: story `Stories.UseIsTruncatedHook`._

## Accessibility

- **The text is all there.** Truncation is CSS; a screen reader reads the whole, and the tooltip is not announced twice.
- **Keyboard reaches it through the control it belongs to.** A plain truncated value with nothing focusable around it is not made a tab stop; where a keyboard reader needs it whole, wrap it.
- **Touch has no reveal.** A truncated name in a list is fine when the row opens the record; anything a phone reader must read whole wraps.
- **Right to left**, the ellipsis sits at the logical end (the RightToLeft story). Reduced motion removes the tooltip's fade.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Truncate`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

- [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs): the surface the reveal uses.

# Typography

The small text parts a record page is made of, beyond body copy and titles. `Eyebrow` is the uppercase micro-label on `font.heading.xxsmall`: a section's name in a rail, a record's kind above its title, a callout's label. `Absent` is the muted dash where a value would be, with a `label` a screen reader hears in its place. `Prose` is authored text: one paragraph or several, with the line breaks it was written with, a safe Markdown subset on request, under an optional Eyebrow label. For body copy and titles, the [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs) and [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) primitives; this page is the three parts between them.

_Example: story `Stories.TypographyMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                     |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Eyebrow | `font.heading.xxsmall`, uppercase, `color.text.subtle`; a tone colours it. A `div`, or the element `as` names. |
| Absent  | An em dash in `color.text.subtlest`, the size of its line. With `label`, the dash is `aria-hidden` and the label is [VisuallyHidden](?path=/docs/primitives-visuallyhidden--docs) text beside it. |
| Prose   | An optional Eyebrow, then the text in `font.body` (or `font.body.large` with `size="large"`) and `color.text`: `space.050` under the Eyebrow, `space.075` above a labelled Prose, `space.100` between paragraphs (`space.150` at large). |

## Variants

| Part    | Use                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Eyebrow | The name of a group of rows in a rail (`as="h3"`), the kind above a record's title, the label of a callout (with a tone), the label of a value in a grid (`as="dt"`). |
| Absent  | Any value that is not there: in a KeyValue, a Fact, a cell.                                                                                                           |
| Prose   | Authored text with or without a name: a rationale, an implementation statement, a control statement, a narrative. In a rail or a detail body.                         |

Not built, and why: a description-list primitive, because KeyValue and Fact are the two shapes of a pair; a "no data" word in place of the dash, because the dash is the product's one absent mark and reads in a column; an Eyebrow with an icon or a count, because it is a label and a count is a Count beside it.

## Sizes

One size each. The Eyebrow is `font.heading.xxsmall` whatever it heads; the Absent is its line's size; the Prose paragraph is `font.body`. A rail's Prose is as wide as the rail, a detail body's is the reading measure.

_Example: story `Stories.InRail`._

## Prose

A string is authored text. A blank line starts a paragraph, and a single line break stays in place, so a statement pasted from a document reads as it was written.

_Example: story `Stories.ProseParagraphs`._

`markdown` takes a safe subset: paragraphs; `-`, `*` and `1.` lists, nested by indentation; `*emphasis*` and `**strong**`; `` `inline code` `` and fenced code; `[links](https://…)` and `<https://…>`. Line breaks are kept. Anything else, headings, tables and HTML included, shows as the characters typed. The application renders its own markup (an OSCAL parameter insertion, say) on top of the text it passes in.

_Example: story `Stories.ProseMarkdown`._

Links render as TextLinks with native anchors; `renderLink` makes each one a router link, so the kit stays router-free.

_Example: story `Stories.ProseRouterLinks`._

_Example: story `Stories.AbsentLabelled`._

## States

None. The three are text. The tone on an Eyebrow or a Prose is a colour for a callout, not a state.

## Modifiers

- **Eyebrow `tone`** for a callout's label: `warning` over a condition, `danger` over a finding. `neutral`, the default, is `color.text.subtle`.
- **Eyebrow `as`**: `h3` or `h4` when it heads a section, so the page's outline has it; `dt` when it labels a value; `span` inline.
- **Prose `label`** and **`tone`**: the text's name, and its colour when it is a callout. Leave the label out under a heading of its own.
- **Prose children as a string** are authored text: a blank line starts a paragraph, and a line break stays a line break (`white-space: pre-line`). Composed inline content (words and a TextLink) is one paragraph.
- **Prose `markdown`** renders a safe subset in place of the children, and **`renderLink`** sends its links through a router's link element.
- **Prose `size`**: `medium` in a rail, `large` for reading text at the measure.
- **Absent `label`**: what a screen reader hears for the empty value, "Not recorded" or "None".

## Content

- **An eyebrow is one to three words**, a noun: "Schedule", "By supplier origin", "Rationale". Uppercase is set by the component; write it in sentence case.
- **Prose keeps the author's paragraphs.** Pass the text as written; do not split it into several Prose to get paragraphs, and do not add `<br>`s.
- **The dash means nothing here.** "N/A" means not applicable, "Unknown" means unknown; those are values and are written as words.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                     |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Eyebrow | `font.heading.xxsmall` · uppercase · `color.text.subtle` · `color.text.<tone>` when toned |
| Absent  | `color.text.subtlest` · the line's font                                                   |
| Prose   | `font.body` or `font.body.large` · `color.text` · `space.050` under the eyebrow · `space.075` above · `space.100` or `space.150` between paragraphs · inline code `font.code` on `elevation.surface.sunken` |

The eyebrow moved from `color.text.subtlest` to `color.text.subtle` in this walk: a label is secondary text, and the prototype had written forty-five of its own eyebrows in subtle against eight in subtlest. The Shell's section headings and the Preview eyebrow took the step with it.

## Accessibility

- **An eyebrow that heads a section is a heading**, with `as="h3"` or `h4`, so the page's outline lists it and a screen reader can jump to it. As a `div` it is a label and is read in place.
- **Uppercase is styling**, so a screen reader reads the words, not the letters; write the text in sentence case.
- **The dash alone is often silent.** Screen readers skip an em dash at their default punctuation level, so a value with nothing in it sounds like a skipped row. Give Absent a `label` ("Not recorded", "None") wherever the empty value matters: the dash is then hidden and the label is read in its place.
- **Prose Markdown injects no HTML.** The source is parsed into React elements; `<script>` and any other markup show as the characters typed. A link whose address is not http(s), mailto, tel or relative (a `javascript:` or `data:` address) shows as its words, not as a link. Links in Prose are underlined, so they are told apart from the text by more than colour.
- **Contrast:** `color.text.subtle` at 11px uppercase passes 4.5:1, and `color.text.subtlest` does for the dash; the gate runs every tone.

# PageHeader

One composable page header for collections and records. Two columns: Heading, what names the page, on the left; Actions on the right; Lead across both above them. Native header, heading, paragraph and div props and refs pass through every part.

_Example: story `Stories.Collection`._
_Example: story `Stories.Record`._
_Example: story `Stories.Constrained`._

Compose a Heading with a Title, an optional Lead and one primary action or Actions menu. A breadcrumb is the Lead through `render={<Breadcrumb />}`; a category line is a Lead with text. Record fields, owner/status editors and property strips belong in the work area or Aside, not in PageHeader or a preview header. Description is optional and wraps without hiding content behind a tooltip.

Use PageHeader.Title once for the page's h1. Actions sit at the end of the title's row while the row can give the title its measure (14rem) beside them; when it cannot, on a phone or in a narrow panel, they take the next row, right-aligned, and the title wraps at its full width. The same rule holds on a page, in a Shell.Panel and in a Sheet (the Stacked story). Keep action groups on one line; use a dropdown when several actions compete for space.

## Title levels

The Title is the h1 on a page. Inside a [HeadingLevelProvider](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) it takes that level instead: a preview's inner record header, in a panel or a sheet whose outline starts at 2, renders the record's name as an h2 with the same type style. The content after that header goes one level below through a HeadingLevelProvider without `level`, so its Sections are h3s. `render` sets the element outright, `render={<h2 />}`, or a sheet's or a dialog's own title part where the surface needs its title for its accessible name. Never copy the Title's classes onto a raw heading: a change to the title's style would miss it.

_Example: story `Stories.TitleLevels`._

No other part has props of its own: the root is a `header`, Heading and Actions are `div`s, Description a `p`, and Lead a `div` or the element given to `render`; each takes its element's native props and ref, and names itself last with `data-slot`. Title takes `render` and its element's props. Every part is also exported by name (`PageHeaderLead`, `PageHeaderHeading`, `PageHeaderTitle`, `PageHeaderDescription`, `PageHeaderActions`), the same component as the member.

_Props: generated from `PageHeader`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props: generated from `PageHeaderTitle`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
