<!-- page: Layout/Pages (src/stories/layout/Pages.mdx) -->

# Page composition

Mount the application shell once around the router outlet. Routes compose normal primitives and components inside Main and contribute optional Aside or Panel content. There are no collection-page or record-page wrapper APIs. A collection page is a PageHeader and a DataTable with `fill`, which takes the rest of the window, and `responsive`, which folds lower-priority fields into each row's More fields on a narrow screen instead of scrolling sideways, with a [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs) as its `toolbar`: the search first, filters, display controls such as Columns, and the one primary at the end. A tab whose only content is the collection starts with that Toolbar and table, with no heading or Section around it; see Register.

The record example brings the visual conventions together: an Actions menu beside the title, a descriptive method selector, a standard input, and inline status and owner editors. App and Storybook load Geist and Geist Mono. Select and Combobox share row spacing, persistent choice indicators and neutral keyboard highlights; descriptions grow the row instead of clipping.

_Example: story `Stories.Record`._
_Example: story `Stories.Register`._
_Example: story `Stories.QueueWithPanel`._
_Example: story `Stories.CompactQueue`._

## Regions and behavior

- **Main** contains the page header, filters, tabs and work area. Keep these visible controls in the route.
- **Aside** provides supporting context, such as properties. It follows Main below the `aside` breakpoint (`dimension.breakpoint.aside`, 75rem: 1200px at the default root size) and sits beside it above that. When a Panel is also open, Aside follows Main until the `wide` breakpoint (110rem, 1760px). The breakpoints are tokens; [Metrics](?path=/docs/tokens-metrics--docs) lists them.
- **Panel** holds a selected record or task. From the `panel` breakpoint (80rem, 1280px) it is a resizable column beside Main that runs the full height of the window; the banner and the top nav stop at its edge. Below that it replaces the visible work area under the top nav while Main stays mounted. Close or Escape returns focus to the opener when it still exists.
- **Sheet** is the modal surface for a workflow that needs focus containment. Compose it with the existing Base UI components.

A route contributes at most one Aside and one Panel. Their portal destinations remain stable across route updates. Route React context travels with the contribution, and unmounting the route removes it. Slots appear after mounting; server rendering does not render portaled region content. The application restores its browser workspace before rendering routes.

## Tabs and accessibility

Keep each tab's primary content inside its TabsContent. Supporting context is a separate labelled landmark and is conditional on the selected tab. Give pages one h1, panels an h2, and contextual regions meaningful names. Avoid placing modal semantics on a panel that leaves global navigation available.

The examples test route cleanup, retained context, tab relationships, queue state, resizing and focus return. Their example route buttons use a horizontal Scroller, so keyboard focus brings each route into view without widening the page on a phone. Responsive behavior is also checked in the application.

## Extending

Compose a new route from Stack, Inline, Grid, PageHeader and the controls it needs. Add a pattern when a repeated interaction earns one—for example record selection, coordinated filtering, or calendar scheduling. Layout ownership stays in Shell.

<!-- page: Layout/PageSkeleton (src/stories/layout/PageSkeleton.mdx) -->

# PageSkeleton

What a screen looks like before its data arrives: a title and a line, a tab strip, then a table's worth of rows, in the [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs)'s shapes. The router shows it for every route that is still loading, so it is the shape most pages share, an index. A page loads progressively; a section that loads on its own draws its own Skeleton inside a page that has already landed.

_Example: story `Stories.PageSkeletonMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is                                                                                     |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Head | A heading shape 240px wide and a line 440px wide, where a PageHeader's title and line will be. |
| Tabs | Four short lines over a rule, where a Tabs strip or a filter row will be.                      |
| Rows | `rows` lines of a table: an id, a title that fills, two values; `space.200` apart.             |

## Variants

One skeleton. Not built, and why: a record variant with a facts strip and a rail, because the router shows one skeleton before it knows the route's shape, and a record's first paint lands within the same 150ms; per-section skeletons, because those are the sections' own, drawn from Skeleton where they load.

## Sizes

`rows` sets how many rows to draw, 8 by default, about a screen at the register's row height. The skeleton is as wide as the page.

## States

One state: waiting. The whole is a `status` region marked busy and named "Loading", so a screen reader hears one announcement and not a hundred grey bars.

## Modifiers

- **`rows`** as in Sizes.

## Content

- **The shape of an index.** A page that is not one still lands on the same title line, so the swap is small.
- **Shown after 150ms**: the router's pending delay, so a fast route never flashes it.
- **Never beside content.** It replaces the page; a section that loads later draws its own.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                             |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Head    | Skeleton heading and line · `space.150` between                                   |
| Tabs    | four Skeleton lines · `space.250` apart · `color.border` rule · `space.150` under |
| Rows    | Skeleton lines · `space.200` between rows and cells                               |
| Layout  | `space.300` between the three parts                                               |

## Accessibility

- **A `role="status"` marked `aria-busy`** and named "Loading", so the wait is announced once.
- **The bars are hidden**; the region carries the meaning.
- **Reduced motion stops the pulse**; the shapes stay.

## Props

_Props: generated from `PageSkeleton`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs): the shapes it is drawn from.
- [Pages](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs): the index it stands in for.
- [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs): a wait on an action, not a page.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

The head's lines are at most 240px and 440px and follow the page's width below that, so the skeleton never scrolls a phone sideways (the Narrow story).

<!-- page: Layout/Section (src/stories/layout/Section.mdx) -->

# Section

Optional presentation for a titled content region. `title`, `count`, `description` and `action` render the built-in header; leave `title` out and compose Section.Header, Section.Heading, Section.Title, Section.Description and Section.Actions yourself when the heading needs a badge or two actions. The Title names the region either way. Native section props and refs pass through every part. A rule is opt-in with `divided`.

_Example: story `Stories.Presentation`._
_Example: story `Stories.Composed`._
_Example: story `Stories.Untitled`._

The header wraps by its own width, not the window's, so it behaves the same on a page, in a Shell.Panel and in a Sheet. The Heading keeps a readable measure of about 12rem, or its own width when shorter, and grows; when the row cannot hold that beside the Actions, the Actions take the next row, at the end, and the title keeps its words whole. A short title keeps its action on its row even in a narrow panel.

_Example: story `Stories.InANarrowPanel`._

## Heading levels

A Section's title takes the contextual heading level and its content one level below, so the outline follows the nesting without a level at every call site:

- On a page, where nothing sets a level, the title is an h2 under the PageHeader's h1, and a Section inside it is an h3.
- In a titled Shell.Panel the body starts at 3, under the panel's h2; in a panel with no title (a preview, whose record title is the body's first heading) it starts at 2. The panel starts its own outline wherever in the route it is rendered from (the In a titled panel and In a preview panel stories).
- Under a record title in a preview or a dialog, wrap the content after the header in a [HeadingLevelProvider](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) so its Sections sit one below the title.
- `Section.Title render={<h4 />}` still sets an element outright. An untitled Section changes nothing.

_Example: story `Stories.Nested`._

## Collapsible

`isCollapsible` folds the content under the title: the collapsed Details section for provenance, counts and derivation a reader opens when they need them. The title and its count become a button inside the heading, a chevron after them turns while the content is open, and the action stays in the header, outside the heading. It is closed until `defaultOpen`, or controlled with `open` and `onOpenChange`. Closed content stays mounted and hidden until found, so a draft inside survives and find-in-page opens it. It needs `title`; compose a [CollapsibleHeader](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs) for a disclosure that is not a Section.

_Example: story `Stories.Collapsible`._

Use it where a page body has a block the reader may not need. Do not build one from a subtle Button with a ChevronDown or a native `<details>`: neither is in the heading outline, and neither chevron turns. In a rail of facts, the collapsed group is [Inspector.Group](?path=/docs/patterns-inspector--docs) with `defaultOpen={false}`.

Use Stack or Grid directly when no titled region is needed. Section imposes no distinction between work, reference, forms or narrative.

## Accessibility

- A titled Section is a region named by its title. Untitled, it is a plain container, and `aria-labelledby` never points at a title that is not there.
- The level follows the outline, as above; check a new composition with a heading list, which should read as a map of the page.
- A collapsible Section's button carries `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` while the content is open; Enter and Space toggle it and focus stays on it. The chevron is decoration and holds still under reduced motion.

_Props: generated from `Section`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `Section.Header`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Heading, Description and Actions take only their element's native props; Title takes `render` for another element.

<!-- page: Layout/Shell (src/stories/layout/Shell.mdx) -->

# Shell

The persistent application frame, inspired by [Atlassian's navigation layout](https://atlassian.design/components/navigation-system/layout/). It owns navigation, page gutters, responsive placement and panel scrolling. Product code supplies navigation links and route content.

_Example: story `Stories.Frame`._
_Example: story `Stories.ComposedPanel`._

Mount Shell once in a shared router layout. Place Banner, TopNav, SideNav and Main there. Child routes render Shell.Aside or Shell.Panel to contribute to the frame's stable region slots. Contributions preserve route React context and disappear when their route unmounts. They mount on the client after slot destinations exist.

Every part renders one element and forwards its native props and its ref to it; AppLogo, Profile, SideNav.Item and Panel.Title take Base UI `render` where the element may change, so Profile is a menu's trigger through `render` and a side nav item is a router link. The SideNav.ToggleButton is a child of TopNav.Start and places itself; TopNav.Search goes in TopNav.Middle and opens the product's [SearchDialog](?path=/docs/patterns-searchdialog--docs); TopNav.End is a named group that renders its children as given, and its TopNav.Item children fold into one More menu when the top nav is narrow (see the end slot below).

Aside contains supporting context. Panel contains dismissible selected-record or task content. With `title` (and `actions`) it renders its built-in header, close and resizer; without them compose Panel.Header, Panel.Title, Panel.Actions, Panel.Close, Panel.Body and Panel.Splitter yourself, as Composed panel shows, to change the heading's level, the labels or the padding. Panel.onClose is required either way and the Title names the landmark. From the `panel` breakpoint (`dimension.breakpoint.panel`, 80rem: 1280px at the default root size; see [Metrics](?path=/docs/tokens-metrics--docs)) the panel is the last column for the whole height of the window: the banner and the top nav stop at its edge, so opening it narrows everything and covers nothing. Below it the panel replaces the visible Main area under the top nav while retaining Main's state. Global navigation remains available; use Sheet for modal work.

The panel's focus contract holds at every width. When it opens while focus is on the page, on its opener or nowhere, focus moves into it (the labelled `aside`, or the element `initialFocus` names), so Escape and the next keys act in the preview; `initialFocus={false}` leaves focus where it is while Main is still visible beside the panel. When it closes with focus inside, focus returns to the control the reader last used in Main: the opener, or another row's eye pressed while the panel was open; `finalFocus` names another element, or `false` leaves it to the caller. Escape closes the panel unless it comes from a field inside it (a text input, a textarea, a select or an editable region), where it belongs to the field. See Panel focus.

_Example: story `Stories.PanelFocus`._

Every default name (Banner, Top navigation, Side navigation, Main content, Page context, Details, Actions, Search, More, Switch product, the toggle's two labels, the splitters' and the skip links') is a locale message, so a product translates them once with `LedgerLocaleProvider`; a `label` prop overrides one instance. The splitters take the arrow keys, Home for the minimum and End for the maximum. Left and Right move the handle in that physical direction, including right-to-left layouts. Restored widths retain the reader’s desktop preference: the current desktop layout caps them (see Main's minimum width below), and opening the shell on a phone does not overwrite that preference. Navigation still uses its 90vw overlay limit on phones.

_Example: story `Stories.PersistedWidths`._
_Example: story `Stories.RightToLeftSplitters`._

Main uses document scrolling; Panel scrolls inside the available viewport. A register that is the page fills the rest of the window with DataTable `fill`: Main publishes its bottom inset as `--shell-inset-bottom`, and the layout otherwise owns placement, so content patterns do not add sticky rails or nested page frames.

Set `collapsedSideNav="icons"` on Shell to keep a 56px navigation rail when collapsed on desktop. The default, `"hidden"`, hides the side nav and retains the hover flyout. Supply meaningful icons for top-level items and expandable groups. In icon mode, destination names remain accessible and appear in tooltips on hover or focus; the active destination and profile avatar remain visible. Section headings and nested destinations are visually hidden. Custom SideNav.Header content, such as navigation search, is hidden in the rail and returns when expanded. Activating an expandable group expands the shell and opens that group. Hovering the toggle does not open a flyout in this mode. With the default app mark, the collapsed expand control occupies the mark’s existing position and appears on hover or keyboard focus. The mark is visible at rest, and the product name keeps its position through collapse and expansion. Phone navigation keeps its separate visible toggle. The splitter returns with the remembered width when expanded, and phone navigation continues to use the existing overlay. `shellScript` and `shellScriptFor` preserve the compact rail before hydration when collapse state is stored. See [Icon rail](?path=/story/layout-shell-icon-rail--desktop) for keyboard, RTL, phone and first-paint examples.

`Shell.Panel.actions` places route-owned controls immediately before Close in the built-in header. Collection previews compose `Panel.Header`, `Panel.Actions` and `Panel.Close` for a navigation-only outer bar: previous/next through the displayed rows, a native full-record link and, for nested frames, Back. Put the visible record name and domain commands in a `PageHeader` at the beginning of `Panel.Body`, using an h2 and `PageHeader.Actions`. Give the panel an accessible `label` when its outer bar has no `Panel.Title`. The route owns row order, destinations and endpoint availability; Shell only supplies placement. The Record header narrow story exercises both headers at the minimum panel width.

## Main's minimum width

However the side nav and the panel are sized, Main keeps room for its content: one list column (`dimension.layout.list`) inside its desktop gutters (`space.300` each side), 388px with the default tokens. Each area is capped at half the viewport as before, and also where Main would fall under that minimum. The splitters stop there, and `aria-valuemax` says where, so End is the widest the area can be now. A remembered or default width that no longer fits is narrowed by the layout, not rewritten: when the panel opens beside a wide side nav, the panel's column gives way first, down to its own 240px minimum, and the side nav is capped so that the three always fit without a sideways scroll. The panel's column still opens and closes on the standard curve.

_Example: story `Stories.MainMinimum`._

## Page changes

Give Shell the router's location as `locationKey` (a pathname or a route id) and it handles a client-side page change at every width, without importing a router: it closes the phone overlay or the desktop flyout, moves focus to Main without scrolling, and announces the page's title through the [Announcer](?path=/docs/components-announcer--docs) it mounts. Focus stays where it is when it is on a control in the page that survived the change, such as a pager or a next-record link. Focus in a menu or a dialog outside the shell, such as a command palette, follows the popup's own return: when it hands focus back to its trigger in the top nav, or drops it, the shell takes it on to Main. The title is `document.title`, read once the new page has rendered, else Main's first h1; `getPageTitle` chooses other words or returns null to say nothing. Pass a key that changes with the page and not with a tab or a filter that writes to the URL, or a tab click would move focus to Main. Without `locationKey` the shell does none of this.

```tsx
const { pathname } = useLocation();
<Shell locationKey={pathname}>…</Shell>;
```

_Example: story `Stories.PageChange`._

On a phone, choosing a link in the side nav closes the overlay and moves focus to Main even without `locationKey`, so the reader lands on the page they chose; a click that opens a new tab or window leaves it open. Set `closeOnNavigate={false}` on SideNav for links that change the page in place and should keep the overlay open; a change of `locationKey` still closes it. Any other close from inside the overlay (`useSideNav().collapse()`, Escape, the scrim) returns focus to the toggle, since the overlay stops accepting input as it closes. `onCollapse` reports a close caused by a page change with the trigger `"navigation"`.

_Example: story `Stories.PageChangePhone`._
_Example: story `Stories.DestinationPhone`._
_Example: story `Stories.KeepOpenPhone`._

See [page composition](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs) for route and tab examples.

### The end slot at narrow widths

`TopNav.End` never shrinks, so what it holds decides the top nav's width. Give each action or destination as a `TopNav.Item` (an icon, a `label`, and `onClick`, or `href` or a router link through `render` for a destination). When the top nav is narrower than 48rem, measured on the row itself so that a panel open beside it counts, the items leave the row for one More menu at End's end: the same icons and names, in the row's order, a destination still a link and an item with a `disabledReason` still saying why. Anything in End that is not an item stays in the row at every width, and so does an item marked `persistent`: keep the colour mode's ModeSwitch as a plain child, since a toggle group cannot become a menu row. An item that opens its own menu or popover is `persistent` and is the trigger through the trigger's `render` (`<DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Shell.TopNav.Item persistent … />} />`), since its popup anchors to the button in the row; an item forwards its native props and its ref to that button, so the trigger's wiring reaches it. Narrowed while an item has focus, focus moves to More, which now holds it, never to a persistent item beside it; widened while More has focus, it moves back to the first item that left. Budget the persistent children for the narrowest window the product serves.

The fold reads the top nav's own width because the top nav is a size container (`container-type: inline-size`, named `topnav`). Inside Shell its width comes from the grid; a top nav placed outside a Shell needs a width from its parent, as a block or a stretched flex item, because it no longer takes one from its contents.

_Example: story `Stories.EndItemsFold`._

`overflow` is the older, all-or-nothing spelling: below the `md` breakpoint one menu of the product's stands in for every child, the colour mode included (the Record rail at 390px story). Items inside an End with `overflow` never fold; `overflow` still decides.

```tsx
<Shell.TopNav.End>
  <ModeSwitch />
  <Shell.TopNav.Item icon={<CircleHelp />} label="Help" onClick={openHelp} />
  <Shell.TopNav.Item icon={<Bell />} label="My work" render={<Link to="/work" />} />
  <Shell.TopNav.Item icon={<Settings />} label="Settings" onClick={openSettings} />
</Shell.TopNav.End>
```

### The search

`TopNav.Search` is the top nav's way into the product's [SearchDialog](?path=/docs/patterns-searchdialog--docs). In a top nav at least 48rem wide it is a field-shaped button that reads its `label` and shows the shortcut's keys; narrower, a Search icon button with the label in its tooltip, so the middle slot never squeezes a field under the create action. Both are one button to assistive technology, named by `label`, with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-keyshortcuts`, and both call `onOpen`. So does the shortcut, ⌘K on Apple platforms and Ctrl+K elsewhere (`shortcut`, `null` for none), from anywhere on the page; it ignores a held key's repeats, other modifiers and text still being composed, and does nothing while a dialog is open, so it never stacks a second dialog over a draft. The search is a button, not a text field: there is one search surface, the dialog, and nothing typed is lost when the row changes width. When the row narrows while the field has focus, focus moves to the icon. One key opens one dialog: `useCommandPalette` also binds ⌘K, and its shortcut cannot be changed, so a page with both gives TopNav.Search another `shortcut`, or `shortcut={null}`.

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
<Shell.TopNav.Middle>
  <Shell.TopNav.Search label="Search records" onOpen={() => setOpen(true)} />
</Shell.TopNav.Middle>;
<SearchDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} results={records} onSelect={openRecord} />;
```

The [Search at 320px](?path=/story/layout-shell--narrow-search) story shows the row at a phone's width: the toggle, the switcher, the mark, Search, Create and More in one row.

_Example: story `Stories.SearchShortcut`._

### Narrow panel headers

Panel header slots respond to the panel container, including a manually resized desktop panel. Below 400px, a title with actions occupies a full row and navigation/Close share the row beneath; title-only headers keep Close beside the title. A PageHeader inside the panel follows its own rule: its actions take the row under the title when the row cannot hold the title's measure beside them. The normal desktop header remains one row. See the 240px, 320px and 640px Panel header stories, composed-slot forwarding and Panel record header examples.

<!-- page: Layout/Shell/Icon rail (src/stories/layout/ShellIconRail.mdx) -->

# Shell icon rail

Set `collapsedSideNav="icons"` on Shell to retain destination icons, the active destination and the profile avatar in a 56px rail on desktop. Names remain accessible and appear in tooltips on hover or focus. Activating an expandable group restores the full navigation and opens its children. The default collapsed mode remains `"hidden"`. With the default app mark, the collapsed expand control occupies the mark’s existing position and appears on hover or keyboard focus. The mark is visible at rest, and the product name keeps its position through collapse and expansion. Phone navigation keeps its separate visible toggle.

_Example: story `Stories.Desktop`._

Expand and minimize animate the sidebar width over Ledger's moderate duration. The page follows the sidebar while the app mark stays fixed; resizing follows the pointer immediately. Reduced motion and restoring a remembered layout skip the transition.

_Example: story `Stories.WidthMotion`._

On phones, navigation slides in and out with a fading scrim, and returns focus to its toggle when dismissed. Choosing a destination in it closes it and moves focus to Main (see [Page changes](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs#page-changes)). Closing navigation stops accepting input immediately, and reversing the action continues from its current position. The rail does not take space from the page.

_Example: story `Stories.Mobile390`._

The RTL and persisted first-paint stories verify logical placement and restoration before hydration. See [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs) for composition, persistence, keyboard behavior and the complete API.

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Overview (src/stories/patterns/Chart.mdx) -->

# Chart

Data drawn on the chart tokens. `Chart` is the Frame: the figure that names a plot, keys it, holds its states, keeps the way back from a drill-down, and lays the same numbers out as a table one toggle away. Each kind of plot is its own part with its own page: [Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs), [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs), [Area](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-area--docs), [Donut](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-donut--docs), [Sparkline](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-sparkline--docs), [Scatter](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-scatter--docs), [Treemap](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-treemap--docs) and [Heatmap](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-heatmap--docs). Recharts draws; the kit decides the paint, the marks, the grid, the tooltip, the legend and the motion, so a chart reads like the rest of the page in both modes. The colour rules follow the data-visualization method, and the categorical order is validated, not eyeballed.

_Example: story `Stories.Framed`._

## Kinds

The data's job picks the kind, and sometimes the right kind is not a chart: one number is a [Stat](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs), one ratio against a limit is a [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs) bar, and more than seven classes that all carry meaning is a [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs).

| The reader must                            | Part                                                            | Colour job                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Compare sizes across categories            | [`Chart.Bar`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs)             | One hue; `horizontal` for long names    |
| See parts of each whole                    | `Chart.Bar` stacked                                             | Status tones, or the categorical set    |
| Read actual against planned                | `Chart.Bar` with `target`                                       | The series' tone; the target is ink     |
| See when things happen                     | `Chart.Bar` horizontal with `[from, to]` values                 | One hue                                 |
| Follow a trend                             | [`Chart.Line`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs)           | `brand`, or a tone per series           |
| Follow parts of a whole over time          | [`Chart.Area`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-area--docs) stacked   | Status tones, or the categorical set    |
| See one number against its whole           | [`Chart.Donut`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-donut--docs)         | The parts' tones on the track           |
| Read a score against a scale               | `Chart.Donut` `arc="half"`                                      | The tone the score earns                |
| See a trend beside a number                | [`Chart.Sparkline`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-sparkline--docs) | One tone                                |
| Place things on two measures               | [`Chart.Scatter`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-scatter--docs)     | `brand`, or at most three groups        |
| See how a total splits, and splits again   | [`Chart.Treemap`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-treemap--docs)     | The categorical set, one hue per branch |
| Read how much across two dimensions        | [`Chart.Heatmap`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-heatmap--docs)     | `sequential`: one hue, light to dark    |
| Read above and below across two dimensions | `Chart.Heatmap` `scale="diverging"`                             | Two hues around grey                    |
| Read status by place                       | `Chart.Heatmap` with a tone function                            | The Badge's fills, values printed       |

Not built, and why: no pie (a ring with the number in the middle says more, and a two-slice pie is a Stat); no second value axis (two measures of different scale are two charts, or one indexed; a dual axis invents a correlation); no gauge with a needle (the half ring reads the same and its number is text); no radar, boxplot, histogram, lollipop, alluvial, word cloud, circle pack or map (none of the four products has asked, and a histogram is a bar chart of bins the data layer makes); no zoom, brush or export toolbar (a range is a control in the Frame's `actions`, a drill-down is the Frame's `path`, and the chart's own export is one Download menu: the table twin as CSV and the plot as PNG; a register's export stays the register's).

## Anatomy

| Part        | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Title       | `font.body` medium in `color.text`, a noun phrase: what the chart shows. It names the plot to a screen reader.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Description | `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`, one line under the title: the period, the unit, the source.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Path        | A [Breadcrumb](?path=/docs/components-breadcrumb--docs) under the description while a drill-down is open: every level so far, every crumb but the last a way back.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Legend      | Swatch and label per series, `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`, at the end of the header. A square for a fill, a stroke for a line, a dot for a point. Present for two or more series; a single series needs none, the title names it. Unless the Frame is given `series`, it keys what the part draws: its series, a scatter's groups, a ring's slices, a treemap's branches. |
| Actions     | Controls at the end of the header: a range, a filter, a Retry. Then the tools: the Values toggle on a colour-scale Heatmap, the Table toggle, the Download menu (the table twin as CSV, the plot as PNG), the Expand button.                                                                                                                                                          |
| Plot        | The part's marks on a hairline grid. Ticks are `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtlest`; grid lines and the axis line are `color.border`, solid, 1px. Focusable when named, with the kit's focus ring on the keyboard only.                                                                                                                                                        |
| Tooltip     | The overlay surface. The category first, then every series at that point: the name, then the value in `font.body.small` medium, keyed by the mark's swatch. A stack adds its total.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Card        | The details on a chosen mark: a Popover anchored to it, the kit's head (swatch, name, category, value; or every series at a category), then whatever the caller adds.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Table       | The same numbers as a [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs), one toggle away, laid out by the kind: the category, then a column per series; a scatter's points, one row each; a ring's slices with their shares; a treemap's leaves, a column per level; a heatmap pivoted.                                                                                                     |

## Variants

| Variant                              | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Chart` (the Frame)                  | Every chart on a page. Title, description, legend, actions, the states, the path, the table twin, the legend's interaction.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `legend="top"`, `"bottom"`, `"none"` | The legend at the end of the header (the default for two or more series), under the plot when the header is busy, or nowhere for one series.                                                                                                                                             |
| `path`                               | The Frame of a drill-down: the levels so far as crumbs, the last being the current one.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `download`, `expandable`             | The tools: a Download menu with the table twin as CSV and the plot as a PNG at twice the pixel density; an Expand button that opens the same chart in a large Dialog, the plot redrawn at `large`.                                                                                       |
| `columns`                            | Columns for the table twin and the CSV beyond the series, each a key in the datum: a name beside the category (`place: "before"`), a total, a share, an owner after the series. Facts the plot does not draw, so the twin is the record's table and not only the plot's.                 |
| `syncId`                             | Charts that share their hover: small multiples, one hover across them, on one `domain`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `texture`                            | Every series wears a pattern as well as its colour, in the plot, the legend, the tooltip and the card.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Chart.Legend`                       | The key on its own, outside a Frame: beside a Donut, under a stacked bar. Inside a Frame it is the interactive one.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| The parts                            | One per kind, each on its own page. A part inside the Frame inherits its name, its formats, its size, its loading state and its legend's state; a Bar, Line or Area also its `data`, `x` and `series`. It tells the Frame what it draws, so the legend, the table and the CSV follow it. |

## Said once

Data, size and format are given once, to whichever holds them best. Given to the Frame, the part inside takes them when it sets none: a bare `<Chart.Bar />` draws the Frame's `data`, `x` and `series` at the Frame's `size`, in its `format`. Given to the part, the Frame learns them from it: its legend keys the part's series under the part's swatch (a stroke for a Line, a dot for a Scatter), and its table and CSV print the part's records in the part's format, so the plot, the tooltip and the table never disagree. The Frame's own props always win, and a part's own props win over what it inherits, except in the expanded Dialog, where every plot draws at `large`.

_Example: story `Stories.SaidOnce`._

The Frame follows the part it holds. When the part changes, the legend, the table and the CSV change with it; a series hidden from the legend stays hidden while its key is still drawn. When the caller puts something that is no part in its place, the legend and the Table toggle leave with the part rather than describe a plot that is gone. An empty or failed Frame keeps the last legend, so its header does not shift. One Frame holds one part.

_Example: story `Stories.FollowsItsPart`._

_Example: story `Stories.Drilldown`._
_Example: story `Stories.Details`._
_Example: story `Stories.Filtering`._
_Example: story `Stories.Linked`._
_Example: story `Stories.Downloads`._
_Example: story `Stories.Textured`._
_Example: story `Stories.Legends`._

## Sizes

| Size     | Height | Where                                                                         |
| -------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 120px  | A rail, a card in a grid of them, a cell of the matrix.                       |
| `medium` | 200px  | A Section. The default.                                                       |
| `large`  | 320px  | The one chart a page is about: the scatter of risks, the treemap of findings. |

The height is the whole plot, axis band included, so a card never scrolls inside itself. `height` takes pixels when a layout must. The Frame's states stand in at the same height, so nothing moves when the data arrives. A Donut and a Sparkline are sized in pixels, since they sit inline, and narrow to a container narrower than that; a Heatmap's `size` is its cell's height.

The width is the container's. Below about 480px the header wraps: the legend and the tools drop under the title, and the plot keeps its height. Reference and band labels move apart rather than overlap and stay within the plot's width, clear of the axis ticks, shortening with an ellipsis when the row is too short for them, and while a mark's details card is open the tooltip stands down, so on a phone the two never stack. An expanded chart is the same Frame at `large` in a Dialog, 860px at most, and the plot inside redraws at `large` whatever size it was given inline: 320px high, a ring 320px across at least, a heatmap's cells at 40px. Hidden series and the chart/table choice are shared with the original: expanding preserves them, and changes made in the dialog remain after it closes.

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

## States

| State      | What changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Hover      | The tooltip, for every series at that point; a hovered bar and a hovered slice take the tone's `hovered` step, a slice grows 2px, a line's marker appears. Synced charts show their tooltips together. A legend item under the mouse or keyboard focus dims the other series to `opacity.disabled`, faded over `motion.duration.fast`; a tap does not. |
| Isolated   | A clicked legend item hides its series; its swatch, a square or a stroke, hollows, and the series left are not dimmed for the one just hidden. Clicking the last visible one shows everything again.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Chosen     | A clicked mark, or the category Enter chose on the focused plot: the other marks dim, the card opens on it. Escape or a click outside closes the card and focus returns to the plot.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Loading    | The plot's own silhouette in `color.skeleton`, pulsing, at the plot's height: columns, a line, a ring, dots, tiles. The header stays.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Refreshing | The last plot stays, dimmed to `opacity.loading`, with a Spinner beside the title. For a refetch, so the reader keeps what they had.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Empty      | A dashed frame at the plot's height: "Nothing to show yet" and one line of why.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Error      | The same frame, the title in `color.text.danger`, and a Retry in `actions`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Table      | The Table toggle swaps the plot for the same numbers as a Table; the legend and the actions stay.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

_Example: story `Stories.States`._

## Modifiers

- **`legend`**, **`swatch`**, **`actions`**, **`state`**, **`statusTitle`**, **`statusText`** on the Frame. `state` is the word DataTable uses for the same thing (`ready`, `loading`, `empty`, `error`, and `refreshing` for a refetch that keeps the last plot); `status` is its deprecated name, which `ledger/no-deprecated-name` renames. The figure carries `data-slot="chart-frame"` and `data-state`.
- **`path`** on the Frame for a drill-down; each crumb's `onSelect` goes back.
- **`download`** (`["csv", "png"]`) and **`expandable`** for the tools; **`summary`** for the sentence a screen reader hears; **`syncId`** to share the hover; **`texture`** for the patterns.
- **`data`**, **`x`**, **`xLabel`** on the Frame, for the table, and for a Bar, Line or Area inside that is given none. Unsaid, the table takes the part's own.
- **`format`** and **`formatX`** for the numbers and the categories, set once on the Frame and inherited by the part, the tooltip, the card and the table. A part's own format wins in the plot, and the table follows it.
- **`size`** and **`height`** on the Frame, for the part that sets neither and for the states that stand in for the plot.
- On every part: **`label`** to name a plot outside a Frame, **`loading`** to draw its skeleton, **`onSelect`** to hear a choice, **`details`** to open a card on it. Each part's page lists its own.

## Choosing a mark

A chart that answers "what is this?" and "show me more" is the point of a platform's charts, and the kit does it one way everywhere:

- **`onSelect`** hears a choice: a bar, a point, a slice, a tile, a cell. It filters what is under the chart, or drills down.
- **`details`** opens a card on the choice: the kit renders its head (the swatch, the name, the category, the value; for a whole category, every series' value) and the caller renders the rest under it, facts and a way to the record. The card is a Popover anchored to the mark: Escape and a click outside close it, and focus returns to the plot.
- **A drill-down** is a Frame whose `path` grows: the click redraws the same plot one level down, the marks moving to their new places, and the path holds the way back. Two or three levels is the ceiling; past that the reader wants a table with filters.
- **The keyboard gets the same.** A named plot is focusable; the arrow keys move across the categories with the tooltip; Enter chooses the one under the tooltip. A Heatmap's cells are buttons and do it themselves.
- **A pointer over a mark that chooses is a pointer.** A plot with neither `onSelect` nor `details` shows the default cursor and no focus ring on a click, so nothing promises what it cannot do.

## Small multiples

Two measures of different scale, or more than six series, are several small charts, not one big one. The Frame makes them honest: give every chart the same `domain`, so a bar's height means the same thing on each, and the same `syncId`, so a hover on one shows the same category on all. A cumulative that needs its own scale says so in its description and keeps `baseline="auto"`.

## Textures

Colour is never the only channel, and in print, under colour-vision loss and in a forced-colours mode it is not a channel at all. `texture` on the Frame gives every series a pattern in its own colour, in a fixed order the legend and the tooltip repeat: the first series solid, then hatch, back-hatch, dots, cross, lines, columns. The pattern is the colour at 30% under 1.5px marks in the colour, 8px across, so the series still reads as its hue. Bars, areas and rings take it; a line's stroke stays solid, since a 2px line has no room for a pattern and its marker and end label already set it apart. Turn it on for a chart that will be printed or exported, or everywhere in a product that must meet a print or high-contrast requirement.

## Motion

Marks arrive once, over `motion.duration.slow` (400ms) on the standard curve: bars grow from the baseline, lines draw in, a ring sweeps round. A change of data moves the marks the same way, which is what makes a drill-down read as the same chart one level down rather than a new one. The tooltip follows the pointer over `motion.duration.fast`; a legend hover fades the other series over the same. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the marks draw in place and nothing fades. Nothing loops, nothing pulses but a skeleton, and no number counts up.

_Example: story `Stories.Motion`._

## Series and tones

Every series names a `color.chart.*` token through its `tone`. A status tone on a chart is data, the same rule as a Badge or a Stat, and a series that is not a status never wears one.

| Tone                                          | Use                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `information` | The series carries a status: satisfied, at risk, overdue, in progress.                                                   |
| `brand`                                       | The one series the reader is asked to look at.                                                                           |
| `neutral`                                     | Context: totals, the remainder, last period, the plan. Also a target line and Other.                                     |
| `categorical.1` to `categorical.6`            | Categories with no status, in this order: blue, orange, teal, red, purple, green. The default when a series has no tone. |
| `categorical.7`                               | Other: the fold for everything past the sixth. Grey.                                                                     |

The order is not cosmetic. It was chosen by enumerating every order of the six hues and keeping the ones whose neighbours stay apart under deutan and protan vision: the worst neighbouring pair sits at ΔE 12.7 in both modes, above the floor of 8, and the first three validate against each other in every pairing, which is why a Scatter takes three groups at most. Assign in order, never by rank: a filter that hides a series must not repaint the survivors. Past six, fold the tail into Other, split into small charts, or make a table; never a seventh hue.

Two more scales exist for a Heatmap: `color.chart.sequential.1` to `5`, blue from light to dark for how much; and `color.chart.diverging.negative.bold`, `negative`, `midpoint`, `positive`, `positive.bold`, red against blue around grey for above and below.

_Example: story `Stories.Emphasis`._

## Content

- **The title is a noun phrase**: "Coverage by control family", "Findings over time". Not a sentence, not a verb.
- **The description is the period, the unit or the source**, one line: "Opened in the month", "Sized by exposure in $K". While a drill-down is open it says the level: "Components of Payments".
- **A crumb is the level's name**: "All systems", then "Payments".
- **A series label is what the legend, the tooltip, the card and the table call it**: "Other than satisfied", not "other". Sentence case, no acronyms the reader would not say.
- **The numbers are formatted once**, on the Frame: grouped, two decimals at most, compact from ten thousand. A unit goes in `format`, so the axis, the tooltip, the labels, the card and the table agree.
- **A card's body is facts and one way onward**: two or three KeyValues and a button to the record. Not a form, not a second chart.
- **A reference says what it is**: "Target", "Limit", "Today", "Milestone C"; a date band says what happened in it: "Assessment window".
- **A summary is one sentence with the numbers in it**: "Open findings fell from 14 in January to 5 in September." A screen reader hears it after the description; nobody sees it.

## Style

| Element      | Token                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Series       | `color.chart.<tone>` · the same step in both modes                                                                                                   |
| Grid, axis   | `color.border` · 1px solid                                                                                                                           |
| Ticks        | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtlest` · tabular                                                                                                 |
| Axis titles  | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                                                             |
| Labels       | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular                                                                                                   |
| Tooltip      | `elevation.surface.overlay` · `color.border` · `radius.medium` · `elevation.shadow.overlay` · `space.150` inline, `space.100` block                  |
| Card         | `elevation.surface.overlay` · `color.border` · `radius.large` · `elevation.shadow.overlay` · `space.150` · 280px · the value in `font.heading.small` |
| Hover cursor | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` behind a bar · `color.border.bold` across a line chart                                                     |
| Reference    | `color.chart.<tone>` · 1px dashed 4 3 · label `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtlest`, above the plot for a vertical line                        |
| Hovered mark | `color.chart.<tone>.hovered`: one step darker in light, one lighter in dark                                                                          |
| Texture      | The series colour at 30% under 1.5px marks in the colour · 8px repeat · `radius` 2px on a swatch                                                     |
| Dimmed       | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                                                                                      |
| Refreshing   | `opacity.loading`                                                                                                                                    |
| Skeleton     | `color.skeleton` and `color.skeleton.subtle`, pulsing                                                                                                |
| Focus        | `color.border.focused` on the plot, keyboard only                                                                                                    |
| Motion       | `motion.duration.slow` on `motion.easing.standard` for the marks · `motion.duration.fast` for the tooltip and the dimming                            |

Every chart colour clears 3:1 on `elevation.surface` in both modes. Text never wears a chart colour: values, labels and legends stay in the text tokens, and a coloured mark beside them carries identity. The one place text sits on a chart colour is a status Heatmap cell, which is the Badge's fill and text, already in the contrast test.

## Accessibility

- **The Frame is a figure named by its title.** A screen reader hears "Coverage by control family, figure", then the description, then the path as a Breadcrumb, then the legend as a list of toggle buttons, then the plot.
- **The table is one toggle away, for everyone.** Every kind in a Frame lays the same numbers out as a Table when the Table toggle is pressed: a Bar, Line or Area by category, a Scatter by point, a Donut by slice with each share, a Treemap by leaf with every level, a Heatmap pivoted. The toggle is a toggle button whose name stays "Table" while `aria-pressed` says whether the table shows, so a voice command that says what the reader sees still works, and the plot's markup is not the only copy of the data. While the table shows, the part stays and draws nothing, so the table follows its data. The tooltip enhances; it never gates.
- **A colour-scale Heatmap's values are one press away.** In a Frame, a Values toggle prints them on their cells, for keyboard, touch and magnifier readers who cannot hover.
- **The plot is a group named by the title**, or by its own `label` outside a Frame. It is focusable, the arrow keys move the tooltip across the categories, and Enter chooses the one under it, opening its card when the plot has one. The focus ring shows on the keyboard, not on a click. A plot with no name is decoration: hidden from a screen reader and not focusable, so a sparkline beside a number says nothing twice.
- **The card is a dialog** named "[the plot's name], details"; focus moves into it and back to the plot when it closes; Escape closes it.
- **Loading says so.** A loading plot is `aria-busy` and named "[the plot's name], loading"; a refreshing one is `aria-busy` over the last plot.
- **A summary is the chart in a sentence.** With `summary`, the figure is described by it, so a screen reader hears the trend without walking the table.
- **Textures are the second channel.** With `texture`, a series is its colour and its pattern, in the plot and in the legend, so a stack reads in greyscale print and in a forced-colours mode where fills are flattened. The categorical order is still validated for colour vision; textures are the belt to that brace.
- **The tools are buttons.** Download is a menu of two items, Expand opens a Dialog that returns focus when it closes, and both are disabled while the plot is loading, empty or failed.
- **Colour is never the only channel.** Two or more series have a legend; a status series has its word in the legend, the tooltip and the table; a Heatmap's status cells print their value; a target is ink, not a hue; a gap in a line is a gap.
- **The categorical order is validated** for deutan and protan vision (Machado 2009, severity 1.0) and for normal vision, both modes. A Scatter's groups stop at three for the same reason.
- **Motion respects the reader.** Under reduced motion the marks draw in place and nothing fades.
- **The axe gate runs every kind's matrix** in both modes.

## Props

The Frame, `Chart`, accepts native figure attributes, events, styles and refs. `title` remains the visible chart title. Native DOM ids, refs and handlers belong to the original figure; expanding creates a separately named figure without duplicating those attributes or moving the caller's ref. Internal PNG export still reads the same figure.

# Area

A [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs) with a wash under it: the hue at 12%, so the plot says "how much" where a line alone says "which way". Stacked, the washes are parts of a whole over time, and the top edge is the total. Everything a Line takes, an Area takes; the difference is the fill and `stacked`. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame.

_Example: story `Stories.AreaMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part     | What it is                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line     | 2px in the series' tone, round joins, as on a Line.                                                                                                              |
| Wash     | The series' tone at 12% from the line to the baseline; in a stack, from the line to the series below. With `texture`, the series' pattern in its colour instead. |
| Marker   | 8px ringed, on hover, or on every point with `dots`.                                                                                                             |
| The rest | End labels, bands, references, gaps and axes as on a Line.                                                                                                       |

## Variants

| Variant                                                                                                      | Use                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One series                                                                                                   | A count whose size matters: open findings, month by month. The wash gives it weight.                     |
| `stacked`                                                                                                    | Parts of a whole over time: open and closed as parts of the month's total. The tooltip totals the stack. |
| `texture`                                                                                                    | Each wash its pattern: four assessors stacked read apart in print.                                       |
| `curve="smooth"`, `labels="end"`, `baseline="auto"`, `domain`, `scale="time"`, `delta`, `bands`, `reference` | As on a Line.                                                                                            |

_Example: story `Stories.Single`._
_Example: story `Stories.Stacked`._
_Example: story `Stories.Textured`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px (the default), `large` 320px, or `height` in pixels; unsaid, the Frame's, and `large` in the Frame's expanded Dialog. As on a Line, `data`, `x` and `series` may be left to the Frame, or given here and learned by it.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | A hairline across the plot at the category, a marker on every line there, the tooltip.                                                                                                  |
| Isolated | A series hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the plot; a stack closes up.                                                                                                             |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: a click in a category's column, or Enter on the focused plot, chooses it; the card opens on the point. On an unstacked area every series is ringed there. |
| Loading  | A skeleton line with a `color.skeleton.subtle` wash, pulsing, at the plot's height.                                                                                                     |
| Entering | The areas draw in over `motion.duration.slow`.                                                                                                                                          |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`stacked`** for parts of a whole; **`texture`** for the patterns.
- **`curve`**, **`dots`**, **`labels`**, **`baseline`**, **`bands`**, **`reference`**, **`connectNulls`**, **`xLabel`**, **`yLabel`**, **`format`**, **`formatX`**, **`onSelect`**, **`details`**, **`loading`**, **`label`** as on a Line.

## Content

- **Stack only parts of one whole.** Series that are not parts (three assessors' counts) are lines.
- **Two series that cross are lines**, not two washes: where washes overlap they mix into a colour on nobody's legend.
- **One series or a stack**; never several unstacked areas.
- The rest as on a Line: label the end, declare a cropped axis, keep a gap.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                             |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line     | `color.chart.<tone>` · 2px · round joins                                          |
| Wash     | `color.chart.<tone>` at 12% · or its pattern: the colour at 30% under 1.5px marks |
| Marker   | 8px · 2px `elevation.surface` ring                                                |
| Skeleton | `color.skeleton` path over a `color.skeleton.subtle` wash                         |
| The rest | As on a Line                                                                      |

## Accessibility

- **As a Line**: named by the Frame or `label`, focusable, arrow keys and Enter, the table one toggle away, a legend for two or more series, `aria-busy` while loading.
- **A stack's total is a column in the table**, since the top edge is the only place the plot shows it.
- **The wash is decoration**: the line carries the value, so a wash at 12% that fails 3:1 against the surface costs nothing.

# Bar

Bars per category: the size of each thing, compared. Several series sit side by side or stack into parts of a whole; a bar runs down the side when its name is long; a value that is a `[from, to]` pair floats, which is how a phase window is drawn. Simple, grouped, stacked, horizontal and bullet bar charts are all this one part; a histogram is a bar chart of bins the data layer makes. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame, which names it, keys it and lays it out as a table.

_Example: story `Stories.BarMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part         | What it is                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bar          | 24px thick at most, the data end rounded 2px and the baseline end square; `barCategoryGap` a quarter of the slot. Grouped bars sit 2px apart.                        |
| Segment      | In a stack, a part of the bar in its series' tone, with a 2px `elevation.surface` gap from the next, so the parts count.                                             |
| Floating bar | A `[from, to]` value: the bar starts at `from`. For windows in time.                                                                                                 |
| Negative bar | A value below zero hangs from the zero line, which is drawn in `color.border.bold`; its rounded end and its label are at the data end, below.                        |
| Texture      | With `texture`, each series' fill is its pattern in its colour; the first series stays solid.                                                                        |
| End label    | The value at the bar's end in `font.body.xsmall` and `color.text.subtle`, outside the bar. `labels="end"`, for a few bars and no stack.                              |
| Target       | A 2px mark in `color.text` across the bar at the datum's `target` value: actual reads against planned.                                                               |
| Line         | A series drawn as a 2px line over the bars on the same axis: a cumulative, a rate, a plan.                                                                           |
| Axes         | The category axis with a hairline; the value axis from zero, no line, ticks in `color.text.subtlest`. Titles in `color.text.subtle` when the keys do not say enough. |
| Tooltip      | The category, every series at it keyed by a square, and the total when stacked. A hovered bar lightens to 80%.                                                       |

## Variants

| Variant             | Use                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One series          | Findings by source. `brand` when the reader is asked to look, `neutral` when it is context. No legend; the title names it. |
| Grouped             | Two or three series side by side, in the categorical set. Past three the groups blur: stack, or emphasise one as a Line.   |
| `stacked`           | Parts of each whole, in the status tones or the categorical set. The tooltip totals them.                                  |
| `horizontal`        | Long names, or many categories: the names read whole down the side.                                                        |
| `target`            | A mark across each bar at its target: a bullet chart, without the qualitative bands.                                       |
| `[from, to]` values | Floating bars: phase windows, with `horizontal` and a `reference` for today.                                               |
| `line`              | One series as a line over the bars, on the same axis: closed against the plan.                                             |
| Below zero          | Variance, change, balance: the bars hang from the zero line. The axis reaches below zero on its own.                       |
| `domain`            | The value axis pinned, so charts side by side share a scale: small multiples.                                              |
| `texture`           | Patterns as well as colours, for print and colour-vision loss.                                                             |

_Example: story `Stories.Single`._
_Example: story `Stories.Grouped`._
_Example: story `Stories.Stacked`._
_Example: story `Stories.Horizontal`._
_Example: story `Stories.Targets`._
_Example: story `Stories.Windows`._
_Example: story `Stories.Combo`._
_Example: story `Stories.Negatives`._
_Example: story `Stories.Rates`._
_Example: story `Stories.Textured`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px (the default), `large` 320px, or `height` in pixels; unsaid, the Frame's, and `large` in the Frame's expanded Dialog. A bar never grows past 24px however wide the plot; the slots grow instead, so a wide chart of four bars still reads as four bars and not four slabs. A horizontal chart gives its category axis the width its longest name needs, to 160px, and cuts the rest with the whole name in a title.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The tooltip for the category; a `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` band behind the slot; the bar under the pointer in its tone's `hovered` step (a textured bar at 85%). Synced charts hover together. |
| Isolated | A series hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the plot; the others keep their places.                                                                                                                        |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: the bars take the pointer, a click on one chooses it and the other categories dim; Enter on the focused plot chooses the category under the tooltip. The card opens on the bar. |
| Loading  | Eight skeleton columns on a hairline, pulsing, at the plot's height; five skeleton bars when `horizontal`.                                                                                                    |
| Entering | The bars grow from the baseline over `motion.duration.slow`; a change of data moves them.                                                                                                                     |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`stacked`**, **`horizontal`**, **`labels="end"`**, **`target`**, **`line`** as in Variants.
- **`xLabel`**, **`yLabel`** print axis titles: the unit on the value axis when the title does not say it.
- **`domain`** pins the value axis, `[0, "auto"]` when unsaid; a value below zero extends it on its own. **`texture`** and **`syncId`** as on the Frame. A series' own **`format`** wins over the plot's in the tooltip, the card and the table: a fraction printed as a percentage.
- **`reference`** draws dashed lines: a target across every bar, a milestone on the category axis, labelled at the end. A `y` reference on a horizontal chart is a vertical line, labelled above the plot.
- **`format`**, **`formatX`** for the numbers and the categories, inherited from the Frame; the Frame's table prints the plot's.
- **`data`**, **`x`**, **`series`**: Inside a Frame, `data`, `x` and `series` may be left to the Frame, and the Frame learns them from the part when they are given here instead: say them once, to either.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ datum, series?, index }`, and `series` is absent when Enter chose the whole category.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.
- **`label`** names the plot outside a Frame.

## Content

- **Categories are short**: a code, a name, a month. A long name goes down the side with `horizontal`.
- **Print a value only at the end** of a few unstacked bars. A stack's parts are the tooltip's and the table's.
- **A target is a fact about the datum**, in its own key, not a series: the mark is ink.
- **The value axis starts at zero.** A bar's length is its meaning; there is no `baseline="auto"` here on purpose. Below zero is allowed, and the zero line is drawn, because a negative bar's length still means something.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                                                      |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bar       | `color.chart.<tone>` · 24px at most · `radius` 2px at the data end · hover in `color.chart.<tone>.hovered` |
| Zero line | `color.border.bold` · 1px                                                                                  |
| Texture   | The colour at 30% under 1.5px marks · 8px repeat                                                           |
| Stack gap | 2px `elevation.surface`                                                                                    |
| Group gap | 2px                                                                                                        |
| End label | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular · 4px off the end                                       |
| Target    | `color.text` · 2px · 24px across                                                                           |
| Line      | `color.chart.<tone>` · 2px · round joins · a ringed 8px marker on hover                                    |
| Cursor    | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` behind the slot                                                  |
| Dimmed    | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                                            |
| Skeleton  | `color.skeleton` columns on a `color.border` hairline                                                      |

## Accessibility

- **Named by the Frame**, or by `label`: the plot is a group, focusable, and the arrow keys move the tooltip across the categories. Enter chooses the category when the plot has `onSelect` or `details`; the card that opens is a dialog, and focus returns to the plot after.
- **The table is the other copy** of the same numbers, one toggle away in the Frame; a stack's parts and its total are columns there.
- **A status series says its status** in the legend, the tooltip and the table; the tone reinforces.
- **The target is a mark in ink**, not a colour, so it reads under every vision.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the plot's name], loading".
- **`texture` gives a stack a second channel**, so its parts read in print and where fills are flattened.
