# Donut

A ring of slices on a `color.chart.track`, with a number in the middle: one number against its whole, the parts around it. Half a ring is a gauge, a score against a scale with the number at its base. It sits inline, sized in pixels, beside a Stat or in a tile, and scales down in a narrower container; in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame it inherits the name and the legend's interaction. There is no pie: the number in the middle is what a pie could not say, and a ring of two slices for one number is a Stat.

_Example: story `Stories.DonutMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Track   | The full ring in `color.chart.track`, under the slices, so a single slice reads against its whole.                                                                                                |
| Slice   | An arc in its tone, clockwise from the top, with a 2px `elevation.surface` gap from the next. A hovered slice grows 2px and takes its tone's `hovered` step; with `texture` it wears its pattern. |
| Label   | The number in the middle, `font.heading.xsmall` in `color.text`: the total, the share, the one that matters.                                                                                      |
| Caption | One word under the number in `font.body.xsmall` and `color.text.subtle`: what it counts.                                                                                                          |
| Tooltip | The slice's name and value, keyed by a square.                                                                                                                                                    |
| Card    | On a chosen slice: the slice, its value and its share of the whole, then the caller's facts.                                                                                                      |

## Variants

| Variant       | Use                                                                                                                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Ring          | Parts of a whole with the whole in the middle: coverage, with the satisfied share printed.                         |
| One slice     | One value against its whole: 62% assessed, the rest the track. The slice's tone is the value's status, or `brand`. |
| `arc="half"`  | A gauge: a score from 0 to 100, the number at the base, the slice in the tone the score earns.                     |
| Beside a Stat | The ring at 120 with its legend as a `Chart.Legend`, the Stat carrying the words.                                  |

_Example: story `Stories.BesideStat`._
_Example: story `Stories.Gauge`._

## Sizes

| `size` | `thickness` | Where                                                   |
| ------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| 64     | 8           | A cell, a list row, a card's corner: done against left. |
| 120    | 12          | Beside a Stat. The default.                             |
| 160    | 16          | A tile of its own, with a number and a caption inside.  |
| 200    | 20          | A gauge that is a section's point.                      |

A gauge is half as tall as it is wide, plus 4px for the base. The label fits inside a ring of 120 or more; at 64 the number sits beside it.

`size` is the most a ring takes. In a container narrower than that, a block, a grid tile or a flex row, the ring scales down with its thickness and keeps its ratio, as an image does; the number and the caption keep their type size. In a Frame's expanded Dialog the ring draws at 320px across at least, the `large` plot's height, its thickness in proportion.

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                             |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The slice grows 2px outward; the tooltip.                                                                                                |
| Isolated | A slice hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the ring; the others keep their angles and the track shows through.                        |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: the slices take the pointer, a click chooses one and the others dim; the card opens at the slice's middle. |
| Loading  | A skeleton ring at the size and thickness, pulsing.                                                                                      |
| Entering | The slices sweep round from the top over `motion.duration.slow`.                                                                         |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

In a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame the ring needs nothing repeated: the Frame's legend keys its slices, a hover dims the others and a click hides one, and its Table toggle lays them out, a row per slice with its value and its share of the whole, headed by the Frame's `xLabel`. A slice hidden from the legend leaves the ring and stays in the table, which is the data.

_Example: story `Stories.Framed`._

## Modifiers

- **`arc="half"`** for the gauge; **`size`** (the largest diameter) and **`thickness`** in pixels; **`texture`** for the patterns.
- **`label`** and **`caption`** for the middle.
- **`format`** for the tooltip, the card and the Frame's table. The Frame's, else the kit's.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ slice, share, index }`.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.
- **`name`** names the ring outside a Frame.

## Content

- **Four slices at most, five with Other.** Past that the angles stop reading; the data is a Bar.
- **The number in the middle is the point**: the share, the total, the score. The slices explain it.
- **A caption is one word**: "satisfied", "open", "posture".
- **Slices in status tones when they are statuses**, the categorical set when they are kinds, and the remainder always `neutral`.
- **A gauge's slice wears the tone its score earns**: `success` past the target, `warning` near it, `danger` below.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                           |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Track    | `color.chart.track`                                                                             |
| Slice    | `color.chart.<tone>` · 2px `elevation.surface` gap · hover +2px in `color.chart.<tone>.hovered` |
| Label    | `font.heading.xsmall` · `color.text`                                                            |
| Caption  | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle`                                                        |
| Dimmed   | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                                 |
| Skeleton | `color.skeleton` ring                                                                           |

## Accessibility

- **Named by `name` or the Frame**, the ring is a group and focusable; unnamed it is decoration beside its Stat, hidden from a screen reader so the number reads once.
- **The number is text**, in the middle, not drawn: a screen reader reads it, and it never wears a chart colour.
- **The legend carries the names**; a slice's tone reinforces its word. Beside a Stat, the legend is a `Chart.Legend`.
- **The table is one toggle away** in a Frame: every slice with its value and its share, so the angles are never the only way to read the parts.
- **A chosen slice's card is a dialog**, and focus returns to the ring when it closes. The slices themselves are not buttons, so a filter the ring drives is also a control on the page.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the ring's name], loading".

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Heatmap (src/stories/patterns/ChartHeatmap.mdx) -->

# Heatmap

A grid of rows by columns with a value painted in each cell: how much, across two dimensions. One hue from light to dark for a magnitude; two hues around grey for above and below; or the status tones by place, which is the risk matrix. It is a table, in the markup as on the page, so a screen reader reads it as one and the keyboard walks it. `Chart.Scale` is its key. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame.

_Example: story `Stories.HeatmapMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cell    | `radius.xsmall`, 2px from its neighbours, its fill the value's step on the scale; `color.background.neutral.subtle` when there is no value.                                       |
| Value   | Printed in the cell on a status scale (the tone's text on its fill); on a colour scale a screen-reader-only text, or with `showValues` the number on an `elevation.surface` chip. |
| Headers | Column names across the top, row names down the side, in `font.body.xsmall` and `font.body.small`; the corner names the rows.                                                     |
| Scale   | `Chart.Scale`: the five steps in a row with the ends named, and the midpoint's word on a diverging one. Under the grid, `space.150` away.                                         |
| Tooltip | The cell's title: row, column, value.                                                                                                                                             |
| Card    | On a chosen cell: the row and column, the value, then the caller's facts.                                                                                                         |

## Variants

| Variant              | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scale="sequential"` | How much: findings by family and month, in `color.chart.sequential.1` to `5`. The default.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `scale="diverging"`  | Above and below a `midpoint`: schedule variance in days, red below and blue above around grey.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| A tone function      | Status by place: the risk matrix, each cell the tone its position earns, the count printed.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `showValues`         | The value printed on a colour scale too, when the reader must read every cell: on a surface chip in `color.text`, since text never sits on a chart colour. Unsaid, a Frame around the grid offers the reader a Values toggle that prints them; `false` offers none. |

_Example: story `Stories.Sequential`._
_Example: story `Stories.Diverging`._
_Example: story `Stories.Status`._

## Sizes

| `size`   | Cell height | Where                                                         |
| -------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 24px        | Many rows: families by month in a rail.                       |
| `medium` | 32px        | A Section. The default.                                       |
| `large`  | 40px        | A five-by-five matrix that is a page's point, values printed. |

A cell is at least 40px wide; the grid scrolls sideways inside its own box past the width it has. In a Frame's expanded Dialog the cells are `large`.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                         |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The cell's title as a tooltip.                                                                                                                       |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details` the cells are buttons: a click or Enter chooses one, it takes the focus ring, the others dim, and the card opens on it. |
| Loading  | Every cell in `color.skeleton`, pulsing, at the grid's size.                                                                                         |
| Isolated | Not applicable: a heatmap has no series to hide.                                                                                                     |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`scale`**, **`domain`**, **`midpoint`**, **`showValues`** as in Variants.
- **`rowLabel`**, **`columnLabel`** name the dimensions: the corner cell, and what a screen reader hears.
- **`format`** for the values, the tooltip, the card and the Frame's table. The Frame's, else the kit's.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ row, column, value }`.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton. The Frame does not set it: a grid's shape is its own.
- **`label`** is required: the grid is a table and needs a name.

## Content

- **A magnitude is one hue.** Never a status tone for a count: nine findings is not "danger".
- **Diverging needs a true midpoint**: zero variance, the plan, last year. Without one the data is sequential.
- **Status by place prints its count**: the tone's text on the tone's fill is the Badge's, already in the contrast test.
- **Name the dimensions**: "Likelihood" by "Impact", "Family" by "Month".
- **The scale's ends are words**: "0" and "12 findings"; "−12 days", "On plan", "+12 days".

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Cell     | `color.chart.sequential.<step>` · `color.chart.diverging.<step>` · or `color.background.<tone>` with `color.text.<tone>` · `radius.xsmall` · 2px apart |
| Empty    | `color.background.neutral.subtle`                                                                                                                      |
| Headers  | `font.body.xsmall` medium `color.text.subtlest` across · `font.body.small` `color.text.subtle` down                                                    |
| Scale    | Five steps 24 by 8 · `radius.xsmall` · ends in `font.body.xsmall` `color.text.subtlest`                                                                |
| Chosen   | `color.border.focused` outline                                                                                                                         |
| Dimmed   | `opacity.disabled`                                                                                                                                     |
| Skeleton | `color.skeleton`                                                                                                                                       |

## Accessibility

- **It is a table**: a `table` named by `label`, column headers across and row headers down, the corner naming the rows and, for a screen reader, the columns ("Likelihood by Impact"). A screen reader reads each cell as "row, column, value".
- **Every cell has its value in text**: printed on a status scale, screen-reader-only on a colour scale, so the colour is never the only channel.
- **A colour scale's values are one press away** in a Frame: Values, a toggle button whose name stays "Values" while `aria-pressed` says whether they show, prints every value on its cell for keyboard, touch and magnifier readers alike. The reader's choice holds across the table view and the expanded Dialog.
- **The table twin is the grid pivoted**: the Frame's Table toggle and CSV lay it out as a row per row and a column per column, headed by `rowLabel`, every value printed and no colour.
- **Cells that choose are buttons**, focusable in reading order, with the kit's focus ring; a chosen one says `aria-pressed`. The card is a dialog and focus returns to the cell when it closes.
- **The scale is `aria-hidden`**: its ends are text, and the values are in the cells.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the grid's name], loading".

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Line (src/stories/patterns/ChartLine.mdx) -->

# Line

A line per series over an ordered axis: a trend, a burndown, one measure against its plan. Two pixels wide with round joins, a ringed marker on hover, the last value printed after the line when asked. Straight segments by default, because the points are what was counted; a smooth curve never overshoots them. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame, which names it, keys it and lays it out as a table.

_Example: story `Stories.LineMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line      | 2px in the series' tone, round caps and joins. `curve="smooth"` is a monotone curve through the same points.                                                                                                                                       |
| Marker    | 8px across, ringed 2px in the surface so it reads over the line. On hover always; on every point with `dots`.                                                                                                                                      |
| End label | The series' last value after its line, `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`; labels that would collide are pushed apart by a line's height.                                                                                                   |
| Gap       | A missing value breaks the line. `connectNulls` joins across it, for a gap that is not data.                                                                                                                                                       |
| Band      | A 10% wash between two values (the tolerable range, labelled at its top edge) or between two categories or dates (an assessment window, labelled above its middle).                                                                                |
| Reference | A dashed hairline at a value (a target, a limit) or at a category (a milestone), labelled at the end or above the plot.                                                                                                                            |
| Axes      | The category axis with a hairline, or a time axis whose ticks are hours, days, months or years by the span; the value axis from zero, cropped to the data with `baseline="auto"`, or pinned with `domain`. A value below zero draws the zero line. |
| Tooltip   | The category, every series at it keyed by a stroke, and with `delta` each change from the point before. The cursor is a `color.border.bold` hairline across the plot.                                                                              |
| Chosen    | The chosen category ringed on every line, in each series' tone.                                                                                                                                                                                    |

## Variants

| Variant              | Use                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain                | Two or three series, each a tone. Findings open and closed.                                                             |
| `curve="smooth"`     | A few points that are readings of one continuous thing. Never for counts that jump.                                     |
| `dots`               | A marker on every point, when each point is an event and there are few of them.                                         |
| `labels="end"`       | The last value after each line: the number the reader takes away. The default for a trend in a Frame.                   |
| `baseline="auto"`    | The value axis cropped to the data: a cumulative in the hundreds where the slope is the story. The description says so. |
| `bands`, `reference` | A burndown: the tolerable range as a band, the limit in `danger`, a milestone on the category axis.                     |
| Emphasis             | One series in `brand`, the rest in `neutral`: the honest answer to "make this clearer".                                 |
| `scale="time"`       | `x` holds dates: the points are spaced by time, the ticks pick their unit, and a band or a reference takes a date.      |
| `domain`             | The value axis pinned, so charts side by side share a scale: small multiples, with `syncId` for one hover.              |
| `delta`              | Each series' change from the point before, in the tooltip and the card.                                                 |

_Example: story `Stories.Lines`._
_Example: story `Stories.Smooth`._
_Example: story `Stories.Burndown`._
_Example: story `Stories.Cropped`._
_Example: story `Stories.Gaps`._
_Example: story `Stories.Dates`._
_Example: story `Stories.Deltas`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px (the default), `large` 320px, or `height` in pixels; unsaid, the Frame's, and `large` in the Frame's expanded Dialog. Category ticks thin themselves to what fits, keeping the first; a time axis draws at most eight ticks, each at a unit's start; the right margin grows by 44px for end labels.

The labels above the plot share one row: where a milestone's and a window's would overlap in a narrow plot, they move apart, the milestone's staying closest to its line, and milestones on one date share one label, joined with a middle dot. Each stays over its mark (a window's middle over its window) and within the plot's width, clear of the axis ticks; where the row is too short for them so, a window's label shortens before a milestone's wherever that makes room, each only as far as the row needs, with an ellipsis and its whole text as its title, and one with no room for three characters is left out. Labels inside the plot are drawn over the lines, ringed in the surface, so a line that crosses one runs behind the words.

_Example: story `Stories.NarrowLabels`._

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | A hairline across the plot at the category, a marker on every line there, the tooltip.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Isolated | A series hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the plot; the axis keeps its domain.                                                                                                                                                      |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: a click anywhere in a category's column, or Enter on the focused plot, chooses it. Every series is ringed there and the card opens on the point. The selection carries no series: a point is the category. |
| Loading  | A skeleton line on a hairline, pulsing, at the plot's height.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Entering | The lines draw in over `motion.duration.slow`; a change of data moves them.                                                                                                                                                              |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`curve`**, **`dots`**, **`labels`**, **`baseline`**, **`bands`**, **`reference`**, **`connectNulls`** as in Variants and Anatomy.
- **`scale="time"`**, **`domain`**, **`delta`** as in Variants; **`syncId`** and **`texture`** as on the Frame (a line's stroke stays solid); a series' own **`format`**.
- **`xLabel`**, **`yLabel`** print axis titles.
- **`format`**, **`formatX`** for the numbers and the categories, inherited from the Frame; the Frame's table prints the plot's.
- **`data`**, **`x`**, **`series`**: Inside a Frame, `data`, `x` and `series` may be left to the Frame, and the Frame learns them from the part when they are given here instead: say them once, to either. The Frame's legend takes a Line's stroke swatch from it.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ datum, index }`.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.
- **`label`** names the plot outside a Frame.

## Content

- **The category axis is ordered**: months, weeks, versions. Unordered categories are a Bar. Real dates go on a time axis, so a gap in the sampling is a gap in the plot.
- **Label the end**, never every point. The tooltip carries the rest.
- **A cropped axis is declared** in the description: "the axis starts at the first month's count".
- **A gap is a gap.** Say why in the description; do not join across it unless the gap is a sampling artefact.
- **A limit is `danger`**, a target is `neutral`, a milestone is `neutral` on the category axis, each labelled with its name.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                           |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line      | `color.chart.<tone>` · 2px · round caps and joins                               |
| Marker    | 8px · 2px `elevation.surface` ring                                              |
| End label | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular · 8px after the line         |
| Band      | `color.chart.<tone>` at 10% · label `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtlest` |
| Reference | `color.chart.<tone>` · 1px dashed 4 3                                           |
| Cursor    | `color.border.bold` · 1px across the plot                                       |
| Zero line | `color.border.bold` · 1px                                                       |
| Delta     | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtlest` · tabular · signed                    |
| Chosen    | The series' tone: an 8px marker in a 16px halo at 20%                           |
| Dimmed    | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                 |
| Skeleton  | `color.skeleton` · 2px path on a `color.border` hairline                        |

## Accessibility

- **Named by the Frame**, or by `label`: the plot is a group, focusable, the arrow keys move the tooltip across the categories, and Enter chooses one when the plot has `onSelect` or `details`. The card that opens is a dialog, and focus returns to the plot after.
- **The table is the other copy** of the same numbers, one toggle away in the Frame.
- **Two or more series have a legend**, and each end label is a number in the text colour, not the series colour.
- **A gap is visible under every vision**: it is an absence, not a colour.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the plot's name], loading".

- [Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs): the same categories, when the size matters more than the change.

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Scatter (src/stories/patterns/ChartScatter.mdx) -->

# Scatter

A point per record on two value axes: where each thing sits on two measures at once. Risks by likelihood and impact; findings by age and severity. Points fall into groups of a tone, three at most; a bubble's area follows a third value; two references make quadrants. Each point is a record, so a click opens its card. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame.

_Example: story `Stories.ScatterMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                                                       |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Point     | 8px across in its group's tone, ringed 2px in the surface so overlapping points stay apart, with a hit area 24px across.                         |
| Bubble    | With `z`, a point whose area follows the value (twice the value, twice the ink), at 70% so what is under it shows.                               |
| Axes      | Both value axes, a hairline on the category side, ticks in `color.text.subtlest`, titles in `color.text.subtle` when the keys do not say enough. |
| Grid      | Hairlines both ways, since both axes are values.                                                                                                 |
| Reference | A dashed hairline at a value on either axis; one on each makes quadrants.                                                                        |
| Tooltip   | The point's name and group, then each axis as name and value. Per point, not per column.                                                         |
| Card      | On a chosen point: its name, group and axes, then the caller's facts and a way to the record.                                                    |

## Variants

| Variant   | Use                                                                                                                     |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One tone  | Every point in `brand`: the shape of the cloud is the point.                                                            |
| `groups`  | Up to three groups by a key, each a tone: status groups in the status tones, kinds in the first three categorical hues. |
| `z`       | A bubble: exposure, cost, count.                                                                                        |
| Quadrants | A `reference` on each axis: the four corners the reader names ("treat", "accept").                                      |

_Example: story `Stories.Groups`._
_Example: story `Stories.Bubbles`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px, `large` 320px (the right one for a scatter that is a page's point), or `height` in pixels. Unsaid, it is the Frame's; in the Frame's expanded Dialog it is `large`. Bubbles range from 64 to 900 square pixels whatever the plot's size.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                          |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The tooltip at the point. No cursor band, since there is no category.                                                                                 |
| Isolated | A group hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the plot.                                                                                               |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: the points take the pointer, a click chooses one, the others dim and the chosen one gains a halo; the card opens on it. |
| Loading  | Eight skeleton dots on two hairlines, pulsing, at the plot's height.                                                                                  |
| Entering | The points arrive over `motion.duration.slow`.                                                                                                        |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._
_Example: story `Stories.AsATable`._

## Modifiers

- **`z`** for a bubble, **`zLabel`** for what its size is called; **`name`** for the key that names a point.
- **`groupBy`** and **`groups`** for the groups and their tones; **`tone`** for every point when there are none.
- **`reference`**, **`xLabel`**, **`yLabel`**, **`format`**, **`formatX`** as on the other parts.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ datum, group, index }`.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.
- **`label`** names the plot outside a Frame.

## Content

- **Both axes are measures.** A category on one axis is a Bar or a strip; two categories are a Heatmap.
- **Three groups at most.** The first three hues validate against each other in every pairing; a fourth does not. Finer distinctions are the tooltip's or a filter's.
- **Name the points** with `name`, so the tooltip and the card say which record.
- **Title the axes** when the keys are not words the reader would say: "Likelihood", "Impact".
- **A quadrant's meaning is in the description**, not drawn: "the lines split the register into quadrants".

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                     |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Point     | `color.chart.<tone>` · 8px · 2px `elevation.surface` ring · 24px hit area |
| Bubble    | The same at 70% · area from 64 to 900 square pixels                       |
| Grid      | `color.border` · 1px both ways                                            |
| Reference | `color.chart.neutral` · 1px dashed 4 3                                    |
| Chosen    | The point's tone: a halo 8px wider at 20%                                 |
| Dimmed    | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                           |
| Skeleton  | `color.skeleton` dots on `color.border` hairlines                         |

## Accessibility

- **Named by the Frame**, or by `label`: the plot is a group and focusable. The arrow keys do not walk points (there is no category axis to walk), so the table is the keyboard's way in: one row per point, a column per axis.
- **The table is one toggle away.** In a Frame the scatter lays its points out as the Frame's table twin and CSV: the point's `name` under "Point", its group's label under "Group", the Frame's `columns` with `place: "before"`, a column per axis headed by `xLabel`, `yLabel` and `zLabel`, then the columns after. The groups stay one column of words: the legend's groups never become a column each. The legend keys the groups when the Frame is given no `series`.
- **A chosen point's card is a dialog**, and focus returns to the plot when it closes.
- **Three groups keep every pair apart** under deutan and protan vision; the legend carries their names, and the tooltip and the card say the group in words.
- **A point's hit area is 24px** whatever its size, so a small point still takes a click.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the plot's name], loading".

_Props: generated from `Chart.Scatter`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

- [Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs): one measure per category.

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Sparkline (src/stories/patterns/ChartSparkline.mdx) -->

# Sparkline

A trend with no axes, no grid and no legend, beside the number it belongs to: in a Stat tile, in a table's trend column, after a count. The number carries the value; the sparkline carries the shape. A line by default, a wash or bars when asked, with an end dot for the last point and a hairline for a reference. Ninety-six by twenty-four pixels. Unnamed it is decoration; named, it is a plot with a tooltip.

_Example: story `Stories.SparklineMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                     |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line      | 1.5px in its tone, round joins; `area` adds the tone at 12% under it; `bars` is a column per point, 1px apart. |
| End dot   | A 6px marker ringed in the surface on the last point: where the series is now.                                 |
| Reference | A dashed hairline at a value in `color.chart.neutral`: last period, the limit.                                 |
| Tooltip   | Only when named: the point's value and category.                                                               |

## Variants

| Variant             | Use                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `appearance="line"` | The default: a count over time.                                                           |
| `appearance="area"` | A count whose size matters, with a reference for the limit.                               |
| `appearance="bars"` | A count per period, where each period is discrete: closed per month.                      |
| In a tile           | Beside the value of a Stat.Tile, `space.150` from the number.                             |
| In a row            | The trend column of a Table, 80 by 20, unnamed, so a screen reader hears the number once. |

_Example: story `Stories.InTiles`._
_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

## Sizes

| `width` × `height` | Where                                                      |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| 80 × 20            | A table row.                                               |
| 96 × 24            | Beside a Stat's value. The default.                        |
| 120 × 28           | Bars, which need the width.                                |
| 160 × 40           | A card's corner, when the trend is the card's second fact. |

Anything larger is a [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs) in a Frame, with axes. `width` is the most a sparkline takes: in a narrower cell, tile or row beside its number it narrows and keeps its height.

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

## States

| State    | What changes                                                       |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Hover    | Nothing, unless named: then a marker and the tooltip at the point. |
| Loading  | A skeleton bar at the size, pulsing.                               |
| Entering | The line draws in over `motion.duration.slow`.                     |

A sparkline does not choose: nothing to click, nothing to open. The number beside it is the way to the record.

## Modifiers

- **`appearance`**, **`tone`**, **`endDot`**, **`reference`** as in Anatomy.
- **`x`** names the category key, for the tooltip of a named sparkline.
- **`width`**, **`height`** in pixels.
- **`format`** for the tooltip.
- **`label`** names it: "Open findings, nine months". Unsaid, it is decoration.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.

## Content

- **Always beside a number.** A sparkline alone says only "up" or "down".
- **One tone, the number's status** when it has one: `danger` beside open findings, `success` beside closed; `brand` or `neutral` otherwise. Never a categorical hue.
- **Six to twelve points.** Fewer is a number; more is a Line.
- **A reference is one value**: last period, the limit. Not a band, not a target series.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                      |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line      | `color.chart.<tone>` · 1.5px · round joins                 |
| Wash      | `color.chart.<tone>` at 12%                                |
| Bars      | `color.chart.<tone>` · `radius` 1px at the top · 1px apart |
| End dot   | 6px · 2px `elevation.surface` ring                         |
| Reference | `color.chart.neutral` · 1px dashed 3 2                     |
| Skeleton  | `color.skeleton` · `radius.xsmall`                         |

## Accessibility

- **Unnamed, it is `aria-hidden`** and not focusable: the number beside it is the fact, and a screen reader hears it once.
- **Named, it is a group**, focusable, with the arrow keys moving the tooltip across the points, and it should sit where no number says the same thing.
- **Never the only carrier of a value.** If the shape matters enough to say, say it in the tile's note: "Down from 14 in January".
- **The tone is not the meaning**: the number's word or Badge is.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Chart.Sparkline`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

- [Stat](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs): the number it sits beside.
- [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs): the same series with axes, when it needs to say more.
- [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs): the trend column.

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Treemap (src/stories/patterns/ChartTreemap.mdx) -->

# Treemap

Part-to-whole with a hierarchy: a tile per leaf, sized by value, in the tone of its top-level branch. Findings by system and component; controls by family and enhancement. Where the total goes, and where inside that. A name shows on a tile when it fits; the rest is the tooltip's. A click on a tile drills into its branch, or opens its card. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame, whose legend names the branches.

_Example: story `Stories.TreemapMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                           |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tile    | A leaf, `radius` 2px, in its branch's tone, with a 2px `elevation.surface` gap from its neighbours. Sized by value, 4:3 as far as the layout allows. |
| Name    | The tile's name on an `elevation.surface` chip at 92% in `color.text`, when the tile is at least 64 by 28; cut with the whole in a title.            |
| Tooltip | The tile's name and value, keyed by a square.                                                                                                        |
| Card    | On a chosen tile: its name, its branch and its value, then the caller's facts.                                                                       |

## Variants

| Variant    | Use                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Branches   | Two levels: systems in the categorical set, their components inside each in the same hue.                                         |
| One branch | One system alone, its components in its one hue: the level under a drill-down.                                                    |
| Drill-down | A click on a tile redraws the treemap with its branch, the way back in the Frame's `path`; a click on a component opens its card. |

_Example: story `Stories.Systems`._
_Example: story `Stories.Drilldown`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px, `large` 320px (the right one: tiles need room for their names), or `height` in pixels. A treemap should be at least 420px wide; narrower, most names fall to the tooltip.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                 |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The tooltip.                                                                                                                 |
| Isolated | A branch hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the treemap; the rest re-tile. A hovered legend item dims the other branches. |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: the tiles take the pointer, a click chooses one, the others dim; the card opens on the tile.   |
| Loading  | Four skeleton tiles, pulsing, at the plot's height.                                                                          |
| Entering | The tiles arrive over `motion.duration.slow`; a drill-down re-tiles the same way.                                            |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

In a Frame the treemap's leaves are its table twin and its CSV: a row per leaf in the tree's order, a column per level holding the names on its way down, then its value. `levels` names the columns (`["System", "Component"]`); unsaid, the top level takes the Frame's `xLabel`, else "Group", and the leaves "Name". The legend keys the top-level branches when the Frame is given no `series`, and a branch hidden from it stays in the table, which is the data.

_Example: story `Stories.AsATable`._

## Modifiers

- **`data`** as nodes: a name, a value on a leaf, children on a branch, a `tone` on a top-level node when the categorical order is not wanted.
- **`levels`** for the table twin's headings, one per level from the top.
- **`format`** for the tooltip, the card and the Frame's table.
- **`size`** or **`height`**: the Frame's when unsaid; `large` in the Frame's expanded Dialog.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ name, value, group }`, `group` being the top-level branch.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.
- **`label`** names the plot outside a Frame.

## Content

- **A hierarchy, or nothing.** A flat list of five is a Bar; a treemap earns its place when the reader asks "where, and where inside that".
- **Six branches at most**, in the categorical set; more folds into Other.
- **Names are short**: a component, a family. What does not fit is the tooltip's, and the table's.
- **Values are one thing**: a count, a cost. Not a score.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                  |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tile     | `color.chart.<tone>` · `radius` 2px · 2px `elevation.surface` gap                      |
| Name     | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text` on an `elevation.surface` chip at 92% · `radius` 2px |
| Dimmed   | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                        |
| Skeleton | `color.skeleton` tiles                                                                 |

## Accessibility

- **Named by the Frame**, or by `label`: the plot is a group. Interactive charts require one of these names. When `onSelect` or `details` is supplied, each leaf is a named button reachable with Tab; Enter and Space perform the same action as a click. Its accessible name includes the branch, full name and value, even when the visible label is shortened. Display-only tiles and unnamed, decorative plots add no tab stops.
- **Text never sits on a tile's colour**: the name is on a surface chip, in the text colour.
- **Every tile has a title** with its whole name and value, whether or not the name fits.
- **The table is one toggle away** in a Frame: every leaf, every level named, every value, so the areas are never the only way to read the sizes.
- **A chosen tile's card is a dialog**, and focus returns to that tile when it closes, or the first available tile if it was removed.
- **Keyboard drill-down preserves the chosen leaf's focus** when Recharts replaces its branch, or focuses the first available tile when that leaf no longer exists.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the plot's name], loading".

## Props

_Props: generated from `Chart.Treemap`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

- [Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs): parts compared without a hierarchy.
- [Donut](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-donut--docs): parts of one whole with the whole in the middle.
- [Tree](?path=/docs/components-tree--docs): the same hierarchy as an outline, when the reader wants to walk it.

<!-- page: Patterns/CommandPalette (src/stories/patterns/CommandPalette.mdx) -->

# CommandPalette

A ⌘K palette over a page or a record: a field at the top, the commands under headings, a shortcut at the end of the ones that have one, the keys in the footer. Choosing a command closes the palette and runs it. The commands are plain objects the caller supplies, so the palette stays presentational and every page can reuse it; `useCommandPalette` holds the open state and toggles it on ⌘K or Ctrl+K anywhere on the page. It runs a command; it does not find a record, which is the [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs), and it does not search the product, which is the [SearchDialog](?path=/docs/patterns-searchdialog--docs) behind the top nav's search.

_Example: story `Stories.CommandPaletteStory`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                    |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field   | "Type a command…", focused on open.                                           |
| Heading | The group's name, over its commands: Record, Go to, Preferences.              |
| Command | A verb and its object; the shortcut or hint at the end in `font.body.xsmall`. |
| Empty   | "No commands match."                                                          |
| Footer  | The keys: the arrows to move, Enter to run, Escape to close.                  |

_Example: story `Stories.CommandPaletteMatrix`._

## Variants

CommandPalette has one appearance. What varies is the commands, which are the page's: a record's verbs first, the places to go after, the preferences last.

Not built, and why: search across records in the palette, because a record is found by the top nav's search and picked by the RecordPicker; nested pages of commands, because a command with choices is a Dialog of its own; recent commands at the top, because the order is the page's and it should read the same every time; icons before the commands, because the heading says the kind.

## Sizes

One: the Command dialog at its medium width, 560px, over the page at the top.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                    |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Closed   | Not rendered. ⌘K opens it.                                      |
| Open     | Over the page at the top, the field focused, every group shown. |
| Filtered | The commands that match, under their headings; empty groups go. |
| None     | The empty sentence.                                             |
| Run      | The palette closes, then the command runs.                      |

## Modifiers

- **`commands`**: id, group, label, hint, run. Commands with the same group in sequence share a heading.
- **`placeholder`** for the field.
- **`useCommandPalette`** returns `open` and `setOpen`, and binds ⌘K and Ctrl+K while mounted.

## Content

- **A command is a verb and its object**: "Record an assessment", "Export the SSP", "Switch the colour mode". Never a noun alone.
- **The headings are kinds of command**: "Record" for what the record does, "Go to" for places, "Preferences" for the reader's own.
- **The hint is the shortcut** when there is one, in the platform's glyphs; otherwise nothing.
- **The page's verbs first**, the places after, the preferences last.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Dialog  | CommandDialog: `radius.xxlarge` · `elevation.surface.overlay` · `elevation.shadow.overlay` · `color.blanket` |
| Heading | CommandGroup's: `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle`                                                     |
| Command | CommandItem: `dimension.control.medium` · `color.background.selected` when selected                          |
| Hint    | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · at the end                                                        |
| Footer  | CommandFooter: `elevation.surface.sunken` · `font.body.xsmall` · Kbd for each key                            |

## Accessibility

- **A dialog named "Command palette"**; focus moves to the field on open and returns to where it was on close.
- **The list is a listbox** with the headings as group labels, so a screen reader hears "Record, group, Record an assessment, A".
- **The arrows move, Enter runs, Escape closes**, and the footer says so with Kbd, each key named in full.
- **⌘K and Ctrl+K both open it**, so the shortcut works on every platform; which glyph the page shows is the product's call, parked in docs/next.md.
- **Running closes first**, so a command that opens a dialog does not stack one over the other.

## Props

_Props: generated from `CommandPalette`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### useCommandPalette

The palette's open state, toggled by ⌘K or Ctrl+K anywhere on the page. Returns `{ open, setOpen }`.

## Related

- [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs): the same CommandDialog, picking one record instead of running a command.
- [Kbd](?path=/docs/components-kbd--docs): the keys in the footer and the hints.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Composer (src/stories/patterns/Composer.mdx) -->

# Composer

An experimental shared text composer for messages, comments and other short drafts. Ledger owns keyboard completion, submission progress and recovery. The consuming application owns recipients, permissions, persistence, suggestion identity and serialized text. Owner: Ledger maintainers; consumers own their adapters.

_Example: story `Stories.ComposerMatrix`._

## Anatomy

A named textarea, optional leading marker, contextual fields above, instructions below, optional `actions` before the buttons (a second thing to do with the draft), optional cancel action, and primary submission action. Suggestions attach beneath the field; rejection produces a visible alert.

## Variants

One composition, with optional suggestion and leading slots. No event taxonomy or built-in mention syntax. The example below uses a `#` adapter and stable topic identifiers to demonstrate a non-person use case.

_Example: story `Stories.Suggestions`._

## Sizes

Three initial textarea rows. The layout follows its container; the suggestion popup is bounded by the available width and scrolls when tall. Long option labels truncate visually while retaining their accessible text.

## States

Empty drafts cannot submit. Nonempty drafts submit with the button or Ctrl/⌘ + Enter. While pending, the textarea is read-only and repeat submission and cancellation are blocked. Fulfillment clears the submitted draft; rejection retains it with a retry message. A newer controlled draft is retained when an earlier request resolves. A disabled composer cannot be edited or submitted.

_Example: story `Stories.SaveRecovery`._

## Modifiers

`value` and `onValueChange` select caller-owned state; `defaultValue` supplies an uncontrolled initial draft. Do not switch ownership while mounted. `ref`, `id`, and `name` target the visible textarea. `leading`, `hint`, `children` and `actions` are rendered slots; `actions` sits before the cancel and primary buttons, for a secondary Button the caller wires to the draft it keeps through `value`.

`getSuggestions(text, caret)` returns UTF-16 replacement offsets and ordered options, or null. The caller provides unique option IDs, accessible labels, exact insertion strings, filtering and result limits. Invalid ranges are ignored. The adapter is synchronous; fetching remote candidates belongs to the caller. No rich-text document model is implied.

## Content

Supply a descriptive `label` independently of placeholder text. Translate `submitLabel`, `cancelLabel`, `suggestionsLabel`, `errorMessage` and `hint`. Use stable identities when your product serializes references; a display name need not be an identity. Resolve `onSubmit` only when your application's promised save boundary succeeds; throw or reject on failure.

## Style

Textarea and Button provide the control styling. Layout uses `space.100`; suggestions use the overlay surface, default border and overlay shadow. Pending and error states remain understandable without animation or color alone.

## Accessibility

The textarea keeps focus while suggestions are navigated. Up/Down selects an option, Enter/Tab inserts it, and Escape closes the list without dismissing a containing overlay. IME confirmation does not insert or submit. Suggestions expose listbox/option semantics and an active descendant. Pointer selection returns focus to the textarea. Instructions and errors describe the textarea; rejection is announced through an alert. The completion key handling and save recovery run in both color modes.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Composer`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._
_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs) for plain multiline input.
- [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs) for rendering events independently of the composer.
- Application Activity.Composer adapts this contract to its people list and `@[Full Name]` format; those workflows remain in the application.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._
