# Data table

The register with its state. [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) is the markup and stays for a table with nothing to sort, filter, page or choose. `DataTable` is the same parts drawn from a TanStack Table 9 instance: the columns are declared by kind, the state has an owner, and every feature is one option on the hook and one part in the renderer. No route sorts, filters or pages by hand.

_Example: story `Stories.RegisterStory`._

## Anatomy

| Part                                   | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `defineColumns<T>((c) => [...])`       | The columns of a record type, by kind. A kind decides alignment, minimum width, sort and filter, and the part that draws the value. Keep the call at module level.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `useDataTable({ columns, data, ... })` | The table instance. `getRowId` names rows; `selectable` draws the checkbox column; `pageSize` pages and draws Pagination, with the Rows per page choice from `pageSizes`; `label` names the table. Any TanStack state slice can be owned outside: pass `sorting` and `onSortingChange`, or `state.columnFilters` from the route's own filters. `initialState` seeds what the table keeps. `manual` hands sorting, filtering or pagination to the server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `DataTable table={table}`              | The renderer: the `toolbar` slot above the header, the Table parts closed by a hairline under the last row, the states drawn under the header so it never moves, and [Pagination](?path=/docs/components-pagination--docs) below when the table pages. No frame: the register sits on the page and its rules are the only lines. With `fill` it is the page's one block: it takes the rest of the window, the rows scroll under the header and the pagination sits at the bottom.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| The toolbar parts                      | `DataTable.Filter`, `.Presets`, `.Sort`, `.Columns` and `.Settings`, each taking the `table`; `.Sort` is the sort as a menu that names it (see Sort menu); `.SelectionBar` appears above the table while rows are chosen. `Presets` is a strip on its own line, or `variant="menu"` for one button in a toolbar that also holds search and filters; narrower than its label, that button shortens the label with an ellipsis, keeps the full label as its title, and keeps its count and chevron. In a [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs) the search is its own field, first in the row: pass `search={table.state.globalFilter}` and `onSearch={table.setGlobalFilter}`. `DataTable.Search` is the same field for a composition without a Toolbar; as a Toolbar child it would land among the controls at the end. |
| The Table parts                        | It draws `Table.Header`, `.Row`, `.Cell`, `.Id`, `.List`, `.Selection`, `.Disclosure`, `.Group`, `.Detail` and `.Handle`; nothing of its own.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Metrics

`DataTable.Metrics` wraps a toolbar, an optional summary region and the table. It starts closed. Put `DataTable.MetricsTrigger` in the toolbar actions and `DataTable.MetricsContent` directly below the toolbar. Compose the content with `Stat` or the app's existing summary cards.

Opening metrics only changes the disclosure. Search, filters, sorting and selection keep their state. The app supplies the values and decides whether they summarize all records or the filtered rows; make that scope clear in the content.

```tsx
<DataTable.Metrics>
  <Toolbar
    search={table.state.globalFilter}
    onSearch={table.setGlobalFilter}
    actions={<DataTable.MetricsTrigger />}
  />
  <DataTable.MetricsContent className="px-200 py-100">
    <Stat label="Total findings" value={findings.length} />
  </DataTable.MetricsContent>
  <DataTable table={table} />
</DataTable.Metrics>
```

The root accepts [Collapsible](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs) props, including `defaultOpen` or controlled `open` and `onOpenChange`. The trigger accepts native button props and a ref, `size` and `variant`; its default is a small secondary button with a chart icon and the localized “Metrics” label. Children replace the label. The content accepts Collapsible content props, including `forceMount`, native props and a ref. Its default region name is localized “Metrics”; `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` can name a custom summary.

_Example: story `Stories.MetricsStory`._

## Group by

`DataTable.GroupBy` replaces a row of grouping pills with one toolbar menu. It shows the selected field, checks that choice in the menu, and offers **None** to return to an ungrouped list. The active treatment matches Metrics. `options` supplies `{ value, label }` fields; `value` and `onValueChange` belong to the caller. The empty string means no grouping. Native button attributes and refs reach the trigger.

For `useDataTable`, bind the same value to `groupBy` and `state.grouping`. Set `initialState.expanded: true` when newly selected groups should start open. Pagination returns when grouping is cleared; search, filters, selection and column settings retain their existing owners.

```tsx
const [group, setGroup] = useState("");
const table = useDataTable({
  columns,
  data,
  groupBy: group || undefined,
  state: { grouping: group ? [group] : [] },
  initialState: { expanded: true },
});
// Inside the toolbar actions:
<DataTable.GroupBy options={groupOptions} value={group} onValueChange={setGroup} />;
```

The menu also works with custom collection renderers. The control board binds it to family, stage, owner and component grouping; the scoped Program controls table offers family, implementation, assessment, owner and applies-to fields. Task tables use the same menu alongside saved views, columns and settings.

`DataTable.Filters table={table} columns={["status", "owner"]}` collects multiple filters in one toolbar popover. It reuses each column's existing checkbox, text or range fields. The trigger shows the number of filtered columns; **Clear all filters** clears column filters while retaining search, grouping and selected records. `DataTable.Filter` remains available for a single exposed filter chip.

Facet choices and counts follow the current data, search and other column filters, including rows loaded or replaced after mount.

_Example: story `Stories.LiveFilters`._

For filters owned outside the table, pass `additionalFilters={{ content, count, onClear }}`. The supplied fields appear first, contribute to the active count, and reset with **Clear all filters**. Controls uses this for its URL-backed Scope filter.

_Example: story `Stories.GroupByStory`._

## Sort menu

`DataTable.Sort table={table}` is the sort as a toolbar menu: the column under **Sort by**, then the direction, in words that follow the column: **Oldest first** and **Newest first** for a date, **Lowest first** and **Highest first** for a number, **A to Z** and **Z to A** for an id, a name or a person, and **Ascending** and **Descending** for a status, a column with its own `sortBy` and a custom sort. The trigger reads the sort ("Sort: Due") with the direction's arrow, and its accessible name starts with those words and adds the direction ("Sort: Due, Oldest first"). Choices keep the menu open, so the column and the direction are set in one visit; Escape closes it and focus returns to the trigger. While nothing is sorted the direction waits, disabled, for a column.

Use it in every `responsive` register, and wherever the reader should see the order without reading the headers. A responsive table folds lower-priority columns into each row's More fields, and a folded column has no header to sort by or to carry the arrow; the menu offers every sortable column the reader shows, folded or not. It writes the table's sorting, so a drawn header keeps its arrow and `aria-sort`, the view store and `useTableQuery` see the change, and no header claims a sort it does not have. Put it among a [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs)'s display controls, before Columns and Settings, where it folds into More with them. A table that never folds does not need it: the headers sort, and their column menus do too. With `enableMultiSort` the menu shows and replaces the first sort.

`columns` limits and orders what it offers; `label` is the trigger's words before anything is sorted. Native button props and a ref reach the trigger.

```tsx
<Toolbar search={table.state.globalFilter} onSearch={table.setGlobalFilter}>
  <DataTable.Sort table={table} />
  <DataTable.Columns table={table} />
  <DataTable.Settings table={table} />
</Toolbar>
```

_Example: story `Stories.SortMenuStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.SortMenuFolded`._

_Props: generated from `DataTableSort`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.SortPlayground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Keeping the question

The view store keeps the reader's layout. `useTableQuery` keeps their question: the search, the sort, the column filters and the page, so a register still asks it after the reader opens a record and comes back. Call it right after `useDataTable`; the layout is restored first, then the question.

- **`useTableQuery(table, { storage: "session" })`** keeps it in this tab's session storage, under `ledger.table.<view>.query`; `key` names it when the table has no `view`. It survives opening a record and pressing Back, and ends with the tab.
- **`useTableQuery(table, { search, onSearchChange, prefix })`** keeps it in the URL through the product's own router, so it can be shared and bookmarked. Pass the route's current search (an object, `URLSearchParams` or a query string); in `onSearchChange`, merge the parameters over the route's search and replace the history entry. `undefined` removes a parameter. Back, Forward or a followed link applies its question to a register that is already open.

```tsx
const search = route.useSearch();
useTableQuery(table, {
  search,
  onSearchChange: (params) =>
    navigate({ search: (previous) => ({ ...previous, ...params }), replace: true }),
});
```

The parameters are `q` (the search), `sort` (column ids, `-` before a descending one: `-due,name`), `filters` (one JSON object keyed by column id) and `page` (from 2); `prefix` keeps two tables on one route apart. A slice at the author's default is left out, so a fresh register has a clean URL. What arrives is validated: a malformed parameter is dropped rather than applied in part, and a column the table does not have, cannot sort or cannot filter is ignored. A restored page waits until its rows exist, and lands on the last page when fewer arrive. Refetched data still returns a client-paged table to its first page, as it does without the hook. A router that commits its search later than the reader types gives back each earlier question on the way; the hook knows the questions it wrote and does not apply those echoes, so the search box never loses a letter, while Back, Forward and a followed link still apply theirs.

The helpers underneath are pure and know no router: `tableQueryToSearch(query, { prefix })` and `tableQueryFromSearch(search, { prefix })` convert both ways, `tableQueryToString` gives a query string for a link, `readTableQuery(table)` reads the question as it stands, and `tableQueryParamNames` names the parameters for a route that declares its search.

Do not keep the question of a table in a dialog, a sheet or a picker: it ends with the task, and the table's own state is enough. Do not put the layout in the URL; `view` keeps it per browser.

_Example: story `Stories.QuestionInSession`._

_Example: story `Stories.QuestionInUrl`._

_Example: story `Stories.QuestionInLaggingUrl`._

## Variants

Which table first: a table sorts, filters, pages, chooses, pins, nests or scrolls inside itself, `DataTable`; otherwise `Table`. Then the modes, each one option on the hook:

| The register                       | Option                                         | Role       |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| Sorted, filtered, paged, chosen    | `pageSize`, `selectable`                       | `table`    |
| A hierarchy with columns           | `tree`                                         | `treegrid` |
| A hierarchy whose rows open too    | `tree` with `detail` and `detailColumn: false` | `treegrid` |
| A record that opens into more      | `detail`                                       | `table`    |
| Records under headings             | `groupBy`                                      | `table`    |
| Rows held above and below          | `pinRows`                                      | `table`    |
| Rows in the reader's order         | `reorderRows`                                  | `table`    |
| A thousand rows                    | `virtualize` with `maxHeight` or `fill`        | `table`    |
| The register that is the page      | `fill` on the renderer                         | `table`    |
| The server sorts, filters or pages | `manual` with `rowCount`                       | `table`    |
| Cells the reader edits in place    | `editable` on a column                         | `grid`     |

There is no per-column filter row under the header: filters are chips in the toolbar, built from the columns. There is no zebra, no radio selection, no expand-all; see Table. There is no third component for a tree: it is a mode of this one.

_Example: story `Stories.TreeStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.TreeWithDetailRows`._

_Example: story `Stories.DetailRows`._

_Example: story `Stories.GroupsStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.PinnedRowsStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.ReorderingRows`._

## Sizes

Rows are `dimension.row` 40px, and `dimension.row.compact` 36px through the reader's density setting, never a prop; the header `dimension.row.header` 32px. Virtualization uses that density as its initial estimate, then measures each mounted record together with any disclosed detail rows. Widths come from the kind (id 92, or 116 with `preview` to hold the eye, status 120, person 160, date 112, number 96, actions 32) as minimums; the author gives `width` for fixed columns and one column takes the slack. `resizable` or `reorderable` switches the layout to `fixed`, so a change to one column leaves the others alone; `layout` sets it by hand. `maxHeight` makes the frame scroll inside itself; `fill` takes the rest of the window instead, and wins when both are given.

_Example: story `Stories.PinnedColumns`._

_Example: story `Stories.MovingColumns`._

_Example: story `Stories.ColumnWidthFromMenu`._

_Example: story `Stories.PinnedNarrow`._

_Example: story `Stories.ColumnGroups`._

## States

| State          | What the renderer draws                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ready          | The rows. With none left after the filters, the empty state.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Loading        | The header kept, a skeleton line per row where the records will be, no Pagination, and the table `aria-busy`. The height of what is already there never changes.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Empty          | No records at all: nothing to search, sort or page, so the toolbar, the header and the hairline go, and the register is one [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs) on its dashed frame: the `records` picture (or `empty.illustration`), `empty.title`, its description, its `action`, which creates the first record, and `secondary`.                    |
| Filtered empty | A search or a column filter is active, or the caller says `narrowed`, and no rows remain: the toolbar and the header stay, and under the header the table draws the `search` picture, **Nothing matches**, a line of copy and **Clear filters**, which clears the search and every column filter. No Pagination under it. `empty.filtered` overrides each part. |
| Error          | `error` under the header.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Sorted         | The header's arrow and `aria-sort`, and `DataTable.Sort`'s trigger ("Sort: Due"), which still names a sort whose column is folded into More fields; one column at a time unless the table says `enableMultiSort`.                                                                                                                                               |
| Filtered       | The applied value on each chip; the presets' counts; the range in Pagination.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Chosen         | The rows on `color.background.selected` and the SelectionBar above: the count, the verbs, Clear, and "Select all 340" as a second, explicit step.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

The row states (hover, selected, active id, static, scrolled edge, expanded) are Table's.

_Example: story `Stories.StatesStory`._

**Narrowed outside the table.** A scope toggle, a route or server filter, or a picker's own search narrows `data` before the table sees it, so the table cannot tell an empty result from an empty register. Say so with `narrowed`: with nothing left, the toolbar and the header stay and the filtered empty shows, so the control that brings the rows back ("Include everything inside", "Clear related-record filter") stays in reach. Give `empty.filtered.action` that way back and a line that says what narrowed the rows; the kit's **Clear filters** shows only while the table's own search or filters are set, since it cannot undo the caller's narrowing. Pass `narrowed` only while the caller's narrowing is on, and `empty.filtered` only while it applies.

_Example: story `Stories.NarrowedOutsideTheTable`._

**The result is said.** After a search, a filter, a saved question, the caller's narrowing or a page, the table says the result once the reader stops (half a second after the last change), in one polite line through the page's [Announcer](?path=/docs/components-announcer--docs): "8 of 24 findings", "9–16 of 24 findings", "No matching findings". `noun` is what a row is, `{ one, other }`, "row" and "rows" unsaid. The first result is not said: the page's heading and its loading say that. A refresh of an unnarrowed register is not said either.

_Example: story `Stories.ResultStatus`._

## Modifiers

The hook's options, each one feature:

- **`rowLabel`**: a row's readable name, its code or its title. Its controls say it: "Select REQ-001", "Row actions for REQ-001", "Reorder REQ-001", "Show details for REQ-001", More fields for it, and a row that moves is said by it. Unset, the controls keep their generic names ("Select row" and the id). Give it to every table whose `getRowId` is a key no reader knows, a UUID. **`selectable`**: the checkbox column; a function says which rows can be chosen. **`pageSize`** pages, and **`pageSizes`** are the sizes the reader can choose from in the Pagination (`10, 20, 50, 100` unsaid); the choice persists with `view`. **`label`** names the table. **`manual`** with `rowCount` hands sorting, filtering or pagination to a server.
- **`pinnable`, `hideable`, `resizable`, `reorderable`, `columnMenu`, `layout`, `view`**: the columns the reader owns. The column menu on a header's hover sorts, moves, pins and hides, and is always shown where nothing can hover; `DataTable.Columns` in the toolbar shows and hides, and the gear beside it, `DataTable.Settings`, holds the rows' density and Reset view. With `reorderable`, a column's grip drags it within the middle band, and its menu's Move left and Move right move it one place each way, disabled at the band's edges: a way to reorder that needs no drag, for the keyboard, a touch screen or a single pointer. After a move, focus is back on the column's menu, scrolled clear of the pinned columns, and a polite status says where the column stands ("Finding, 3 of 5"). A pinned column and the row actions keep their band. In a right-to-left table the words follow the screen, so Move right moves a column towards the start. With `resizable`, the handle drags, and the column's menu sets the width with one press each, a way that needs no drag (WCAG 2.5.7): **Wider** and **Narrower** step 32px and keep the menu open for another press, stopping at the column's minimum and maximum, and **Reset width** returns to the author's width; the same polite status says the width the column now has ("Finding, 272 pixels wide"). A column's `width` is also its floor, so Narrower stops there. The checkbox, the disclosure, the handle and the detail chevron are always the first columns and always pinned; the row's actions are always the last and always pinned to the end, so the kebab sits at the table's trailing edge however far the columns scroll; a pinned column keeps its hairline while the frame is scrolled, and the frame's scroll padding is the pinned bands, so a heading, a cell or a menu that scrolls into view for focus lands clear of them; a band's heading sticks to the frame's leading edge. Pins give way to a narrow frame: while the pinned columns would take more than 60% of it, they are drawn unpinned from the middle outward, the end band first and then the start column nearest the middle, so the id is the last to go and the middle keeps room to scroll; they return as the frame widens, and the reader's pins, the column menu and the export do not change. The preview eye sits at the end of the row's first value cell: it appears on the row's hover and on focus in the cell, stays on the row whose preview is open, and is always shown where nothing can hover; while it shows, the value beside it keeps the eye's 24px clear and ends in an ellipsis before it. An id column with `preview` is 24px wider by default to hold both. The row-actions kebab is always shown where nothing can hover. A column's `pin` is the author's default and `hideable: false` keeps it on screen. `view: "risks"` names the table, and the reader's order, widths, visibility and pins persist in this browser under `ledger.table.risks.view`; `useTableQuery` keeps the question (search, sort, filters, page) beside it, in the URL or the session (see Keeping the question).
- **`tree`**: `children` reads a row's parts, `label` names the row for the chevron, `hint` is the muted text after a folded row's first value, `initialExpanded` says which open first; a filter or a search keeps a matching row's ancestors, so a child never shows without its parent. The chevron is a leading column of its own, always first and always pinned, so the disclosure never moves when the reader reorders, hides or pins a column. It is one narrow width at every depth, so opening and closing a row never shifts the columns; the nesting reads as an indent on the row's first value. Set `guides: true` to move the existing disclosure into the first value cell alongside vertical ancestor guides. Each guide starts below its parent and spans only its descendant rows; there are no horizontal branches. The chevron, icon and label then indent together at each depth; the separate leading disclosure column is omitted. Guides are decorative, and the disclosure retains its expand/collapse label and keyboard behavior. **`detail`** opens a row into what it returns, a child table included; its open rows are its own state, so a tree's row opens its parts and its detail apart and neither closes the other (`initialState.expanded` still says which details start open). It draws a leading chevron column of its own, which **`detailColumn: false`** leaves out: in a treegrid two chevron columns read as twins, so the row is opened from a cell instead, a `list` column with `opens: "detail"`. **`groupBy`** puts the rows under a band per value; pagination is off while it is on. **`pinRows`** lets `row.pin("top")` and `"bottom"` hold rows under the header or above the footer. **`reorderRows`** puts a handle on every row and tells you which row moved next to which; sorting is off while it is on. The row actions menu gains **Move up** and **Move down**, one press each, disabled at the ends, and a polite status says where the row now stands ("FND-2200, 2 of 6"): the way to reorder that needs no drag. Give a reorderable table an actions column, `c.actions(() => [])` when the rows have no actions of their own, so every row has that menu.
- **`virtualize`**: only the rows in view are drawn; give the renderer a `maxHeight` or `fill` and leave `pageSize` off.
- **A number column's `footer`** totals the rows the filters leave: sum, mean, min, max, count, or your own.
- **`editable`** on a text or status column: `onChange` commits the value at once, `save` settles it (the cell shows saving, saved or the error and rolls back on failure), `validate` blocks a bad value, and a status column's `options` are its menu.

The renderer's: **`toolbar`**, **`state`**, **`empty`**, **`narrowed`**, **`noun`**, **`error`**, **`onRowClick`**, **`maxHeight`**, **`fill`**, **`responsive`**, **`className`**. `toRows(table)` and `toCsv(table)` export the rows the filters leave, in the sort chosen, every page, with the columns the reader shows; a custom column exports what its `text` says. The kit has no router: `useTableQuery` binds the search, sort, filters and page to the URL through the product's router, or to the session (see Keeping the question).

**`fill`** is for the register that is the page: a collection route, a record's register tab, anywhere the table is the one block of content and only a page header, a section heading or a note sits above it. The register takes the rest of the window below its own top edge, the header sticks to the frame, the rows scroll inside it, and the pagination sits at the bottom of the page's inset whether the page has three rows or three thousand; below a header, six rows and the pagination the page scrolls again. Do not fill a table in a dialog, a sheet, a panel, a rail or a card, or one stacked above other content: give those `maxHeight` or let them scroll with the page. The document keeps scrolling for every other page.

_Example: story `Stories.FillStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.ThousandRows`._

_Example: story `Stories.RenderBudget`._

_Example: story `Stories.NameLinkFocus`._

_Example: story `Stories.ColumnsWithoutAMenu`._

_Example: story `Stories.ServerStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.EditingStory`._

## Content

The kinds carry the rules, so a DataTable cannot get them wrong:

| Kind                                           | Aligns  | Sorts by                       | Filters by | Draws                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------ | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `c.id(key, { glance, preview, active, tone })` | start   | alphanumeric                   | text       | `Table.Id`: the eye opens the preview, hover on the id shows the `glance` (the hover ladder's first rung)                                                                                                                            |
| `c.text(key, { wrap })`                        | start   | alphanumeric                   | text       | the value, truncated; `wrap` lets the row grow                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `c.number(key, { format })`                    | end     | numeric                        | range      | integer, decimal, percent or a formatter, tabular numerals                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `c.date(key, { format })`                      | start   | date                           | range      | an ISO date as `d MMM yyyy`; anything else as given                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `c.status(key, { tone } or { statuses })`      | start   | alphanumeric; `statuses`' rank | equals     | `Badge` in the tone the row decides, or the map's label in its tone                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `c.person(key)`                                | start   | text                           | equals     | `Person`                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `c.list(id, { items, empty, note, opens })`    | start   | the labels                     | contains   | `Table.List`: the first item by name, the rest as a count, every item in a hover card; the click is the row's preview, or its `detail`, which the line then carries a chevron for and whose card is suppressed while the row is open |
| `c.actions((row) => RowAction[])`              | end     | never                          | never      | the kebab on row hover and focus, always shown where nothing can hover; always the last column, pinned to the trailing edge, with no column menu                                                                                     |
| `c.custom(id, { cell, sort, align })`          | as said | `sort`'s value, or not at all  | never      | whatever `cell` returns: a bar, an icon, a composed cell                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `c.group(header, columns)`                     |         |                                |            | a second header row over the columns                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

Every kind takes `priority` (smaller numbers stay visible longer in responsive mode), `header`, `width` (pixels; also the minimum), `minWidth`, `sortable: false` and `cell(row)` to draw the value its own way while keeping the kind's behaviour. An absent value is `Absent`. Headers are one or two words in sentence case; a number's header ends with its numbers; the id first, the name second, actions last; a status is a Badge and a person a Person. Cells truncate, and the full text is the cell's title; a column that must wrap says `wrap: true` and is never the one sorted by eye.

_Example: story `Stories.ListCells`._

A status vocabulary that appears in more than one place is one map, kept beside the product's own status badge and passed to every column that shows it: `c.status("state", { statuses })`, with `statuses` a `StatusMap` of each stored value to `{ label, tone, rank }`. The badge shows the label in the tone. The column sorts by rank, the map's order unless an entry's `rank` says otherwise, and a value the map does not know sorts after the known ones (before them when the sort is descending) in a neutral badge with its value as the words. The search finds a status by its label as well as by its stored value, the filter lists the labels in that order, and export writes the labels. A `tone` function still wins for a row that needs its own, and `sortBy` still wins over the rank. Use `tone` alone for a column whose statuses appear nowhere else.

```tsx
const taskStatuses = {
  overdue: { label: "Overdue", tone: "danger" },
  in_review: { label: "In review", tone: "information" },
  done: { label: "Done", tone: "success" },
} satisfies StatusMap;

c.status("state", { header: "Status", statuses: taskStatuses });
```

_Example: story `Stories.StatusMapStory`._

## Style

| Element         | Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame           | none: no border, no radius; the header's hairline and the one under the last row bound the register · `fill`: the rest of the window from the register's top edge, never under a header, six rows and the pagination |
| Toolbar slot    | above the header, flush with the table's edge, `space.200` under, no rule                                                                                                                                            |
| Header, rows    | As Table: `dimension.row.header`, `dimension.row`, the hairline, the hovered and selected surfaces                                                                                                                   |
| Leading columns | the checkbox, the handle and the detail chevron 32px, the disclosure 28px, each centred; the tree's indent is `space.200` per level on the row's first value                                                         |
| Preview eye     | over the end of the first value cell, `opacity` 0 until the row is hovered or focused (always shown where nothing can hover), on the row's own surface; the value beside it keeps `space.300` clear while it shows   |
| Pinned column   | `elevation.surface.current` · `color.border.bold` at the edge while the frame is scrolled                                                                                                                            |
| Skeleton rows   | one `Skeleton` line per row, the row's height                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Empty           | no records: the Empty alone, on its dashed frame · filtered: under the header, `space.200` around, no frame                                                                                                          |
| Error           | under the header, `space.150` around                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Selection bar   | `color.border.brand` · `color.background.selected` · `color.text.brand` · `radius.medium` · `space.150` × `space.075`                                                                                                |
| Footer          | `color.border` above · a static row                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Pagination      | under the closing hairline, `space.100` above, flush with the table's edge · the range, then Rows per page as a small Select, then the pager at the end                                                              |
| Resize guide    | `color.background.brand.bold`, 2px, on hover and while dragging                                                                                                                                                      |

## Accessibility

- **The role follows the mode.** A DataTable is a `table`: Tab moves through the interactive elements in reading order and that is enough. A `tree` is a `treegrid`: Tab enters the first visible row, or the last focused row while it remains visible; arrow keys move, open and close, and Home and End jump. Exactly one visible tree row is a tab stop. An editable table is a `grid`: Enter accepts a valid text commit and moves down the column; validation failures and IME composition confirmations keep focus in the editor. Tab keeps its meaning and moves across. The plain table stays a table; the treegrid and grid roles are the ARIA patterns for what those modes add.
- **Named.** `label` names the table and, through it, its pagination ("Findings pagination"). The header checkbox is "Select all rows on this page". With `rowLabel` each row's controls carry its name ("Select REQ-001", "Row actions for REQ-001", "Reorder REQ-001", "Show details for REQ-001"); without it the checkbox is "Select row" and the id, the kebab "Row actions", the handle "Reorder row" and the id. The eye is "Preview row"; the tree's chevron names its row; the detail row's chevron carries `aria-controls`; a column's grip is "Reorder" and its header ("Reorder Status column"), and is hidden from assistive technology while the column's menu moves it; the resize handle is a vertical `separator` named "Resize column"; the Rows per page select is named so. A drag says a row by its label and a column by its header, never by a raw id.
- **Sorting** reports `aria-sort`; the chevron shows on hover and on focus. Only a drawn header reports it: while the sorted column is folded into More fields no header claims the sort, and `DataTable.Sort`'s name says it ("Sort: Due, Newest first"), in words, not only by its arrow. **Filtering** reads on the chips (pressed or expanded, the value in the text) and in the presets' counts. **Selection** is the checkbox, never the row's click; the SelectionBar is a region named "Selection" and Escape clears it.
- **Loading never removes the header** or changes the height of what is already there, so nothing jumps under a screen reader's cursor. Error and the filtered empty sit under the header. With no records at all there is no table: the region is the Empty and its action, so a screen reader meets the message first and the way forward second, not eight empty column headers.
- **A thousand rows may be chosen one at a time**: a row is memoized on what it shows, so one checkbox redraws one row and a preview step the two rows it changes. The leading columns, the fitted layout and the handlers the rows get are stable, and `onRowClick` is read through a ref, so an inline handler costs nothing; new `data` or new column definitions redraw every row, so keep both stable (module level or `useMemo`). A cell, a `detail` and a tree's `hint` draw from their row; state they read from outside it reaches the rows through new column definitions, so put it in the `useMemo`'s dependencies. A responsive table redraws when its frame folds or returns a column or a pin gives way, never on the pixels between: the identity column takes the slack through CSS, so a panel that opens or a splitter that drags costs the rows no render. The row actions menu and the id's glance are one menu and one card per table, which each row's trigger opens with its row, so a closed menu costs a row nothing. The Render budget story counts the rows each change redraws.
- **The name keeps its focus ring.** A link in a cell that is cut cuts itself at the cell's width, ends in its own ellipsis and draws its ring inside its box, so the clip that cuts the value never cuts the ring; the id's glance trigger does the same.
- **Reordering and resizing take the keyboard from the column's menu.** A column's grip and its resize handle are for the pointer and are no tab stops, so a header costs the keyboard two stops, its sort and its menu. A table with `columnMenu: false` has no menu to do this, so there the grip takes Space and the arrow keys and the handle takes the arrow keys (see Columns without a menu). A grip from `useColumnDrag` in a header drawn by hand keeps its keys too; pass `pointerOnly` when that header's menu moves the column. The menu moves the column one place with Move left or Move right, one press each, which is also the way on a touch screen, and a status says where it went; a resizable column's menu sets its width by single presses (Wider, Narrower, Reset width), with the width said in the same status. A row's handle takes Space and the arrow keys, and its menu's Move up and Move down move it one place.

## Props

`DataTable` is generic over the row type, so its table is written here rather than generated.

| Prop         | Type                                                                     | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `table`      | `DataTableInstance<T>`                                                   | From `useDataTable`. Required.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `toolbar`    | `ReactNode`                                                              | Sits above the header, flush with the table's edge.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `state`      | `"ready"`, `"loading"`, `"empty"`, `"error"`                             | Drawn under the header. Default `ready`; `ready` with no rows is empty.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `empty`      | `{ title, description?, action?, secondary?, illustration?, filtered? }` | What the empty state says. `illustration` is `records`, `search`, `done` or `false`. `filtered` is the narrowed state's `{ title?, description?, action?, illustration? }`; its defaults are localized and its default action clears the filters. |
| `narrowed`   | `boolean`                                                                | The caller narrowed `data` outside the table: an empty result keeps the toolbar and header and shows the filtered empty. See Narrowed outside the table.                                                                                          |
| `noun`       | `{ one, other }`                                                         | What a row is, for the result status ("8 of 24 findings"). "row" and "rows" unsaid.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `error`      | `ReactNode`                                                              | What the error state shows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `onRowClick` | `(row: T) => void`                                                       | Opens the record. Never selects.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `maxHeight`  | `number`                                                                 | Pixels; the frame scrolls inside itself past it.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `fill`       | `boolean`                                                                | The register is the page's one block: it fills the window, the frame scrolls inside, the pagination stays at the bottom. Wins over `maxHeight`.                                                                                                   |
| `responsive` | `boolean`                                                                | Fit the container: lower-priority fields move into each row's More fields instead of scrolling sideways. See Responsive containers.                                                                                                               |
| `className`  | `string`                                                                 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

The hook's options are the Modifiers above; `DataTableOptions<T>` is exported with each one described.

_Example: story `Stories.DataTableMatrix`._

## Responsive containers

Set `<DataTable responsive table={table} />` when the table must fit its container. Set `priority: 0` and a readable minimum width on the primary identity; the renderer retains it and row actions, then fits other columns by priority. Lower-priority fields appear in each row's localized More fields disclosure with their labels and original cell renderers. A reader-hidden column stays hidden. Resizing does not change the table's column-visibility state, view persistence, selection, sort, filters or export. The observer follows the container, including a neighbouring panel, rather than a viewport breakpoint.

Responsive mode uses fixed column geometry and keeps virtualization active. Expanded fields contribute their measured height to the same virtual record; scrolling away and back preserves its disclosure state. Column or container changes invalidate cached heights, including records outside the rendered window. Paging remains an independent choice. `c.id` honours an explicit `minWidth` when no width is supplied.

Use responsive mode for record lists whose drafts belong to a form outside the cells. A field that moves between its cell and the More fields disclosure remounts its renderer, so a local inline editor's uncommitted draft is not retained through that move. Generic editable or wide comparison tables keep the default horizontal scrolling until their draft state is owned outside those renderers.

_Example: story `Stories.ResponsiveContainers`._

_Example: story `Stories.ResponsiveGroupedHeaders`._

_Example: story `Stories.ResponsiveVirtualRows`._

In a responsive table Move left and Move right step only among the columns the row draws, so every move shows, and the last one drawn cannot move past a folded one. Columns without a `priority` rank by their place, so a move can change which of them fit: when the moved column folds into More fields, focus stays in the header row, on the column it passed, and the status says where it went.

_Example: story `Stories.MovingColumnsNarrow`._

On a phone nothing waits for a hover: the eye and the row-actions kebab are always shown, the value beside the eye ends in an ellipsis before it, and every control smaller than 24px takes a 24px hit area wherever a pointer is coarse. A header's column menu and grip sit beside the heading, and the column is drawn that much wider there (24px for one, 46px for both), so the heading keeps the room it has at rest on a desktop; beside a menu that sorts, the heading drops its up-down hint. A table that is not `responsive` redraws on a resize of its frame only when a pin gives way or returns.

_Example: story `Stories.RowControlsPhone`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Editable (src/stories/patterns/Editable.mdx) -->

# Editable

A value edited where it sits. The reader clicks it, changes it, and it saves: no form, no Save button, no dialog. It commits at once and shows the save beside the value; a refused save puts the old value back with the reason under it. **Editable.Text** edits text, with `multiline` for full paragraphs; **Editable.Select** is one of a fixed set, drawn as the record draws it.

It is for one value on a record that already exists: the owner in the rail, the next action in a table's cell, the status as a Badge. A record that does not exist yet is a [form](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs); several values that change together are a form in a Dialog; a paragraph uses `Editable.Text multiline` to edit in a Textarea in the same cell.

_Example: story `Stories.Rail`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row     | A button the full width of its cell, 24px tall. The value sits flush on the text column; under the pointer the row tints, the tint reaching `space.050` past the value.         |
| Value   | The committed value in `font.body`, one line that truncates. Empty, the `placeholder` in `color.text.subtlest`, or the muted dash.                                              |
| Mark    | At the end of the row: a Spinner while saving, a check in `color.icon.success` for a moment after, a warning in `color.icon.danger` after a refusal. A chevron on a Select.     |
| Field   | Text, editing: an input of `dimension.control.xsmall` in the value's place, its box reaching `space.050` past the column so the text stays on it.                               |
| Menu    | Select, editing: the options under the row, the current one marked, and nothing else; a short set uses Select; a long set uses Combobox with its search input inside the popup. |
| Message | Under the row in `font.body.xsmall` and `color.text.danger`: what `validate` refused, or why the save failed.                                                                   |

## Variants

Two, by what the value is. **Text** for a value the reader writes: a name, an acronym, a next action, a date typed as text. **Select** for one of a fixed set: a status, a method, an owner from a roster, drawn by `render` as the record draws it, a Badge or a Person, so the rail and the table agree.

Where it lives: in a [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs) row of the rail, in a [Fact](?path=/docs/components-fact--docs), in a [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) cell under the column's heading. A [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) column with `editable` draws these itself.

_Example: story `Stories.InTable`._

Use `multiline` for criteria and other paragraphs: the entire value wraps at rest, and the textarea grows with its content. Enter adds a newline, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter or leaving the cell saves, and Escape cancels and returns focus. Validation and save recovery are the same as single-line text.

_Example: story `Stories.Multiline`._

## Sizes

One: 24px, `dimension.control.xsmall`, so the row is a line of body text with `space.025` above and below, the height of the KeyValue row and the table cell it sits in. The width is the cell's.

Each instance accepts one save at a time. While saving, the resting control cannot reopen for another edit. A rejected save restores its previous value only while this request still owns the current value; an external update is preserved. Completion after unmount is ignored. The caller remains responsible for reconciling server updates to the record.

## States

| State   | Look                                                                                                                                         |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rest    | The value, flush. Nothing says it edits until the pointer arrives; the rail's rows all edit, so nothing needs to.                            |
| Hover   | The row tints `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered`; pressed, `.pressed`.                                                                |
| Focus   | The kit's focus outline on the row.                                                                                                          |
| Editing | Text: the field in the value's place, focused, the existing value ready to edit. Select: the listbox or searchable popup open under the row. |
| Invalid | Editing, the field's border `color.border.danger` and the message under it, as the reader types. The commit is refused while it shows.       |
| Saving  | The new value shows at once and a Spinner sits at the end of the row.                                                                        |
| Saved   | A check for `motion.duration.slower` twice, then nothing.                                                                                    |
| Failed  | The old value is back, the warning mark at the end, the reason under the row. It stays until the next edit.                                  |
| Empty   | The placeholder in `color.text.subtlest`, or the muted dash. Never a grey instruction.                                                       |

There is no disabled state. A value the reader cannot change is plain text in the same row, which lines up with the editable ones.

_Example: story `Stories.EditableMatrix`._

## Modifiers

- **`validate`**: a function of the draft that returns a message or null. It runs as the reader types and again at the commit, so a rule is seen before Enter is refused.
- **`save`**: a promise. Resolved, the check; rejected, the rollback and the error's message. `onChange` is called at once with the new value, and again with the old one when the save fails, so the caller's state is always what the reader sees.
- **`placeholder`** on Text: what goes here, as a noun.
- **`options`** and **`render`** on Select: the set, and how a value is drawn.
- **`label`**: the field's name for a screen reader. The KeyValue or the column shows the visible one.

_Example: story `Stories.Validation`._

_Example: story `Stories.Failing`._

## Content

- **The label is the field's name as the rail shows it:** "Owner", "Next action". The same word as the KeyValue's label or the column's heading.
- **A placeholder says what goes here, as a noun:** "Unassigned", "Add next action". Not "Click to edit", not "Enter a value".
- **A validation message says the rule, in one sentence:** "Two to twelve letters, digits or hyphens." Not "Invalid".
- **A save failure says why, from the server's message when it has one,** and "Could not save" when it does not.
- **A Select's options are the record's words,** drawn as the record draws them.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                                                       |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row     | `dimension.control.xsmall` 24px · `space.025` block · `space.075` gap · `radius.small` · tint reaching `space.050` past the column          |
| Value   | `font.body` · `color.text` · `color.text.subtlest` for the placeholder                                                                      |
| Tint    | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered`, `.pressed` · `motion.duration.fast` on `motion.easing.standard`                                  |
| Field   | `dimension.control.xsmall` · `color.background.input` · `color.border.input`, `color.border.focused` focused, `color.border.danger` invalid |
| Mark    | `dimension.icon.small` 14px · `color.icon.success` · `color.icon.danger` · the Spinner                                                      |
| Message | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.danger`                                                                                                    |
| Focus   | The kit's focus outline, `color.border.focused`                                                                                             |

## Accessibility

- **Touch:** the value keeps its 22px line. Where any pointer is coarse the trigger's `::after` is a hit area at least 24px tall across the value, centred on it (the shared `touch-target-block-after` band); `::before` holds the hover tint. A finger reaches the whole area in a table cell (In table) and in a rail, since KeyValue truncates its value across only (Rail).
- **The row is named by the label and the value:** "Owner: Dana Whitfield". The label is read before the value, so a screen reader hears what the field is where a sighted reader reads the KeyValue's label beside it.
- **The field is named by the label** (`aria-label`) and, invalid, is `aria-invalid` and described by the message.
- **Keyboard:** Tab reaches the row; Enter or Space opens the field with the existing value; Enter commits and Escape puts the old value back, and either returns focus to the row. Leaving the field by Tab or a click commits and focus goes where the reader sent it. Select and searchable Combobox triggers expose the native combobox role. Enter, Space or Down opens the options; arrows move between them and Enter chooses. Escape closes without changing the value. While saving, the trigger stays focusable and read-only, with `aria-disabled` announcing that another edit must wait.
- **In a DataTable:** Enter moves to the next row only after accepting a valid text commit. Invalid input keeps focus, and an IME composition confirmation neither saves nor changes rows.
- **A landed save is announced:** "Saved", or "Not saved", from a status region under the row; the Spinner says "Saving". The region is visually hidden inside the Editable's own positioned wrapper, so in a table that scrolls sideways it stays in the table's frame and never widens the page (In table).
- **The stories** exercise validation, keyboard selection, search, save rejection, rollback, pending guards and focus restoration in both themes.

## Props

Editable keeps its value, validation and save contract while composing the shared Input, Select and Combobox. No application API migration is required. The searchable popup follows [shadcn](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/combobox#popup) and [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox#input-inside-popup).

### Editable.Text

| Prop          | Type                                  | What it is                                                                       |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`       | `string`, required                    | The field's name for a screen reader: "Owner".                                   |
| `value`       | `string`, required                    | The committed value, shown at rest.                                              |
| `onChange`    | `(next: string) => void`, required    | Called at once with the new value, and with the old one again if the save fails. |
| `save`        | `(next: string) => Promise`, required | Saves it. Rejected, the value rolls back and the error's message shows.          |
| `validate`    | `(next: string) => string \| null`    | A message blocks the commit; null lets it through.                               |
| `placeholder` | `string`                              | What goes here, as a noun, shown while empty.                                    |

### Editable.Select

| Prop         | Type                               | What it is                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`      | `string`, required                 | The field's name, for the screen reader; the options have no heading.                                                                                                   |
| `value`      | `T`, required                      | The current option.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `options`    | `readonly T[]`, required           | The set, in the order it shows.                                                                                                                                         |
| `onChange`   | `(next: T) => void`, required      | As Text.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `save`       | `(next: T) => Promise`, required   | As Text.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `validate`   | `(next: string) => string \| null` | As Text: a status the record is not ready for, with the reason.                                                                                                         |
| `render`     | `(value: T) => ReactNode`          | Draws a value: a Badge, a Person. Unsaid, the value as text. The same rendering appears in short and searchable lists; option names and search use the original string. |
| `searchable` | `boolean`                          | A search field over the rendered options. On by itself past eight options.                                                                                              |
